title: ReferItGame: Referring to Objects in Photographs of Natural Scenes
authors: Sahar Kazemzadeh, Vicente Ordonez, Mark Matten, et al.
architecture: Attribute-based REG model solved as binary integer linear programming over visual attribute predictors and learned priors
mechanism: Two-player crowd game: one player writes an expression for a segmented region, the other must click it; successful clicks validate the expression
objective: Game-collected expressions; REG model selects attributes and values with unary and pairwise potentials learned from dataset statistics
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Short game-style expressions on IAPR TC-12 photos; regions include stuff (sky, road); REG evaluated only by attribute precision/recall (our reading)

title: Generation and Comprehension of Unambiguous Object Descriptions
authors: Junhua Mao, Jonathan Huang, Alexander Toshev, et al.
architecture: CNN region features + LSTM language model (speaker); comprehension scores candidate regions by expression likelihood
mechanism: Comprehension = argmax over region proposals of p(expression | region, image); discriminative (MMI) training contrasts the target with other regions
objective: Max-likelihood plus maximum-mutual-information (softmax/margin) loss against distractor regions; semi-supervised variant generates expressions for unlabelled boxes and keeps only those the comprehension model decodes back to the same object
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Proposal-and-rank: cannot recover objects missed by proposals; single target assumed (our reading)

title: Modeling Context in Referring Expressions
authors: Licheng Yu, Patrick Poirson, Shan Yang, et al.
architecture: CNN + LSTM speaker/listener with visual-comparison features to same-category objects
mechanism: Visual comparison: difference features between the target and other same-category objects (appearance and location) are added to the region representation; joint generation for all objects of a category
objective: Max-likelihood with MMI-style discriminative training
robustness_tests: testA/testB splits separate people from other objects; RefCOCO+ bans location words
limitations: Proposal-and-rank, single-target; context limited to same-category objects (our reading)

title: Flickr30k Entities: Collecting Region-to-Phrase Correspondences for Richer Image-to-Sentence Models
authors: Bryan A. Plummer, Liwei Wang, Chris M. Cervantes, et al.
architecture: Baseline: CCA image-text embedding over region proposals + detector, colour and size cues
mechanism: Rank region proposals by phrase-region embedding similarity, combined with object-detector scores and size prior
objective: Normalised CCA embedding fitted on annotated phrase-box pairs
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: A phrase may map to several boxes but standard protocol scores a merged box or any-box; gains in localisation did not transfer to retrieval (authors)

title: Segmentation from Natural Language Expressions
authors: Ronghang Hu, Marcus Rohrbach, Trevor Darrell
architecture: LSTM expression encoder + FCN (VGG-16) spatial feature map with coordinate features; upsampling deconvolution
mechanism: Tile the sentence vector over the spatial feature map and fuse by concatenation + 1x1 convolutions to output a per-pixel response map
objective: Per-pixel binary (logistic) loss on low- and high-resolution masks
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Concatenation fusion of a single sentence vector; single-target masks; evaluated mainly on ReferIt (our reading)

title: MAttNet: Modular Attention Network for Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Licheng Yu, Zhe Lin, Xiaohui Shen, et al.
task: REC (+ RES via Mask R-CNN masks)
architecture: Mask R-CNN (ResNet-101) proposals and features + Bi-LSTM language encoder; subject, location and relationship modules
foundation_models: Mask R-CNN / Faster R-CNN ResNet-101 trained on COCO (excluding RefCOCO val/test images)
mechanism: Language attention decomposes the expression into subject, location and relationship phrases and weights three visual modules; module scores are combined to rank candidate objects
objective: Ranking (hinge) loss against negative objects and negative expressions, plus attribute prediction loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Proposal-and-rank: cannot ground objects the detector misses; always returns exactly one object (our reading)

title: TransVG: End-to-End Visual Grounding with Transformers
authors: Jiajun Deng, Zhengyuan Yang, Tianlang Chen, et al.
architecture: ResNet + DETR transformer encoder (visual branch), BERT (linguistic branch), 6-layer visual-linguistic transformer fusion with a learnable [REG] token
mechanism: Concatenate visual tokens, text tokens and a [REG] token; joint self-attention fusion; [REG] output regresses the box directly (no proposals/anchors)
objective: Smooth L1 + GIoU box regression
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Regresses exactly one box, so it cannot express no-target or multi-target (our reading)

title: MDETR - Modulated Detection for End-to-End Multi-Modal Understanding
authors: Aishwarya Kamath, Mannat Singh, Yann LeCun, et al.
task: phrase grounding / REC / RES / text-conditioned detection
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: CNN backbone (ResNet-101 / EfficientNet) + RoBERTa text encoder, joint transformer encoder over concatenated image and text features, DETR decoder
mechanism: Early fusion of image and text in one transformer encoder; DETR object queries predict boxes plus a distribution over text-token spans
objective: Soft token prediction (box-to-span alignment) + contrastive alignment between object queries and tokens + DETR box losses; pre-training on 1.3M text-image pairs with explicit phrase-box alignment
robustness_tests: Table 2 caption flags a test-set leak in BUTD-detector-based baselines; MDETR pre-training excludes downstream val/test images
limitations: No explicit no-target behaviour reported; REC protocol takes the top-scoring box (our reading)

title: LAVT: Language-Aware Vision Transformer for Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Zhao Yang, Jiaqi Wang, Yansong Tang, et al.
architecture: Swin-B hierarchical vision encoder with a pixel-word attention module (PWAM) and language gate at every stage; BERT-base text encoder; light-weight mask predictor
mechanism: Early fusion: language features are injected into intermediate stages of the vision Transformer (pixel-word attention) with a gated language pathway, so the encoder itself produces language-aware features
objective: Pixel-wise mask loss on the referred object
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single referent assumed; no handling of empty or multi-object expressions (our reading)

title: CRIS: CLIP-Driven Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Zhaoqing Wang, Yu Lu, Qiang Li, et al.
architecture: CLIP image encoder (ResNet-50/101) and CLIP text encoder; transformer vision-language decoder; projector producing pixel embeddings
mechanism: Vision-language decoder propagates fine-grained text semantics to pixel features; text-to-pixel contrastive alignment makes the sentence embedding similar to referred pixels and dissimilar to others
objective: Text-to-pixel contrastive loss (per-pixel binary)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single referent; CLIP's image-level pre-training is only adapted, not re-trained for dense alignment (our reading)

title: PolyFormer: Referring Image Segmentation as Sequential Polygon Generation
authors: Jiang Liu, Hui Ding, Zhaowei Cai, et al.
architecture: Swin-B/L image encoder + BERT-base text encoder, multimodal transformer encoder, regression-based transformer decoder emitting box corners and polygon vertices
mechanism: Grounding as sequence-to-sequence generation: the decoder autoregressively predicts floating-point box and polygon vertex coordinates (bilinear interpolation over a 2D coordinate codebook, no quantisation)
objective: L1 coordinate regression + token-type classification; REC pre-training on VG + RefCOCO/+/g + Flickr30k, then multi-task RIS/REC fine-tuning
robustness_tests: Zero-shot transfer from images to referring video segmentation (Ref-DAVIS17)
limitations: Single polygon sequence per expression; single target; fine-tuning uses the combined RefCOCO/+/g training set (our reading)

title: GRES: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation
authors: Chang Liu, Henghui Ding, Xudong Jiang
architecture: ReLA: Swin-B visual encoder + BERT; P x P region-based queries with Region-Image Cross Attention (RIA) and Region-Language Cross Attention (RLA); pixel decoder for mask features
mechanism: Image split into adaptive sub-instance regions; region queries attend to image (RIA) and to words and each other (RLA); region masks weighted by a region probability minimap; global no-target classifier empties the mask
objective: Cross-entropy on the output mask, on the minimap of region probabilities and on the no-target label
robustness_tests: No-target evaluation (N-acc for no-target samples, T-acc for target samples); classic RES baselines re-trained on gRefCOCO for comparison
limitations: Existence decision is a single global binary label; N-acc only ~56-59% leaves many false positives on no-target expressions (from Table 6)

title: GREC: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Shuting He, Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, et al.
architecture: Benchmark: existing REC models (MCN, VLT, MDETR, UNINEXT) adapted to output multiple boxes selected by a confidence threshold
mechanism: Box sets selected by score threshold (0.7) for multi- and no-target expressions
objective: Baselines re-trained on gRefCOCO boxes
robustness_tests: No-target and multi-target evaluation at box level
limitations: Technical report without a proposed method; thresholded baselines only (our reading)

title: GREx: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation, Comprehension, and Generation
authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He, et al.
architecture: ReLA (region-based queries with RIA/RLA) with mask, box-regression and target-count heads; Swin-B or ResNet-50 + BERT
mechanism: Region-level relationship modelling (region-image and region-language attention); explicit no-target prediction; boxes output via top-k/threshold over region predictions
objective: Mask, minimap and no-target cross-entropy plus box regression and target-number prediction; joint GRES/GREC training
robustness_tests: No-target and multi-target evaluation across segmentation, comprehension and generation; GREG evaluated for classic REG and MLLMs
limitations: Same single global existence decision as GRES; N-acc remains below 60% (from Tables 10 and 14)

title: Beyond One-to-One: Rethinking the Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Yutao Hu, Qixiong Wang, Wenqi Shao, et al.
architecture: DMMI: ResNet-101 or Swin-B visual encoder + BERT; text-to-image decoder for segmentation and image-to-text decoder for phrase reconstruction
mechanism: Dual multi-modal interaction: text queries visual features to localise; visual features must reconstruct the erased entity phrase, forcing them to carry target semantics
objective: Mask loss + entity-phrase reconstruction loss (training-time)
robustness_tests: Ref-ZOM evaluation including one-to-zero (no referent) expressions; Acc reported for empty-target samples
limitations: Reconstruction acts only at training time; no explicit existence head reported (our reading)

title: Described Object Detection: Liberating Object Detection with Flexible Expressions
authors: Chi Xie, Zhao Zhang, Yixuan Wu, et al.
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; novel categories/compositions
architecture: Benchmark D3 + OFA-DOD baseline (OFA REC model with multi-target outputs, rebuilt training data and a binary presence classification step)
mechanism: Every description annotated on every image of its scenario; detectors must return all matching boxes or none; OFA-DOD adds a second step that rejects false positives
objective: Evaluation-only dataset; baseline trained on reconstructed REC/OVD data with binary classification
robustness_tests: Breakdown by number of instances (no-instance FPPC, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4+), description length, and absence vs presence descriptions; score-threshold analysis of false positives
limitations: Evaluation-only; OFA-DOD still has 35.6% FPPC on no-instance images (Table 3) and inter-scenario mAP is very low

title: OneRef: Unified One-tower Expression Grounding and Segmentation with Mask Referring Modeling
authors: Linhui Xiao, Xiaoshan Yang, Fang Peng, et al.
architecture: Single modality-shared BEiT-3 transformer (B or L) with lightweight box/mask heads; no separate fusion encoder or decoder
mechanism: One-tower joint encoding of image patches and text tokens; referring-aware masked modelling teaches the shared encoder where the referent is
objective: Mask Referring Modeling (referring-aware masked image and language modelling with dynamic masking of the referred region) + box/mask regression
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single-target outputs only; no rejection of absent referents (our reading)

title: SegGPT: Towards Segmenting Everything In Context
authors: Xinlong Wang, Xiaosong Zhang, Yue Cao, et al.
architecture: Painter-style generalist: ViT-L encoder (307M) over stitched example image/mask pairs and query image, predicting the query's coloured mask
mechanism: In-context colouring: example image-mask pairs define the target via a random colour mapping; the model paints the query mask in the same colour; supports context ensembling and learnable in-context tuning
objective: Masked image modelling-style regression of the coloured mask with random colour mapping across mixed segmentation datasets
robustness_tests: Out-of-domain evaluation (FSS-1000 not used in training; video benchmarks without video training)
limitations: Target defined only by visual exemplars; no language query and no explicit rejection of absent targets (our reading)

title: Personalize Segment Anything Model with One Shot
authors: Renrui Zhang, Zhengkai Jiang, Ziyu Guo, et al.
architecture: Frozen SAM; reference-mask feature as target embedding; PerSAM-F adds 2 learnable weights over SAM's multi-scale masks
mechanism: Location prior from reference-target feature similarity gives positive/negative point prompts; target-guided attention and target-semantic prompting steer SAM's decoder; cascaded post-refinement re-prompts SAM with its own mask
objective: Training-free (PerSAM); PerSAM-F tunes 2 scale weights on the one-shot reference in ~10 s
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Mask-scale ambiguity between part and whole (authors; motivates PerSAM-F); single concept per reference (our reading)

title: Matcher: Segment Anything with One Shot Using All-Purpose Feature Matching
authors: Yang Liu, Muzhi Zhu, Hengtao Li, et al.
architecture: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 image encoder for dense matching + SAM as mask generator
mechanism: Bidirectional (forward-reverse) patch matching between reference and target; robust prompt sampler turns matched points into SAM prompts; instance-level matching scores proposals against the reference mask and merges the best
objective: Training-free
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Relies on DINOv2 matching quality; fragmented false positives from matching outliers are suppressed heuristically (authors' motivation)

title: T-Rex2: Towards Generic Object Detection via Text-Visual Prompt Synergy
authors: Qing Jiang, Feng Li, Zhaoyang Zeng, et al.
task: open-set detection with text and visual prompts (exemplar grounding)
A_query: phrase/class name; visual exemplar; visual prompt; composite
architecture: Deformable-DETR detector with Swin backbone; CLIP text encoder for text prompts and a deformable-attention visual-prompt encoder for box/point exemplars
mechanism: Late fusion: prompt embeddings classify DETR queries; text and visual prompt embeddings of the same category are aligned by contrastive learning so either or both can be used
objective: DETR detection losses + text-visual prompt contrastive alignment; trained on Objects365, OpenImages, GoldG and data-engine pseudo-labels
robustness_tests: Compares text vs visual prompts on rare/long-tail categories (LVIS rare)
limitations: Category-level prompts, not referring expressions; no explicit absence handling (our reading)

title: Visual In-Context Prompting
authors: Feng Li, Qing Jiang, Hao Zhang, et al.
architecture: DINOv: MaskDINO encoder-decoder (Swin-T/L) with a versatile visual prompt encoder (points, boxes, strokes)
mechanism: Reference-image segments (any number) are encoded as visual prompts that match DETR-style queries in the target image, for referring (most relevant object) or generic (all instances) segmentation
objective: Joint training on COCO and SA-1B with mask/box losses and prompt-query matching
robustness_tests: Zero-shot video object segmentation without video training
limitations: Visual prompts only; no language referring or absence rejection reported (our reading)

title: Multi-task Collaborative Network for Joint Referring Expression Comprehension and Segmentation
authors: Gen Luo, Yiyi Zhou, Xiaoshuai Sun, et al.
architecture: One-stage Darknet-53 (COCO-pretrained, RefCOCO val/test images removed) + Bi-GRU; collaborative REC (anchor-based) and RES (mask) branches
mechanism: Joint REC/RES learning; Consistency Energy Maximization aligns the two branches' attention; Adaptive Soft Non-Located Suppression suppresses RES responses outside the REC-predicted region
objective: Box regression/confidence for REC + binary mask loss for RES + consistency-energy loss
robustness_tests: Inconsistency error (IE) between REC and RES predictions (prediction conflict) reported in ablations
limitations: Single referent; consistency is between two heads of the same model, not a check against the input (our reading)

title: Referring Transformer: A One-step Approach to Multi-task Visual Grounding
authors: Muchen Li, Leonid Sigal
architecture: ResNet-50/101 visual backbone + BERT; visual-lingual transformer encoder; decoder producing contextualised lingual queries; box regression and mask heads
mechanism: Two modalities fused in a visual-lingual encoder; decoder turns the expression into contextualised queries that are decoded to regress the box and produce the mask in one step
objective: Box regression + mask losses (multi-task); optional pre-training on Visual Genome region descriptions (~100k images, val/test images of downstream sets removed)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single referent per expression (our reading)

title: SeqTR: A Simple yet Universal Network for Visual Grounding
authors: Chaoyang Zhu, Yiyi Zhou, Yunhang Shen, et al.
architecture: Darknet-53 visual encoder + Bi-GRU language encoder, fusion, transformer decoder emitting discrete coordinate tokens
mechanism: Grounding as point prediction: boxes and masks (contour points) serialised as sequences of discrete coordinate tokens, predicted autoregressively without task-specific heads
objective: Single cross-entropy loss over coordinate tokens for all tasks
robustness_tests: Inconsistency error between REC and RES in multi-task ablation (Table 6)
limitations: Mask quality bounded by the number of sampled contour points (authors note 36 GT points give 95.63 mIoU upper bound); single target

title: TransVG++: End-to-End Visual Grounding With Language Conditioned Vision Transformer
authors: Jiajun Deng, Zhengyuan Yang, Daqing Liu, et al.
architecture: Pure-transformer: ViT (tiny/small/base) whose intermediate layers become Language Conditioned Vision Transformer layers; BERT text encoder; [REG] token box regression
mechanism: Removes external fusion modules; language conditions the ViT at intermediate layers so the uni-modal vision encoder performs vision-language fusion
objective: Smooth L1 + GIoU box regression
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single-box output; no rejection (our reading)

title: Language Adaptive Weight Generation for Multi-task Visual Grounding
authors: Wei Su, Peihan Miao, Huanzhang Dou, et al.
architecture: VG-LAW: ViT-B visual backbone whose weights are generated per expression (language adaptive weights) + BERT; language adaptive pooling; multi-task box/mask head
foundation_models: ViT-B (pre-trained on MS-COCO with val/test overlaps removed), BERT
mechanism: Active perception: expression-specific dynamic weights turn the visual backbone into an expression-conditioned feature extractor, removing a separate cross-modal fusion module
objective: Box regression + mask loss (multi-task head)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single referent; per-expression weight generation adds cost (our reading)

title: CLIP-VG: Self-paced Curriculum Adapting of CLIP for Visual Grounding
authors: Linhui Xiao, Xiaoshan Yang, Fang Peng, et al.
architecture: CLIP ViT-B/16 image and text encoders with multi-level visual features and a light transformer regression head (no separate cross-modal backbone)
mechanism: Transfers CLIP to grounding; single- and multi-source self-paced curriculum selects progressively more reliable pseudo-language labels using source-specific and cross-source reliability scores
objective: Box regression on pseudo-labels (unsupervised) or ground truth (fully supervised), with curriculum sample selection
robustness_tests: Reliability analysis of pseudo-label sources (proportion of unreliable labels per source, Table VIII)
limitations: Unsupervised setting still far below supervised; pseudo-label reliability estimated from the model itself (our reading)

title: SimVG: A Simple Framework for Visual Grounding with Decoupled Multi-modal Fusion
authors: Ming Dai, Lingfeng Yang, Yihao Xu, et al.
architecture: BEiT-3 multimodal encoder (ViT-B/32 or ViT-L/32) with extra object tokens; token branch (decoder) and lightweight MLP branch trained synchronously
mechanism: Decouples multimodal fusion from the downstream head by reusing a pre-trained multimodal encoder; dynamic weight-balance distillation transfers the decoder branch to a single MLP branch
objective: Box losses for both branches + dynamic weight-balance distillation
robustness_tests: GREC evaluation with no-target and multi-target expressions
limitations: No-target handled only by a fixed score threshold; N-acc ~55% (our reading of Table 2)

title: Vision-Language Transformer and Query Generation for Referring Segmentation
authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Suchen Wang, et al.
architecture: Darknet CNN encoder (416x416 input) + Bi-GRU; transformer encoder-decoder where language-generated queries attend to the image; Query Generation and Query Balance modules
mechanism: Referring segmentation as direct attention: multiple query sets generated from the expression (different word emphases) query the image; a balance module weights their outputs for the mask
objective: Mask segmentation loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single referent; queries model diverse readings of the expression but not their absence (our reading)

title: Locate then Segment: A Strong Pipeline for Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Ya Jing, Tao Kong, Wei Wang, et al.
architecture: Darknet-53 (COCO-pretrained, val/test images removed) + language encoder; cross-modal fusion, localisation module with position prior, light-weight segmentation network
mechanism: Locate-Then-Segment: fused visual-textual features first produce an explicit localisation (position prior) of the referent, then a light segmentation network refines the mask
objective: Localisation supervision + mask segmentation loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Explicit single-location prior assumes one referent (our reading)

title: ReSTR: Convolution-free Referring Image Segmentation Using Transformers
authors: Namyup Kim, Dongwon Kim, Cuiling Lan, et al.
architecture: ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-21K) vision encoder + transformer language encoder; self-attention multimodal fusion encoder; adaptive segmentation module
mechanism: Convolution-free: both modalities encoded by transformers and fused by joint self-attention; segmentation decoder adapts to the image-expression pair
objective: Mask loss
robustness_tests: Performance broken down by expression length (Table 2)
limitations: Single referent; accuracy drops for long expressions (Table 2)

title: Contrastive Grouping with Transformer for Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Jiajin Tang, Ge Zheng, Cheng Shi, et al.
architecture: Swin Transformer (ImageNet-22K, LAVT setting) + BERT; learnable object query tokens that alternately query language and group visual features; consecutive decoder
mechanism: Mask classification: object tokens group pixels into candidate objects; contrastive learning between tokens and the expression selects the referent token and its mask
objective: Mask loss + token-expression contrastive loss
robustness_tests: Generalisation setting: seen vs unseen object categories on RefCOCO/+/G-Ref (Table 2; e.g. RefCOCO val unseen mIoU 63.17 vs seen 75.52)
limitations: Selects exactly one token, so no-target and multi-target are not handled (our reading)

title: Mask Grounding for Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Yong Xien Chng, Henry Zheng, Yizeng Han, et al.
architecture: MagNet: Swin-B image encoder + BERT-base language encoder with a cross-modal alignment module
mechanism: Mask Grounding auxiliary task: masked textual tokens must be predicted from matching visual objects (with mask cues), forcing word-to-object grounding; plus cross-modal alignment loss
objective: Mask loss + Mask Grounding token-prediction cross-entropy + cross-modal alignment loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single referent (our reading)

title: Unveiling Parts Beyond Objects: Towards Finer-Granularity Referring Expression Segmentation
authors: Wenxuan Wang, Tongtian Yue, Yisi Zhang, et al.
architecture: UniRES with query-based grouping of high- and low-level features for unified object- and part-level grounding
mechanism: Query-based grouping decodes object and part masks from expressions in one model; pre-training on the model-assisted MRES-32M corpus
objective: Mask losses; pre-training on MRES-32M then fine-tuning on RefCOCO/+/g
robustness_tests: Part-only vs object-and-part evaluation on RefCOCOm
limitations: Part-level grounding remains weak (RefCOCOm val part-only mIoU 19.6, Table 3); MRES-32M labels are model-assisted (our reading)

title: DeRIS: Decoupling Perception and Cognition for Enhanced Referring Image Segmentation through Loopback Synergy
authors: Ming Dai, Wenxuan Cheng, Jiang-jiang Liu, et al.
architecture: Perception branch initialised from Mask2Former (Swin) producing instance masks; cognition branch on BEiT-3 (low resolution) for image-text referent classification; Loopback Synergy connecting them
foundation_models: Mask2Former (Swin-S/B), BEiT-3 (B/L); 7B variant uses Qwen2-OV-7B + SigLIP
mechanism: Decomposes RIS into perception (what objects/masks exist) and cognition (which match the text); loopback synergy iteratively exchanges information; auxiliary non-referent judgement
objective: Mask losses + referent classification + non-referent supervision; non-referent sample conversion augmentation
robustness_tests: Analysis of non-referent judgement and non-referent sample conversion rate; perception-vs-cognition bottleneck analysis on gRefCOCO
limitations: Authors find cognition (image-text understanding), not perception, is the main bottleneck; non-referent cases are long-tailed and need augmentation

title: Hierarchical Alignment-enhanced Adaptive Grounding Network for Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Yaxian Wang, Henghui Ding, Shuting He, et al.
architecture: ResNet-101 or Swin-B visual encoder + RoBERTa-base; Hierarchical Multi-modal Semantic Alignment (word-object, phrase-object, text-image) and Adaptive Grounding Counter
mechanism: Three-level cross-modal alignment; the Adaptive Grounding Counter predicts how many targets (including zero) to output
objective: L1 + GIoU box losses, focal + dice mask losses, counting loss with auxiliary contrastive loss pulling together features with the same count
robustness_tests: No-target and multi-target evaluation (GREC/GRES); success/failure case analysis
limitations: N-acc around 60% leaves many no-target false positives (our reading of Tables 1 and 5)

title: Zero-Shot Grounding of Objects from Natural Language Queries
authors: Arka Sadhu, Kan Chen, Ram Nevatia
architecture: ZSGNet: single-stage SSD-like detector-grounder with ResNet-50 features fused with the language embedding, dense anchor classification and regression
mechanism: Replaces the proposal stage (biased to seen categories) by dense anchors scored directly against the query, so unseen nouns are not filtered out by a detector
objective: Focal-loss anchor classification + box regression
robustness_tests: Four zero-shot cases by relation of the query noun to training categories; language-blind and image-blind ablations (Table 8); proposal-recall analysis
limitations: Single box per query; zero-shot cases still well below seen-category accuracy (our reading)

title: ReCLIP: A Strong Zero-Shot Baseline for Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Sanjay Subramanian, William Merrill, Trevor Darrell, et al.
architecture: CLIP (RN50x16 and ViT-B/32) scoring detected proposals (MAttNet detections) + rule-based spatial relation resolver over parsed expressions
mechanism: Isolated proposal scoring (crop + blur) with CLIP; a parser-driven spatial-relation resolver combines entity scores because CLIP alone cannot do spatial reasoning
objective: Training-free
robustness_tests: Controlled CLEVR test showing CLIP fails at spatial relations; RefGTA (synthetic video-game domain) transfer where zero-shot beats supervised models trained on RefCOCO
limitations: Hand-written relation rules; depends on proposal quality; CLIP lacks spatial reasoning (authors)

title: Pseudo-Q: Generating Pseudo Language Queries for Visual Grounding
authors: Haojun Jiang, Yuanze Lin, Dongchen Han, et al.
architecture: ResNet-50 + transformer visual encoder, BERT language encoder, multi-level cross-modality attention, box regression
foundation_models: Off-the-shelf object detector; ImageNet ResNet-50; BERT-base
mechanism: Detector finds objects in unlabelled images; templates combine nouns, attributes and spatial relations into pseudo queries; a query prompt module adapts them; model trained as if supervised
objective: Box regression on pseudo query-box pairs (no human annotation)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Template queries lack the diversity of human expressions; RefCOCO+ (no location words) is much harder (our reading of Table 1)

title: Zero-shot Referring Image Segmentation with Global-Local Context Features
authors: Seonghoon Yu, Paul Hongsuck Seo, Jeany Son
architecture: CLIP (ResNet-50 or ViT-B/32) + FreeSOLO unsupervised mask proposals + dependency parser for the target noun phrase
mechanism: Mask-guided visual encoder scores each mask proposal with global (whole-image) and local (masked) context; global-local text features combine the full sentence and the parsed head noun phrase; best-matching mask is returned
objective: Training-free
robustness_tests: PhraseCut unseen-category subset; upper-bound analysis with COCO ground-truth instance masks (Table 2)
limitations: Bounded by unsupervised mask-proposal quality (oIoU rises to 37-51 with GT masks, Table 2); always returns one mask

title: Referring Image Segmentation Using Text Supervision
authors: Fang Liu, Yuhao Liu, Yuqiu Kong, et al.
architecture: TRIS: CLIP-initialised ResNet-50 visual and text encoders with bilateral prompts; response-map calibration; segmentation network trained on pseudo-labels (Step-2)
mechanism: Localisation as classification of positive (own) vs negative (other images') expressions; calibrated response maps and positive response-map selection give pseudo-masks
objective: Text-classification loss + calibration loss (Step-1); pseudo-label segmentation training (Step-2)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Mask quality far below fully supervised RES (IoU ~31 vs ~73 for LAVT in the same table)

title: Curriculum Point Prompting for Weakly-Supervised Referring Image Segmentation
authors: Qiyuan Dai, Sibei Yang
architecture: PPT: lightweight point generator (20.7M trainable parameters) on CLIP text-image features that prompts SAM
mechanism: Point generator produces positive and negative point prompts for SAM, countering SAM's noisy and part-focused masks; multi-source curriculum from object-centric images to complex RIS
objective: Weak (image-text pair) supervision with curriculum learning
robustness_tests: Shows naive TRIS+SAM regresses (RefCOCO val 25.56 vs 31.17) because of SAM noise and part focus
limitations: Still far below fully supervised RES; relies on SAM and CLIP behaviour (our reading)

title: Generating Enhanced Negatives for Training Language-Based Object Detectors
authors: Shiyu Zhao, Long Zhao, Vijay Kumar B. G, et al.
task: language-based object detection / described object detection
architecture: GLIP-T and FIBER-B detectors fine-tuned with generated negatives
foundation_models: GLIP-T, FIBER-B, LLMs (negative text), text-to-image diffusion model (negative images)
mechanism: LLMs rewrite positive descriptions into hard negative descriptions and diffusion models synthesise matching negative images, so the discriminative detector learns to reject near-miss descriptions
objective: Detector contrastive/grounding loss with generated negative texts and images
robustness_tests: D3 breakdown by description length; OmniLabel negative-description subset
limitations: Gains shrink for long descriptions (XL length mAP 14.2 for FIBER-B, Table 2)

title: Grounded Language-Image Pre-training
authors: Liunian Harold Li, Pengchuan Zhang, Haotian Zhang, et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Swin image encoder + BERT-initialised text encoder with deep (early) cross-modal fusion; DyHead-style detector head
mechanism: detection recast as word-region alignment: region-token alignment scores replace class logits; deep fusion layers before the head
objective: alignment (grounding) loss + box regression on detection (O365) and human grounding data (GoldG), plus teacher-generated pseudo grounding boxes on web image-text pairs (self-training)
robustness_tests: none reported beyond zero-shot/few-shot transfer to LVIS and the 13 ODinW datasets (domain transfer)
limitations: box-only output; absence of a prompted concept must be decided by thresholding alignment scores, with no explicit no-target mechanism; pseudo-label noise from self-training on web data (our reading)

title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-training for Open-Set Object Detection
authors: Shilong Liu, Zhaoyang Zeng, Tianhe Ren, et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: DINO (DETR-style) detector with Swin-T/L image backbone and BERT text backbone; feature enhancer, language-guided query selection, cross-modality decoder
mechanism: tight three-phase image-text fusion (feature enhancer, language-guided query selection, cross-modality decoder); sub-sentence text representation
objective: contrastive region-token alignment + box (L1/GIoU) losses with grounded pre-training on detection, grounding and caption data
robustness_tests: none reported (zero-shot transfer to COCO/LVIS/ODinW only)
limitations: returns boxes for any prompt; no-target decisions rely on score thresholds (our reading); large gap between zero-shot (50.4) and RefCOCO-trained (73.98 without fine-tuning, 89.19 fine-tuned, Swin-T) REC accuracy shows dependence on in-domain referring data

title: OFA: Unifying Architectures, Tasks, and Modalities Through a Simple Sequence-to-Sequence Learning Framework
authors: Peng Wang, An Yang, Rui Men, et al.
task: REC within a generalist seq2seq model (also captioning, VQA, generation)
architecture: single Transformer encoder-decoder (ResNet stem + BART-style), 33M-930M parameters
mechanism: boxes emitted as discrete location tokens in a unified output vocabulary; instruction-based task specification, no task heads
objective: multitask seq2seq cross-entropy pre-training (incl. visual grounding on RefCOCO/+/g and VG) then per-task fine-tuning
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single-box output per query; no mechanism for absent or multiple referents (our reading); pre-training already contains RefCOCO-family grounding data

title: Generalized Decoding for Pixel, Image, and Language
authors: Xueyan Zou, Zi-Yi Dou, Jianwei Yang, et al.
task: RES within a generalist pixel-language decoder (also generic/open-vocabulary segmentation, retrieval, captioning)
architecture: image backbone (Focal/Swin/DaViT) + text encoder + X-Decoder taking generic latent queries and text queries, producing masks and semantic outputs
mechanism: generic non-semantic latent queries + text queries decoded jointly; masks and token-level semantics in one shared embedding space
objective: joint pre-training on COCO panoptic + referring segmentation (30k images) + 4M image-text pairs; optional task-specific fine-tuning
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: referring segmentation evaluated only on RefCOCOg; always outputs a mask for a referring query, no absence handling (our reading)

title: Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once
authors: Xueyan Zou, Jianwei Yang, Hao Zhang, et al.
task: promptable segmentation incl. referring segmentation (text, points, boxes, scribbles, masks, referring image)
architecture: X-Decoder-style image encoder + text encoder + decoder with joint visual-semantic prompt space and memory prompts for multi-round interaction
mechanism: visual prompts pooled from image features and text prompts share a joint space, so they can be composed; learnable memory prompts retain previous-round masks
objective: supervised segmentation losses on COCO panoptic, LVIS, and referring data with simulated interactive clicks
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: referring results only on RefCOCOg; composite prompts inflate cIoU and are not comparable with text-only RES; no absent-target handling (our reading)

title: Segment Anything
authors: Alexander Kirillov, Eric Mintun, Nikhila Ravi, et al.
task: promptable segmentation (points, boxes, masks; text-to-mask only as proof of concept)
architecture: MAE-pretrained ViT image encoder (ViT-B/L/H) + prompt encoder + lightweight two-way-transformer mask decoder
mechanism: prompt embeddings attend to image embeddings in a light decoder; multiple candidate masks for ambiguous prompts ranked by a predicted-IoU head (a confidence score; its calibration is not evaluated)
objective: focal + dice mask losses and IoU-prediction loss; model-in-the-loop data engine producing SA-1B (1.1B masks)
robustness_tests: zero-shot transfer across 23 diverse datasets; ambiguity handled by multi-mask output
limitations: no language grounding in the released model (text prompts only a proof of concept); predicted-IoU score is not a calibrated absence detector (our reading)

title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
authors: Nikhila Ravi, Valentin Gabeur, Yuan-Ting Hu, et al.
task: promptable segmentation in images and videos
architecture: hierarchical image encoder + streaming memory attention + memory bank + mask decoder with occlusion head
mechanism: per-frame decoding conditioned on a memory of past predictions and prompts (streaming memory); an extra head predicts whether the object of interest is present on the current frame (e.g. under occlusion)
objective: supervised mask losses on SA-1B and the SA-V video data engine output
robustness_tests: none for language grounding (video/interactive segmentation benchmarks only)
limitations: no text prompts; used as the mask/track back-end by MLLM grounders (Sa2VA, Seg-Zero uses SAM2-Large)

title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
authors: Nicolas Carion, Laura Gustafson, Yuan-Ting Hu, et al.
task: promptable concept segmentation (all instances of a noun phrase / exemplar) in images and videos; SAM 3 Agent for RES and reasoning segmentation
A_query: phrase/class name; visual exemplar; implicit instruction
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; novel categories/compositions
architecture: shared perception backbone with an image-level DETR-style detector (with presence head) and a memory-based video tracker; SAM 3 Agent wraps an MLLM that iteratively calls SAM 3
foundation_models: Perception Encoder backbone (per paper); SAM 3 Agent with Qwen2.5-VL 7B/72B, Llama4 Maverick, Qwen3-VL, Gemini 2.5 Pro
mechanism: presence token/head decouples 'is the concept in the image?' from localisation; exemplar and noun-phrase prompts; agent loop: MLLM proposes noun phrases, inspects SAM 3 masks and accepts/refines
objective: detection/segmentation losses with presence supervision on data-engine labels including hard negatives (concepts absent from the image)
robustness_tests: image-level presence evaluated with IL_MCC (classification of concept presence, i.e. hard negatives) on SA-Co; agent evaluated with several MLLMs
limitations: concept prompts are short noun phrases; complex referring language needs the agent wrapper, whose zero-shot RES cIoU (71.6 RefCOCO val with a 72B MLLM) remains below fine-tuned MLLM segmenters (our reading)

title: Florence-2: Advancing a Unified Representation for a Variety of Vision Tasks
authors: Bin Xiao, Haiping Wu, Weijian Xu, et al.
task: prompt-based multitask vision incl. REC, RES (polygon), phrase grounding, detection, captioning
architecture: DaViT vision encoder + Transformer encoder-decoder (0.23B / 0.77B) emitting text with quantised location tokens (boxes, polygons)
mechanism: all tasks posed as text-prompted seq2seq; regions expressed as location tokens, masks as polygons
objective: seq2seq cross-entropy on FLD-5B (5.4B annotations from an iterative automated annotation/model-refinement engine); optional task-agnostic generalist fine-tuning on public data incl. RefCOCO-mix
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: large zero-shot vs fine-tuned gap on RefCOCO (56.3 vs 93.4) indicates reliance on in-domain referring data; training labels largely auto-generated (label-noise risk, our reading); no absence handling

title: Universal Instance Perception as Object Discovery and Retrieval
authors: Bin Yan, Yi Jiang, Jiannan Wu, et al.
task: unified instance perception: detection, segmentation, REC, RES, SOT, VOS, MOT, VIS, R-VOS
A_query: phrase/class name; referring expression; visual prompt
architecture: ResNet-50 / ConvNeXt-L / ViT-H visual encoder + BERT text encoder, early fusion, Deformable-DETR-style object discovery, prompt-instance matching for retrieval
mechanism: 'discover then retrieve': class-agnostic instance proposals are scored against prompt embeddings (category names, expressions or reference annotations)
objective: joint multi-stage training (Objects365 -> COCO + RefCOCO/g/+ -> video/tracking mixture) with detection/segmentation and retrieval losses; single unified weights
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: referring tasks assume exactly one target (top-1 retrieval); no absent-target mechanism (our reading)

title: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models to the World
authors: Zhiliang Peng, Wenhui Wang, Li Dong, et al.
task: grounded captioning, REC, phrase grounding, REG
architecture: Kosmos-1-style causal Transformer LM (24-layer Magneto, ~1.6B trainable parameters) with vision encoder + resampler; 32x32 location-token vocabulary
mechanism: boxes as discrete location tokens inside Markdown-style links '[text span](<loc> <loc>)'
objective: next-token prediction on GrIT (web image-text pairs with noun phrases auto-grounded by a detector) plus interleaved and text data
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: zero-shot REC far below fine-tuned models; GrIT boxes are produced automatically (noise risk, our reading); no absence handling

title: Ferret: Refer and Ground Anything Anywhere at Any Granularity
authors: Haoxuan You, Haotian Zhang, Zhe Gan, et al.
task: referring (point/box/free-form region in) and grounding (box out) in dialogue; REC, phrase grounding
architecture: CLIP image encoder + Vicuna LLM (7B/13B) + spatial-aware visual sampler for free-form regions
mechanism: hybrid region representation (discrete coordinates + continuous features sampled from the region); boxes output as text coordinates
objective: instruction tuning on GRIT (1.1M refer-and-ground samples incl. 95K hard negatives from spatial negative mining)
robustness_tests: object hallucination on POPE (Table 10); spatial negative mining (image-conditioned and semantics-conditioned negative categories) aimed at recognising absent objects
limitations: absence recognition is learned as a textual response from negative-mined data rather than a dedicated, evaluated abstention head; no gRefCOCO-style no-target evaluation (our reading)

title: LISA: Reasoning Segmentation via Large Language Model
authors: Xin Lai, Zhuotao Tian, Yukang Chen, et al.
architecture: LLaVA-7B/13B (v1.1; LLaVA-1.5 variants) + ViT-H SAM encoder and mask decoder; <SEG> token hidden state projected as mask prompt
mechanism: embedding-as-mask: last-layer embedding of a <SEG> token prompts the SAM decoder
objective: text cross-entropy + BCE/DICE mask loss on semantic segmentation, referring segmentation (refCLEF/RefCOCO/+/g), VQA and 239 ReasonSeg samples (LoRA)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: always emits a mask: no rejection for absent targets (GSVA reports LISA-7B N-acc 2.71 on gRefCOCO val) and single-target only; ReasonSeg has only 239 train / 200 val / 779 test images (small benchmark)

title: GLaMM: Pixel Grounding Large Multimodal Model
authors: Hanoona Rasheed, Muhammad Maaz, Sahal Shaji Mullappilly, et al.
task: grounded conversation generation (GCG); RES; region captioning
A_query: referring expression; visual prompt; implicit instruction
architecture: ViT-H/14 CLIP global image encoder + region encoder + Vicuna-7B LLM + SAM-based grounding image encoder and pixel decoder
mechanism: <SEG> tokens interleaved in the response are decoded into masks for the preceding phrases (pixel-level grounded conversation)
objective: pre-training on auto-annotated GranD (11M images, 810M regions) then fine-tuning (GranD-f for GCG; refCOCO/+/g for RES)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: GranD is auto-annotated at very large scale (noise risk, our reading); no absent-target handling; RES numbers come from a RES-fine-tuned checkpoint, yet later tables list them alongside generalist models

title: PixelLM: Pixel Reasoning with Large Multimodal Model
authors: Zhongwei Ren, Zhicheng Huang, Yunchao Wei, et al.
architecture: CLIP-ViT encoder + LLaVA LLM (7B / Llama2-13B) + lightweight pixel decoder with a multi-scale segmentation codebook (no SAM)
mechanism: groups of codebook tokens per target fused and decoded by a light pixel decoder; target refinement loss separates multiple targets
objective: text loss + mask losses + target refinement loss on mixed segmentation/referring data and the GPT-4V-built MUSE dataset
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no explicit absent-target handling; multi-target evaluated on MUSE/MRefCOCO, not gRefCOCO (our reading)

title: Groma: Localized Visual Tokenization for Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models
authors: Chuofan Ma, Yi Jiang, Jiannan Wu, et al.
architecture: image encoder + class-agnostic region proposer + region encoder producing region tokens + Vicuna-7B
mechanism: localized visual tokenization: proposals become region tokens; the LLM grounds by emitting region-token references instead of coordinates
objective: detection pre-training of the proposer, alignment pre-training, then instruction fine-tuning (incl. RefCOCO/g/+ and GPT-4V-curated Groma Instruct)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: recall of the region proposer bounds grounding (our reading); no absence handling evaluated

title: GSVA: Generalized Segmentation via Multimodal Large Language Models
authors: Zhuofan Xia, Dongchen Han, Yizeng Han, et al.
architecture: LLaVA (Vicuna-7B/13B or Llama2-13B) + SAM ViT-H mask decoder; multiple [SEG] tokens and a [REJ] token
mechanism: one [SEG] per target (multi-target) and a learnable [REJ] token emitted for null referents, so no mask is produced for absent targets
objective: text + mask losses on SemSeg, RES (RefCOCO/+/g, refCLEF, gRefCOCO), VQA and ReasonSeg mix (LoRA); optional fine-tuning on gRefCOCO or classic RES
robustness_tests: no-target evaluation on gRefCOCO (N-acc); ablation (Table 4): removing [REJ] drops val N-acc from 56.45 to 30.32 (multiple [SEG] kept) and LISA-7B scores 2.71 N-acc
limitations: rejection is a single global token (no per-target uncertainty); N-acc ~56-66 shows absent targets are still often segmented (failure case Fig. 7)

title: Sa2VA: Marrying SAM2 with MLLM for Dense Grounded Understanding of Images and Videos
authors: Haobo Yuan, Xiangtai Li, Tao Zhang, et al.
task: RES and grounded conversation in images and videos (Ref-VOS)
architecture: InternVL2/2.5 (also Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, Qwen3-VL variants) MLLM + SAM 2 decoder/tracker; [SEG] token hidden state prompts SAM 2
mechanism: decoupled design: MLLM produces [SEG] instruction embedding that prompts SAM 2; SAM 2 memory propagates masks over frames
objective: single-stage instruction co-training on image QA, image seg (RefCOCO/+/g, GranD-f), video QA and video seg (incl. auto-labelled Ref-SAV)
robustness_tests: none reported for absence/robustness
limitations: always segments a target; no rejection mechanism; Ref-SAV labels auto-generated with a manually validated subset only

title: Shikra: Unleashing Multimodal LLM's Referential Dialogue Magic
authors: Keqin Chen, Zhao Zhang, Weili Zeng, et al.
task: referential dialogue: REC, REG, PointQA, grounded captioning
architecture: CLIP ViT-L/14 visual encoder + one FC alignment layer + Vicuna-7B/13B
mechanism: coordinates written as plain normalised numbers in natural language (no extra vocabulary, no detector); Table 2 ablation finds numerical text slightly better than extra location tokens
objective: two-stage instruction tuning on converted grounding data (RefCOCO/+/g, VG, Flickr30K Entities, PointQA, VQAv2) plus generated referential dialogue (Shikra-RD)
robustness_tests: none reported for grounding (POPE hallucination results are reported in the paper)
limitations: single box per query; no absence handling; RefCOCO-family train sets inside the instruction mix

title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond
authors: Jinze Bai, Shuai Bai, Shusheng Yang, et al.
task: general VLM with REC / grounded captioning
architecture: OpenCLIP ViT-bigG visual encoder + single-layer cross-attention adapter + Qwen-7B LLM
mechanism: boxes as normalised text coordinates wrapped in special <box>/<ref> tokens
objective: 3-stage training: pre-training, multi-task pre-training (incl. GRIT, VG, RefCOCO/+/g grounding), supervised fine-tuning (Qwen-VL-Chat)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no absent-target handling; RefCOCO-family data in pre-training

title: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
authors: Shuai Bai, Keqin Chen, Xuejing Liu, et al.
task: general MLLM with box/point grounding (also documents, video, agents)
architecture: native dynamic-resolution ViT with window attention + Qwen2.5 LLM (3B/7B/72B)
mechanism: absolute pixel coordinates (no normalisation) emitted as text/JSON for boxes and points
objective: large-scale pre-training incl. grounding data with absolute coordinates, synthesised non-existent object categories in queries, and multi-instance images; SFT + preference post-training
robustness_tests: none reported for grounding (training adds synthesised non-existent categories, but no absence evaluation is reported)
limitations: grounding data composition and RefCOCO-family exposure not disclosed; no evaluated abstention

title: Seg-Zero: Reasoning-Chain Guided Segmentation via Cognitive Reinforcement
authors: Yuqi Liu, Bohao Peng, Zhisheng Zhong, et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: decoupled: Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B reasoning model emits CoT + box + points; frozen SAM2-Large produces the mask
mechanism: reasoning chain then positional prompts (bbox + 2 points) handed to a promptable segmenter
objective: pure RL (GRPO) with format rewards and box-IoU/L1 and point accuracy rewards on 9,000 RefCOCOg-derived samples; no explicit reasoning data
robustness_tests: in-domain vs out-of-domain comparison of RL vs SFT (Table 1: SFT lowers ReasonSeg from 47.6 to 44.9, RL+CoT raises it to 53.8)
limitations: always outputs one mask; no absent-target handling; RES reported only on testA/test splits

title: VLM-R1: A Stable and Generalizable R1-style Large Vision-Language Model
authors: Haozhan Shen, Peng Liu, Jingcheng Li, et al.
task: REC and open-vocabulary detection via RL-tuned VLM
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (also 7B/32B scaling) trained with an open-r1-based GRPO framework
mechanism: R1-style think-then-answer; rule-based IoU reward for REC and an odLength-penalised mAP reward for OVD
objective: GRPO with verifiable rewards on RefCOCO/+/g train (REC) and detection data (OVD), compared with SFT
robustness_tests: out-of-domain REC on LISA-Grounding (RL 63.14 vs SFT 54.82 at step 600); analysis of reward hacking in OVD (Sec. 5.3.1)
limitations: reward hacking observed for detection (models emit many boxes under naive AP reward); REC gains over the base model are small in-domain

title: Detect Anything via Next Point Prediction
authors: Qing Jiang, Junan Huo, Xingyu Chen, et al.
task: detection, object referring, pointing, visual prompting, GUI grounding, OCR, keypoints
A_query: phrase/class name; referring expression; visual prompt
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Qwen2.5-VL-3B with special tokens for quantised coordinates
mechanism: next-point prediction: boxes/points as quantised coordinate tokens; GRPO with geometry-aware rewards suppresses duplicate and oversized boxes
objective: SFT on public + data-engine data (incl. HumanRef, RefCOCOg for referring), then GRPO with geometry-aware rewards
robustness_tests: none for absence: the HumanRef rejection subset is excluded from evaluation (only five subsets used); RL analysed as reducing duplicate predictions
limitations: F1-based metrics are not comparable with Acc@0.5 tables; rejection not evaluated

title: MiniGPT-v2: large language model as a unified interface for vision-language multi-task learning
authors: Jun Chen, Deyao Zhu, Xiaoqian Shen, et al.
task: multi-task MLLM incl. REC, REG, grounded captioning, VQA
architecture: ViT visual backbone + linear projection (4 adjacent tokens merged) + LLaMA2-chat 7B
mechanism: task identifier tokens (e.g. [refer], [grounding]) select the task; boxes as text coordinates
objective: 3-stage training: weakly-labelled image-text + GRIT-20M grounding, then fine-grained datasets (RefCOCO/+/g, VG, VQA), then multimodal instruction data
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single box output; no absence handling

title: CogVLM: Visual Expert for Pretrained Language Models
authors: Weihan Wang, Qingsong Lv, Wenmeng Yu, et al.
task: general VLM; grounding variant CogVLM-Grounding for REC, grounded captioning, grounded VQA
architecture: EVA2-CLIP-E ViT + MLP adapter + Vicuna-7B with trainable visual-expert (QKV/FFN) modules in every layer (CogVLM-17B)
mechanism: deep fusion via visual expert weights for image tokens; boxes as text '[[x0,y0,x1,y1]]'
objective: image-text pre-training then alignment; CogVLM-Grounding trained on public grounding data (Flickr30K Entities, RefCOCO, Visual7W, VG, Grounded CoT-VQA)
robustness_tests: none reported for grounding (POPE hallucination reported for CogVLM-Chat)
limitations: grounding requires a separate CogVLM-Grounding checkpoint; no absence handling

title: Ferret-v2: An Improved Baseline for Referring and Grounding with Large Language Models
authors: Haotian Zhang, Haoxuan You, Philipp Dufter, et al.
task: referring and grounding (REC, phrase grounding) with any-resolution input
architecture: CLIP encoder (any-resolution grid) + additional DINOv2 encoder for multi-granularity features + Vicuna LLM (7B/13B)
mechanism: any-resolution referring/grounding; multi-granularity visual encoding; hybrid region representation as in Ferret
objective: three-stage training with an added high-resolution dense-alignment stage before instruction tuning
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no absence/abstention evaluation (our reading)

title: GroundingGPT: Language Enhanced Multi-modal Grounding Model
authors: Zhaowei Li, Qi Xu, Dong Zhang, et al.
task: multi-modal grounding: image REC, video temporal grounding, audio(-visual) grounding
architecture: modality-specific encoders + adapters (MLP) + Vicuna-v1.5-7B
mechanism: boxes and timestamps emitted as text; coarse-to-fine three-stage multimodal grounding training
objective: 3-stage training: alignment, fine-grained grounding (RefCOCO/+/g, VG, DiDeMo/Charades-STA, VGGSS), multi-granularity instruction tuning
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no absence handling; video/audio grounding parts belong to other slices

title: PSALM: Pixelwise SegmentAtion with Large Multi-modal Model
authors: Zheng Zhang, Yeyao Ma, Enming Zhang, et al.
task: generalist segmentation: RES, GRES (zero-shot), panoptic, open-vocabulary, interactive
A_query: referring expression; phrase/class name; visual prompt
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; novel categories/compositions
architecture: Swin-B visual encoder + Phi-1.5 (1.3B) LMM + Mask2Former-style mask decoder with mask tokens
mechanism: LMM outputs condition embeddings from instruction/condition prompts; mask tokens query a mask decoder that proposes and classifies masks
objective: vision-language alignment then joint training on COCO panoptic, RefCOCO/+/g, COCO-Interactive and LLaVA-1.5 data
robustness_tests: zero-shot generalized RES on gRefCOCO (multi/no-target) without N-acc; zero-shot open-vocabulary and video segmentation
limitations: zero-shot gRefCOCO far below single-target RES (42.0 vs 83.6 cIoU), indicating weak handling of empty/multi-target expressions; no explicit rejection

title: OMG-LLaVA: Bridging Image-level, Object-level, Pixel-level Reasoning and Understanding
authors: Tao Zhang, Xiangtai Li, Hao Fei, et al.
task: pixel-, object- and image-level understanding: RES, GCG, region captioning, panoptic segmentation
architecture: single frozen universal segmenter (OMG-Seg, ConvNeXt-L CLIP) as visual encoder + perception-prior embedding + InternLM2-7B; [SEG] decoded by the frozen OMG decoder
mechanism: object queries from the segmenter enter the LLM as object-centric tokens; [SEG] embeddings are decoded by the (optionally frozen) segmentation decoder
objective: pre-training + instruction tuning on mixed segmentation, RES, GCG and VQA data
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no absent-target handling; frozen-decoder generalist trails fine-tuned variant by 2-3.5 cIoU

title: VisionLLM v2: An End-to-End Generalist Multimodal Large Language Model for Hundreds of Vision-Language Tasks
authors: Jiannan Wu, Muyan Zhong, Sen Xing, et al.
task: generalist MLLM with REC, RES, reasoning segmentation, detection, pose, generation
A_query: referring expression; implicit instruction; visual prompt; phrase/class name
architecture: CLIP-L/14 image encoder + Vicuna-7B-v1.5 + task-specific decoders (Grounding DINO for boxes/masks, UniPose for keypoints, diffusion for generation) linked by 'super link' queries
mechanism: 'super link': routing tokens + learnable super-link queries pass LLM hidden states to task decoders end-to-end
objective: three-stage end-to-end multi-task training on hundreds of datasets (incl. RefCOCO/+/g, ReasonSeg)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: REC below specialist detectors despite a Grounding DINO decoder; no absence handling

title: SAM4MLLM: Enhance Multi-Modal Large Language Model for Referring Expression Segmentation
authors: Yi-Chia Chen, Wei-Hua Li, Cheng Sun, et al.
architecture: Qwen-VL-7B-Chat (or LLaVA-1.6 8B) MLLM with LoRA + SAM (decoder fine-tuned on COCO)
mechanism: MLLM outputs a box and positive/negative prompt points as text (PPG) or is proactively queried whether sampled points lie inside the target (PQPP); points + box prompt SAM
objective: LoRA fine-tuning on RefCOCO/+/g and gRefCOCO (plus VQAv2; extra seg data for the * variant) with text targets derived from GT masks
robustness_tests: no-target evaluation on gRefCOCO (N-acc reported)
limitations: PQPP needs many MLLM queries per image (inference cost, our reading); the no-target decision mechanism is not separately analysed

title: u-LLaVA: Unifying Multi-Modal Tasks via Large Language Model
authors: Jinjin Xu, Liwu Xu, Yuzhe Yang, et al.
task: RES, REC, salient segmentation, VQA in one MLLM
architecture: CLIP ViT-L/14 visual encoder + projector + Vicuna-7B LLM + task-specific expert decoders for segmentation/grounding (boxes derived from masks)
mechanism: LLM hidden states of special tokens routed to expert decoders (embedding-as-mask)
objective: two-stage training (alignment, then joint instruction tuning on captioning, VQA, RES, semantic and salient segmentation)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no absence handling; RES gains partly from full-parameter LLM training (LoRA variant ~2 cIoU lower)

title: LISA++: An Improved Baseline for Reasoning Segmentation with Large Language Model
authors: Senqiao Yang, Tianyuan Qu, Xin Lai, et al.
task: reasoning semantic and instance segmentation in dialogue
architecture: LISA architecture unchanged (LLaVA-1.5 7B + SAM); data/format upgrades
mechanism: instance-level reasoning segmentation (multiple [SEG] per instance) and segmentation-in-dialogue answers interleaving masks with text
objective: instruction tuning with LLM-generated instance-level reasoning (ReasonSeg-Inst) and segmentation-in-dialogue data (prompt shown in Table 4) on top of LISA's mixture
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: still no rejection of absent targets (our reading); the new instance-level data are LLM-generated

title: Reasoning to Attend: Try to Understand How <SEG> Token Works
authors: Rui Qian, Xin Yin, Dejing Dou
task: reasoning segmentation; RES; false-premise referring segmentation
architecture: LISA/SESAME-style LLaVA-1.5 (7B/13B) + SAM, with a similarity-as-points module
mechanism: <SEG>-token-to-image-token similarity maps localise where the token 'attends'; high-similarity points are fed as extra prompts (reasoning to attend)
objective: text + mask losses on semantic/referring/ReasonSeg/VQA data plus FP-RefCOCO(+/g) and R-RefCOCO false-premise data
robustness_tests: false-premise evaluation on FP-RefCOCO/+/g val: 'see' accuracy 82.87/83.51/84.67 vs SESAME 79.84/80.00/81.78 (Table 5)
limitations: false-premise handling inherited from SESAME-style training data rather than a calibrated abstention score

title: POPEN: Preference-Based Optimization and Ensemble for LVLM-Based Reasoning Segmentation
authors: Lanyun Zhu, Tianrun Chen, Qianxiong Xu, et al.
task: reasoning segmentation (multi-target, MUSE) with text-hallucination reduction; RES
architecture: PixelLM architecture (CLIP-ViT-L/14-336 + LLaVA-7B or LLaVA-Llama2-13B + light pixel decoder)
mechanism: preference-based optimisation of text and segmentation outputs; at inference, multiple sampled responses are fused by preference-score-based attention (ensemble)
objective: PixelLM training, then preference optimisation with curriculum-collected segmentation preference data and a segmentation preference loss
robustness_tests: object hallucination in text responses measured with CHAIR-style CS/CI on MUSE (Table 1)
limitations: ensemble requires K sampled responses at inference (cost); no absent-target handling

title: SegLLM: Multi-round Reasoning Segmentation with Large Language Models
authors: XuDong Wang, Shaolun Zhang, Shufan Li, et al.
architecture: mask-aware MLLM (7B) with mask and box encoders feeding previous-round outputs back into the LLM + mask decoder
mechanism: previous segmentation outputs are re-encoded (mask-enc, box-enc) and reinserted into the conversation so later queries can reference earlier targets
objective: training on the MRSeg multi-round dataset (built from RefCOCO/+/g, PACO, LVIS, etc.) with mask and text losses
robustness_tests: robustness to question templates (Table 6: SegLLM 79.7/70.0/72.2 averaged cIoU vs LISA-7B(ft) 70.1/61.0/63.0); performance vs. conversation round on MR-RefCOCO (degrades from ~82 to ~70 cIoU by round 8)
limitations: accuracy still drops with more rounds; no absence handling

title: Advancing Visual Large Language Model for Multi-granular Versatile Perception
authors: Wentao Xiang, Haoxian Tan, Yujie Zhong, et al.
task: box and mask prediction from word- and sentence-level instructions: detection, panoptic/open-vocabulary segmentation, REC, RES, GRES
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; novel categories/compositions
architecture: Swin-B visual encoder + Phi-1.5 LLM + multi-granularity decoder (box and mask heads) with query selection
mechanism: CoT-style response (optionally captions/existing objects) then summary tokens condition a DETR-style multi-granularity decoder
objective: stage 1 connector alignment on CC3M; stage 2 joint training on COCO-Panoptic, RefCOCO, Objects365 and GoldG with LLM + box/mask losses
robustness_tests: zero-shot gRefCOCO (multi/no-target) only
limitations: strong single-target RES (83.6) but weak zero-shot gRefCOCO (37.6), i.e. poor transfer to empty/multi-target expressions; no rejection mechanism

title: Text4Seg: Reimagining Image Segmentation as Text Generation
authors: Mengcheng Lan, Chaofeng Chen, Yue Zhou, et al.
task: RES, GRES, REC and open-vocabulary segmentation via text output
architecture: off-the-shelf MLLMs (DeepSeek-VL 1.3B/7B, Qwen-VL-7B, LLaVA-1.5 7B/13B, InternVL2-8B) fine-tuned; optional SAM mask refiner
mechanism: semantic descriptors: each image patch (e.g. 16x16 grid) gets a text label; row-wise run-length encoding (R-RLE) shortens sequences by ~74%; masks decoded from text, optionally refined by SAM
objective: supervised fine-tuning (text cross-entropy) on RES/GRES data converted to semantic descriptors
robustness_tests: none reported (gRefCOCO N-acc not reported)
limitations: patch-level masks are coarse without the SAM refiner (e.g. RefCOCO val 74.7 at 32x32 without refiner vs 79.2 with); no-target accuracy not reported

title: Visual-RFT: Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
authors: Ziyu Liu, Zeyi Sun, Yuhang Zang, et al.
task: RL fine-tuning for perception: few-shot/open-vocabulary detection, reasoning grounding, fine-grained classification
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Qwen2-VL-2B/7B trained with GRPO
mechanism: think-then-answer outputs scored by verifiable IoU / confidence rewards (detection) and accuracy rewards (classification)
objective: GRPO with IoU-based rewards on small data (e.g. 239 ReasonSeg training images for reasoning grounding)
robustness_tests: none for absence; generalisation to novel categories (OV detection)
limitations: ReasonSeg is used as box-level 'reasoning grounding'; how masks/gIoU are obtained from boxes is not stated in the table, so numbers are not directly comparable with mask-based ReasonSeg results (our reading)

title: UniVG-R1: Reasoning Guided Universal Visual Grounding with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Sule Bai, Mingxing Li, Yong Liu, et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Qwen2-VL-7B
mechanism: CoT-then-box answers; cold-start SFT on 90k MLLM-generated CoT grounding samples, then GRPO with IoU rewards and difficulty-aware weighting
objective: SFT on CoT data sampled from MGrounding-630k, then rule-based RL (GRPO)
robustness_tests: zero-shot transfer to four image/video reasoning-grounding benchmarks (reported average +23.4%)
limitations: RL/CoT training does not improve standard RefCOCO over its base (91.64 vs 91.70 val); single-box outputs; no absence handling

title: Rex-Thinker: Grounded Object Referring via Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
authors: Qing Jiang, Xingyu Chen, Zhaoyang Zeng, et al.
task: object referring (multi-target REC with rejection) via grounded CoT
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; novel categories/compositions
architecture: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct; candidate boxes (box hints from a detector) given as input
foundation_models: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, Grounding DINO (box hints in OOD evaluation)
mechanism: retrieval-based referring: planning -> per-candidate verification (action) -> summarisation; may output no box when nothing matches
objective: SFT cold start on GPT-4o-generated HumanRef-CoT, then GRPO with F1-based accuracy and format rewards
robustness_tests: HumanRef rejection subset (1,000 images with absent referents): rejection score 68.2 for Rex-Thinker-GRPO vs 7.1 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, 0.0 for Groma/ChatRex and 2.0 for Ferret-7B (Table 2); box hints raise DF1 but lower rejection (71.7 -> 53.5, Table 4)
limitations: depends on candidate box hints; OOD RefCOCOg protocol injects GT category via detector hints; rejection still fails on ~1/3 of absent cases

title: GROUNDHOG: Grounding Large Language Models to Holistic Segmentation
authors: Yichi Zhang, Ziqiao Ma, Xiaofeng Gao, et al.
task: grounded generation and language-to-segmentation (RES, GRES, reasoning seg, phrase grounding)
A_query: referring expression; implicit instruction; visual prompt; phrase/class name
architecture: LLaMA2-7B (initialised from LLaVA-1.5) + vision encoders + Mask2Former+ class-agnostic mask proposals; grounding tokens select/merge proposals
mechanism: holistic Mask2Former+ proposals become entity tokens; phrases wrapped in <GRD>...</GRD> grounding tokens use their hidden states to score, select and merge mask proposals (decoupled recognition and localisation)
objective: instruction tuning on M3G2 (2.5M text-image pairs, 36 sub-problems from 27 datasets) with box and mask supervision
robustness_tests: object hallucination on POPE (Sec. 4.3 'Reduced Object Hallucination'); failure diagnosability via inspecting selected proposals
limitations: grounding bounded by proposal quality (Mask2Former+); gRefCOCO N-acc not reported

title: TALL: Temporal Activity Localization via Language Query
authors: Jiyang Gao, Chen Sun, Zhenheng Yang et al.
architecture: C3D (Sports-1M) clip features (fc6) for sliding-window clips + LSTM / Skip-thought sentence embeddings; CTRL cross-modal processing module
mechanism: CTRL: multimodal fusion (add, multiply, FC) of clip+context features with sentence embedding; scores sliding-window candidates and regresses temporal offsets
objective: alignment (matching) loss + temporal boundary regression loss (reg-np: non-parameterised offsets)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: sliding-window proposals are dense and costly; assumes the queried activity exists in the video (our reading); Charades-STA later shown to contain moment-location biases (Otani et al. 2020; Yuan et al. 2021)

title: Localizing Moments in Video with Natural Language
authors: Lisa Anne Hendricks, Oliver Wang, Eli Shechtman et al.
architecture: Moment Context Network (MCN): RGB + optical-flow features with local and global video context, LSTM language encoder, shared embedding space
mechanism: ranks candidate moments (fixed 5-s segment combinations) by distance between moment (local+global+temporal-endpoint) embedding and sentence embedding
objective: ranking losses (intra-video and inter-video negatives)
robustness_tests: none reported; expressions were collected and validated so that they uniquely identify one moment (ambiguity reduced by design)
limitations: coarse fixed candidate segments (5-s units); single-moment assumption (our reading)

title: Detecting Moments and Highlights in Videos via Natural Language Queries
authors: Jie Lei, Tamara L. Berg, Mohit Bansal
architecture: Moment-DETR: transformer encoder-decoder over concatenated SlowFast + CLIP ViT-B/32 clip features (every 2 s) and CLIP text features; moment queries + saliency head
mechanism: joint self-attention encoder over video and query tokens; learnable moment queries decode a set of spans with Hungarian matching; clip-level saliency scores for highlights
objective: L1 + gIoU span losses, foreground classification, hinge saliency loss; optional weakly-supervised pre-training on ASR captions
robustness_tests: none reported (performance breakdown by video category in appendix Table 7)
limitations: assumes at least one relevant moment per query; no rejection of irrelevant queries (later shown by Flanagan et al. 2025); fixed 2-s clip granularity (our reading)

title: UniVTG: Towards Unified Video-Language Temporal Grounding
authors: Kevin Qinghong Lin, Pengchuan Zhang, Joya Chen et al.
task: moment retrieval + highlight detection + video summarisation
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 + SlowFast R-50 video features, CLIP text encoder; multimodal transformer encoder with foreground, boundary-regression and saliency heads
mechanism: unified clip-level label formulation (foreground indicator, boundary offsets, saliency) lets one single-stream model serve MR, HD and VS; inter/intra-video contrastive saliency
objective: focal foreground loss + SmoothL1/IoU boundary losses + inter/intra contrastive saliency losses; large-scale pre-training on 4.2M pseudo-labelled samples (Ego4D points, VideoCC intervals, CLIP-teacher curves)
robustness_tests: zero-shot transfer reported (QVHighlights test MR R1@0.5 25.16, HIT@1 53.50; Charades-STA R1@0.5 25.22, mIoU 27.12; Tables 2-3); no negative-query or bias tests
limitations: assumes the queried moment is present (Flanagan et al. 2025 build UniVTG-NA to reject negatives); relies on frozen pre-extracted features (our reading)

title: Ego4D: Around the World in 3,000 Hours of Egocentric Video
authors: Kristen Grauman, Andrew Westbury, Eugene Byrne et al.
architecture: benchmark suite; NLQ baselines adapt existing temporal grounding models (details not extracted)
mechanism: n/a (dataset); NLQ maps a question about the wearer's past to the temporal window where the answer is visible or deducible
objective: n/a
robustness_tests: none reported for NLQ; privacy/de-identification protocol described
limitations: NLQ answers may only be deducible rather than directly visible; very long clips make localisation hard (our reading)

title: TimeChat: A Time-sensitive Multimodal Large Language Model for Long Video Understanding
authors: Shuhuai Ren, Linli Yao, Shicheng Li et al.
task: video-LLM temporal grounding / highlight detection / dense captioning
architecture: EVA-CLIP ViT-G/14 image encoder + timestamp-aware image Q-Former (InstructBLIP init) + sliding video Q-Former (Video-LLaMA init) + LLaMA-2 7B (frozen ViT and LLM, LoRA)
foundation_models: EVA-CLIP ViT-G/14, InstructBLIP Q-Former, Video-LLaMA, LLaMA-2 7B
mechanism: frame features fused with their timestamps; sliding-window video Q-Former yields variable-length video tokens; timestamps generated as text
objective: instruction tuning on TimeIT (125K instances, 6 timestamp-related tasks) + Valley
robustness_tests: none reported; heuristic rules are needed to parse colloquial LLM outputs into timestamps
limitations: timestamps produced as free text require parsing; zero-shot accuracy far below task-specific models; no handling of queries without a matching moment (our reading)

title: Time-R1: Post-Training Large Vision Language Model for Temporal Video Grounding
authors: Ye Wang, Ziheng Wang, Boshen Xu et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (also 3B) post-trained with reinforcement learning; reasoning (think) then timestamp answer
mechanism: reasoning-guided RL post-training (GRPO/DAPO-style) with timestamp-aware tIoU and format rewards; TimeRFT data-efficient curriculum with sample filtering
objective: RL with verifiable reward (tIoU + format) on ~2.5K curated samples
robustness_tests: TVGBench balances 11 query types across videos and queries to limit distribution bias; per-type mIoU breakdown (Appendix Table 3); no negative-query test
limitations: no rejection of absent moments; zero-shot R1@0.7 remains well below fine-tuned specialists (our reading)

title: Uncovering Hidden Challenges in Query-Based Video Moment Retrieval
authors: Mayu Otani, Yuta Nakashima, Esa Rahtu et al.
architecture: analysis of 2D-TAN and SCDM plus blind (video-free) baselines
mechanism: sanity checks: action-aware blind baselines that ignore the video, human re-annotation agreement, nearest-neighbour vs representative references
objective: n/a
robustness_tests: Core bias audit: blind baselines exploiting moment-location/length priors reach competitive R@1; annotation ambiguity measured with repeated human annotations (Charades-STA representative-human R@1 IoU>0.5 52.1 vs 2D-TAN 39.7, SCDM 51.7; Table 1)
limitations: analyses two benchmarks and two models; no new debiased benchmark released (our reading)

title: Moment of Untruth: Dealing with Negative Queries in Video Moment Retrieval
authors: Kevin Flanagan, Dima Damen, Michael Wray
architecture: UniVTG-NA: UniVTG backbone (also applied to CG-DETR and QD-DETR) with a negative-aware rejection head
foundation_models: CLIP, SlowFast (inherited from UniVTG features); GPT-4o and Claude 3 Opus used to generate out-of-domain negative queries
mechanism: learns to reject queries with no matching moment (in-domain negatives from other videos, out-of-domain LLM-generated negatives) before localising
objective: standard moment losses + negative-query rejection training
robustness_tests: Core: standard VMR models (UniVTG, CG-DETR, QD-DETR) reject 0% of negative queries; thresholding saliency/indicator scores gives poor or inconsistent rejection (Table 1); UniVTG-NA reaches 96.84% ID / 100% OOD rejection on QVHighlights at a cost of ~3.9 R1@0.5 (Table 2)
limitations: in-domain negatives on Charades-STA remain hard (64% rejection); negatives are query-level, not partial mismatches (our reading)

title: Where Does It Exist: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Multi-Form Sentences
authors: Zhu Zhang, Zhou Zhao, Yang Zhao et al.
architecture: STGRN: object proposals (Faster R-CNN, Visual Genome) per frame organised into a spatio-temporal region graph; GRU query encoder; spatio-temporal localiser
foundation_models: Faster R-CNN pre-trained on Visual Genome (per TubeDETR Table 4)
mechanism: multi-step cross-modal graph reasoning over implicit/explicit spatial and temporal subgraphs; dynamic selection of tube without tube pre-generation
objective: temporal boundary loss + spatial region selection loss
robustness_tests: none reported; interrogative sentences (unknown object attributes) evaluated separately from declarative sentences
limitations: depends on pre-extracted detector proposals; target may occupy only a short temporal segment, and temporal localisation is the bottleneck (with GT temporal bounds m_vIoU rises to 38.04) (from Table 2)

title: Human-Centric Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding With Visual Transformers
authors: Zongheng Tang, Yue Liao, Si Liu et al.
