architecture: STGVT: person tubes from a detector + linking, visual transformer for cross-modal tube-sentence matching and temporal trimming
foundation_models: pre-training on Visual Genome + Conceptual Captions (per TubeDETR Table 4)
mechanism: visual-transformer cross-modal representation of candidate person tubes and sentence; matching plus temporal trimming
objective: tube-sentence matching loss + temporal localisation loss
robustness_tests: none reported; dataset is built from multi-person scenes so that distractor persons are present
limitations: two-stage pipeline bounded by person-tube proposals; single human referent only (our reading)

title: TubeDETR: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding with Transformers
authors: Antoine Yang, Antoine Miech, Josef Sivic et al.
architecture: video-text encoder (slow multimodal branch on sparsely sampled frames + fast visual-only branch) on MDETR (ResNet-101 + RoBERTa) weights; space-time decoder with time-aligned queries
foundation_models: MDETR (pre-trained on Flickr30k, MS COCO, Visual Genome), ResNet-101, RoBERTa
mechanism: per-frame time-encoded queries with temporal self-attention and cross-attention to video-text features jointly predict boxes and start/end probabilities
objective: L1 + gIoU box losses, KL temporal start/end losses, guided attention loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single target per query; sparse frame sampling trades accuracy for memory; numbers in arXiv v2 differ from the CVPR camera-ready (authors' note)

title: Embracing Consistency: A One-Stage Approach for Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
authors: Yang Jin, Yongzhi Li, Zehuan Yuan et al.
architecture: STCAT: ResNet-101 visual encoder + RoBERTa text encoder, cross-modal encoder with temporal interaction, decoder with local and global multimodal templates
mechanism: multimodal template (global objective plus per-frame local templates) generated from video-text context conditions all frame queries so predictions stay consistent across frames; no external detector
objective: box (L1+gIoU) and temporal boundary losses
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single-target assumption; template consistency does not handle target absence (our reading)

title: Actor and Action Video Segmentation from a Sentence
authors: Kirill Gavrilyuk, Amir Ghodrati, Zhenyang Li et al.
architecture: I3D video encoder + text encoder; fully-convolutional decoder with dynamic filters generated from the sentence
mechanism: sentence-conditioned dynamic convolutional filters applied to video feature maps at several resolutions
objective: per-pixel segmentation loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: expressions mostly describe actors with static cues; no target-absence handling (our reading)

title: URVOS: Unified Referring Video Object Segmentation Network with a Large-Scale Benchmark
authors: Seonguk Seo, Joon-Young Lee, Bohyung Han
architecture: ResNet-50 encoder; cross-modal attention (referring image segmentation) + memory attention (mask propagation) in one network
mechanism: cross-modal attention localises the referent per frame; memory attention propagates previous masks for temporal coherence and to prevent drift
objective: per-frame mask loss
robustness_tests: none reported beyond drift mitigation
limitations: single referent per expression; offline two-step inference (our reading)

title: Language as Queries for Referring Video Object Segmentation
authors: Jiannan Wu, Yi Jiang, Peize Sun et al.
architecture: ReferFormer: visual backbone (ResNet / Swin / Video-Swin) + RoBERTa; Deformable-DETR transformer; cross-modal FPN; dynamic mask head
mechanism: a small set of object queries conditioned on the sentence attend to frame features; per-frame queries generate dynamic convolution kernels for masks and are linked across frames for tracking
objective: Hungarian-matched box, class, dice and focal mask losses
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: assumes the referent exists in the clip; MeViS later shows it relies on static appearance cues (our reading)

title: MeViS: A Large-scale Benchmark for Video Segmentation with Motion Expressions
authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He et al.
architecture: LMPM baseline: Mask2Former-style language-guided extractor (Swin-T) producing per-frame object embeddings, motion perception transformer over object embeddings, RoBERTa text encoder (frozen)
mechanism: language queries select candidate object embeddings per frame; motion perception across frames; matching to expression allows multiple referred objects
objective: mask losses with matching over object trajectories
robustness_tests: Shortcut analysis: image-based VLT (one frame) reaches 63.1 J&F on Ref-YouTube-VOS and 60.4 on DAVIS17-RVOS but only 27.8 on MeViS (Table 2), showing earlier RVOS benchmarks are solvable from static cues; expressions can refer to multiple objects
limitations: baseline LMPM leaves large headroom; no explicit no-target expressions in v1 (added in TPAMI v2) (our reading)

title: MeViS: A Multi-Modal Dataset for Referring Motion Expression Video Segmentation
authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He et al.
architecture: LMPM++: LMPM object-embedding extractor (Video-Swin-T/B) + Video-LLaMA-7B reasoning over object embeddings, outputs target object tokens or no-target
mechanism: LLM consumes per-frame object embeddings and the (text or audio) expression, selects 0..K targets; consistency loss across frames
objective: segmentation losses + LLM token loss + temporal consistency loss (L_con)
robustness_tests: No-target evaluation on MeViSv2: prior RVOS models (URVOS, MTTR, ReferFormer, VLT+TC) never predict no-target (N-acc 0.0), DsHmp 21.0, LMPM++ 45.7 (Table VII); single- vs multi-target breakdown; audio-expression (AVOS) evaluation; RMOT on MeViSv2 with no-target-adapted HOTA* (TransRMOT 18.6, LMPM++ 38.1; Table X)
limitations: LLM-based model is slow (2.86 FPS vs 32.1 for LMPM; Table V); no-target accuracy still below 50%

title: Referring Multi-Object Tracking
authors: Dongming Wu, Wencheng Han, Tiancai Wang et al.
architecture: TransRMOT: ResNet-50 + RoBERTa, Deformable-DETR encoder with early cross-modal fusion, MOTR-style detect and track queries, referent head
mechanism: cross-modal encoder fuses expression into multi-scale visual features; track queries carry identities across frames; referent score thresholded (beta_ref = 0.4) to select 0..K referred tracks
objective: detection/tracking set losses + binary referent loss
robustness_tests: none reported (ablation of referring threshold shows HOTA 31.1-35.5 sensitivity; Table 3d)
limitations: small driving dataset (18 videos); expressions are template-like; performance sensitive to referent threshold (our reading)

title: TRACE: Temporal Grounding Video LLM via Causal Event Modeling
authors: Yongxin Guo, Jingyu Liu, Mingda Li et al.
task: video-LLM temporal grounding / dense captioning / highlight detection
architecture: video LLM with separate time, score and text encoders/heads and a vision compression layer; frozen vision encoder (LLM backbone name not extracted)
mechanism: causal event modeling: video output is a sequence of events, each = (timestamps, salient score, caption) produced by task-specific heads conditioned on previous events
objective: two-stage instruction tuning (1.9M then 0.9M samples incl. VTG-IT, InternVid, ActivityNet Captions)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: no rejection of absent events; performance depends on number of sampled frames (Table 3) (our reading)

title: VTimeLLM: Empower LLM to Grasp Video Moments
authors: Bin Huang, Xin Wang, Hong Chen et al.
architecture: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 frame features (100 frames) + linear projector + Vicuna v1.5 (7B/13B) with LoRA
mechanism: boundary-aware three-stage training: image-text alignment, multi-event video boundary perception (InternVid-derived), instruction tuning on high-quality dialogues; frame indices emitted as text
objective: next-token prediction across three stages
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: timestamps as text; coarse 100-frame sampling; no absent-moment handling (our reading)

title: Number it: Temporal Grounding Videos like Flipping Manga
authors: Yongliang Wu, Xinting Hu, Yuyang Sun et al.
architecture: NumPro: frame numbers rendered onto frames (visual prompt) fed to off-the-shelf Vid-LLMs (GPT-4o, Qwen2-VL, LLaVA-Video, LongVA); NumPro-FT fine-tunes LongVA-7B-DPO (frozen visual encoder)
mechanism: visible frame numbers let the Vid-LLM answer with frame indices that link language queries to frame-level boundaries, like reading manga panel numbers
objective: none (training-free) or NumPro-augmented VTG instruction fine-tuning (NumPro-FT)
robustness_tests: none reported; ablation of number font size, colour and position (Table 3) shows sensitivity of the visual prompt (Charades R@0.5 29.5-37.8)
limitations: relies on frame sampling and OCR-like reading of overlaid numbers; prompt placement affects accuracy (Table 3)

title: A Closer Look at Temporal Sentence Grounding in Videos: Dataset and Metric
authors: Yitian Yuan, Xiaohan Lan, Xin Wang et al.
architecture: re-evaluation of CTRL, ACRN, ABLR, SCDM, 2D-TAN, DRN, TSP-PRL, WSSL plus bias-only baselines
mechanism: re-splits datasets so moment-location distributions differ between train and test-ood; bias-penalising metric discounts predictions by boundary error
objective: n/a
robustness_tests: Core OOD test: on Charades-CD, 2D-TAN drops from 43.46 (test-iid) to 30.77 (test-ood) dR@1,IoU@0.5 and a bias-only baseline reaches 16.87 on test-iid (Table 2); similar drops on ActivityNet-CD
limitations: only moment-location shift is studied; models evaluated with authors' re-implementations (our reading)

title: VideoGLaMM: A Large Multimodal Model for Pixel-Level Visual Grounding in Videos
authors: Shehan Munasinghe, Hanan Gani, Wenqi Zhu et al.
architecture: dual encoder (CLIP ViT-L/14-336 spatial + InternVideo2 temporal) with V->L adapters, Phi3-Mini-3.8B LLM, SAM2-initialised frame encoder and spatio-temporal pixel decoder
mechanism: LLM emits segmentation tokens tied to caption phrases; L->V adapter maps them to SAM2-style pixel decoder prompts producing masks across frames
objective: text generation loss + mask (BCE/Dice) losses on semi-automatically annotated grounded conversation data
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single-target masks per phrase; no target-absence handling (our reading)

title: VISA: Reasoning Video Object Segmentation via Large Language Models
authors: Cilin Yan, Haochen Wang, Shilin Yan et al.
architecture: Text-guided Frame Sampler (LLaMA-VID) selects key frames; Chat-UniVi 7B/13B multimodal LLM emits <SEG>; SAM decoder masks the key frame; XMem propagates to remaining frames
mechanism: LLM reasons over world knowledge and video, its <SEG> embedding prompts SAM on a target frame, then object tracking propagates the mask
objective: text generation + mask (BCE/Dice) losses; instruction tuning with ReVOS
robustness_tests: ReVOS includes hallucination (no-target) instructions; robustness score R (from R2-VOS) reported: VISA 13B R = 8.3 without and 14.5 with ReVOS instruction tuning (Table 1) -- low values indicate frequent false-positive masks
limitations: single key-frame reasoning then propagation can miss temporal reasoning; low robustness score on hallucination queries (Table 1)

title: RefEgo: Referring Expression Comprehension Dataset from First-Person Perception of Ego4D
authors: Shuhei Kurita, Naoki Katsura, Eri Onami
architecture: dataset + baselines adapting image REC models (MDETR) with per-frame object-presence handling (details not extracted)
mechanism: frame-level grounding over egocentric clips where the referent may leave the frame
objective: n/a
robustness_tests: referred object can be absent in some frames and similar distractor objects are present (dataset design)
limitations: not extracted beyond dataset design (our reading)

title: Learning 2D Temporal Adjacent Networks for Moment Localization with Natural Language
authors: Songyang Zhang, Houwen Peng, Jianlong Fu et al.
architecture: 2D-TAN: 2D temporal feature map over all (start, end) candidate moments built by max-pooling or stacked convolution over clip features (VGG for Charades, C3D for ActivityNet/TACoS); LSTM sentence encoder
mechanism: sentence feature fused with every cell of the 2D moment map; temporal adjacent network of 2D convolutions models context between neighbouring moments; each cell scored
objective: scaled-IoU binary cross-entropy on moment-map cells
robustness_tests: none reported in the paper; later audits (Otani et al. 2020; Yuan et al. 2021) show 2D-TAN drops from 43.46 to 30.77 dR@1,IoU@0.5 under the Charades-CD OOD split
limitations: quadratic candidate map; dense proposal scoring exploits moment-location priors (per later bias audits)

title: Span-based Localizing Network for Natural Language Video Localization
authors: Hao Zhang, Aixin Sun, Wei Jing et al.
architecture: VSLNet: I3D clip features + GloVe word embeddings, shared feature encoder, context-query attention, query-guided highlighting, conditioned span predictor
mechanism: treats the video as a text passage and the moment as an answer span (QA-style); query-guided highlighting enlarges the foreground region to search
objective: start/end span cross-entropy + highlighting (foreground) loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single span per query; assumes the moment exists (our reading)

title: Negative Sample Matters: A Renaissance of Metric Learning for Temporal Grounding
authors: Zhenzhi Wang, Limin Wang, Tao Wu et al.
task: temporal sentence grounding (also STVG on HC-STVG)
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: MMN: 2D moment map (2D-TAN-style) + DistilBERT sentence encoder; separate moment and sentence embeddings in a joint space (dual-stream / late fusion)
mechanism: mutual matching: cross-modal metric learning with intra-video and inter-video negative moments and sentences instead of early fusion
objective: binary IoU loss + mutual matching contrastive losses
robustness_tests: none reported (negative samples are used for training, not for evaluating absent-moment rejection)
limitations: quadratic moment map; negatives are other videos' moments, so no explicit absent-target decision (our reading)

title: Query-Dependent Video Representation for Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
authors: WonJun Moon, Sangeek Hyun, SangUk Park et al.
architecture: QD-DETR: cross-attentive transformer encoder (video clips attend to query words), transformer encoder, DETR decoder with dynamic anchor moment queries, saliency token
foundation_models: SlowFast + CLIP features (QVHighlights); VGG / C3D / SF+C for Charades; optional PANN audio
mechanism: query-dependent video representation via cross-attention injection; negative (irrelevant) video-query pairs train saliency to depend on the query
objective: L1 + gIoU + CE span losses, saliency margin and rank-contrastive losses, negative-pair saliency loss
robustness_tests: none reported; Flanagan et al. (WACV 2025) later show QD-DETR rejects 0% of negative queries
limitations: assumes a relevant moment exists; negative pairs only shape saliency, not rejection (our reading)

title: Knowing Where to Focus: Event-aware Transformer for Video Grounding
authors: Jinhyun Jang, Jungin Park, Jin Kim et al.
architecture: EaTR: DETR-style video grounding with event reasoning (slot-attention-like event units) that initialises video-specific moment queries, plus gated-fusion transformer layer
mechanism: event-aware dynamic moment queries derived from the video's own event structure instead of input-agnostic learnable queries; gated fusion with the sentence
objective: DETR span losses + saliency loss + event loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: assumes queried event exists; higher HD HIT@1 not achieved vs QD-DETR (58.65 vs 62.40) (Table 1)

title: TR-DETR: Task-Reciprocal Transformer for Joint Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
authors: Hao Sun, Mingyao Zhou, Wenjing Chen et al.
architecture: TR-DETR: local-global multimodal alignment, visual feature refinement, and task-cooperation modules on a DETR-style MR/HD model
foundation_models: SlowFast+CLIP (QVHighlights); VGG / I3D / SF+C for Charades
mechanism: highlight-detection saliency scores are injected into moment retrieval and retrieved moments refine highlight scores (task reciprocity)
objective: DETR span losses + saliency losses + alignment losses
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: assumes a relevant moment exists (our reading)

title: Correlation-Guided Query-Dependency Calibration for Video Temporal Grounding
authors: WonJun Moon, Sangeek Hyun, SuBeen Lee et al.
architecture: CG-DETR: adaptive cross-attention with dummy tokens, clip-word correlation learner, moment-adaptive saliency detector on a DETR-style MR/HD model
mechanism: dummy tokens absorb attention for clips irrelevant to the query, calibrating query dependency; clip-word correlation supervises fine-grained alignment
objective: DETR span losses + saliency losses + orthogonality/alignment losses
robustness_tests: none reported in the paper; Flanagan et al. 2025 show 0% negative-query rejection for CG-DETR, and TD-DETR (ICCV 2025) measures its spurious predictions on masked videos
limitations: query dependency is calibrated but no absent-moment output (our reading)

title: MomentDiff: Generative Video Moment Retrieval from Random to Real
authors: Pandeng Li, Chen-Wei Xie, Hongtao Xie et al.
architecture: MomentDiff: similarity-aware condition generator over video/text features + video moment denoiser (transformer decoder) operating on noisy spans
foundation_models: VGG / C3D / SlowFast+CLIP video features; GloVe or CLIP text features
mechanism: generative diffusion over spans: random spans are iteratively denoised into real moments conditioned on video-text similarity, reducing reliance on learned location priors
objective: diffusion denoising with span regression (L1/gIoU) and similarity loss
robustness_tests: Bias/OOD: introduces anti-bias splits Charades-STA-Len and Charades-STA-Mom (length and moment-location shifts) and evaluates on Charades-CD / ActivityNet-CD; on Charades-STA-Mom R1@0.5 MomentDiff 33.59 vs 2D-TAN 20.44, MMN 27.20, Moment-DETR 22.16 (Table 5); on Charades-CD R1@0.5 47.17 vs Moment-DETR 41.18 (Table 4)
limitations: iterative denoising slower than Moment-DETR (Table 8/9 timing); still degrades substantially under location shift

title: Momentor: Advancing Video Large Language Model with Fine-Grained Temporal Reasoning
authors: Long Qian, Juncheng Li, Yu Wu et al.
architecture: Video-LLM with a temporal perception module (continuous temporal tokens with interpolation and neighbouring token propagation) and grounded event-sequence modeling
mechanism: continuous temporal position tokens let the LLM read and emit precise timestamps; trained on automatically built segment-level instruction data
objective: instruction tuning on Moment-10M (automatically generated, 10M instructions)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: zero-shot grounding accuracy remains low (Charades R1@0.7 11.6); synthetic training data quality not audited (our reading)

title: SnAG: Scalable and Accurate Video Grounding
authors: Fangzhou Mu, Sicheng Mo, Yin Li
task: temporal sentence grounding / egocentric NLQ (long video)
architecture: SnAG: transformer video encoder (multi-scale), late cross-attention fusion with token-wise sentence embeddings, point-based (anchor-free) moment decoder
mechanism: late fusion lets one video encoding be reused across many queries (query-centric training), making grounding in hour-long videos scalable
objective: focal classification + distance-IoU regression per time point
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: assumes the queried moment exists; Ego4D-NLQ accuracy remains low (R@1 IoU0.5 11.26 with EgoVLP features) (Table 1)

title: The Devil is in the Spurious Correlations: Boosting Moment Retrieval with Dynamic Learning
authors: Xinyang Zhou, Fanyue Wei, Lixin Duan et al.
architecture: TD-DETR: QD-DETR-style model with a video synthesizer for dynamic context (VSDC) and a temporal dynamics enhancement module (TDEM); plug-in to QD-DETR, CG-DETR, BAM-DETR and SnAG
mechanism: synthesises videos that splice target moments into new backgrounds so the model cannot rely on spurious moment-context correlations; enhances temporal dynamics of the query-relevant clips
objective: DETR span and saliency losses on original and synthesised videos
robustness_tests: Spurious-correlation test: target clips in QVHighlights val videos are replaced by random-valued masks; models that still predict the masked span are counted as spurious (Spurious R1@0.7: QD-DETR 9.35 -> 8.26, CG-DETR 4.65 -> 2.58, BAM-DETR 7.16 -> 1.61 with TD-DETR; Table 3)
limitations: evaluated on two benchmarks; masking test probes context reliance but not absent-query rejection (our reading)

title: Context-Guided Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
authors: Xin Gu, Heng Fan, Yan Huang et al.
architecture: CG-STVG: STCAT/TubeDETR-style one-stage DETR STVG with instance context generation (ICG) and instance context refinement (ICR) modules in the decoder
foundation_models: ResNet-101 + RoBERTa (MDETR-style; not re-checked this session)
mechanism: mines visual context of the target instance from the video and uses it as extra guidance for the spatial/temporal decoder queries, refining it stage by stage
objective: box (L1+gIoU) and temporal boundary losses
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single target per query; assumes the target appears (our reading)

title: Knowing Your Target: Target-Aware Transformer Makes Better Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
authors: Xin Gu, Yaojie Shen, Chenxi Luo et al.
architecture: TA-STVG: DETR-style STVG whose object queries are generated from the video-text pair by text-guided temporal sampling and attribute-aware spatial activation, instead of zero-initialised queries
foundation_models: not extracted this session (same family as CG-STVG)
mechanism: target-aware query initialisation: select text-relevant frames, activate attribute-relevant spatial features, then decode the tube
objective: box and temporal boundary losses (plus auxiliary sampling/activation supervision)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: single target; gains over CG-STVG are modest (+0.4 to +0.7 m_vIoU) (Tables 1-3)

title: End-to-End Referring Video Object Segmentation with Multimodal Transformers
authors: Adam Botach, Evgenii Zheltonozhskii, Chaim Baskin
architecture: MTTR: Video Swin-T visual backbone + RoBERTa, multimodal transformer encoder over joint video-text tokens, DETR-style decoder producing instance sequences, segmentation head
mechanism: joint multimodal transformer predicts a set of object sequences across frames; temporal segment voting selects the sequence matching the text
objective: Hungarian-matched sequence losses (dice + focal mask, reference score)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: short temporal window (w frames); target existence assumed (our reading)

title: OnlineRefer: A Simple Online Baseline for Referring Video Object Segmentation
authors: Dongming Wu, Tiancai Wang, Yuang Zhang et al.
architecture: OnlineRefer: ReferFormer-style per-frame DETR model (ResNet-50 / Swin-L / Video-Swin-B) with query propagation across frames
mechanism: explicit query propagation: target cues (reference point and query embedding) from the previous frame initialise the current frame's queries, giving online frame-by-frame tracking
objective: ReferFormer-style matched box/mask losses
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: errors propagate through queries once the target is lost; no re-detection or absence handling (our reading)

title: Spectrum-guided Multi-granularity Referring Video Object Segmentation
authors: Bo Miao, Mohammed Bennamoun, Yongsheng Gao et al.
architecture: SgMg: Video-Swin backbone + RoBERTa, multi-granularity segmentation optimiser, conditional patch kernel and spectrum-guided cross-modal fusion (frequency domain)
mechanism: segments directly from encoded (multi-granularity) features to avoid feature drift between decoder and encoder; spectrum-guided fusion performs cross-modal fusion in the frequency domain
objective: matched mask/box losses
robustness_tests: feature-drift analysis between decoder and encoder features (Table 6); no robustness tests
limitations: single referent; target existence assumed (our reading)

title: Robust Referring Video Object Segmentation with Cyclic Structural Consensus
authors: Xiang Li, Jinglu Wang, Xiaohao Xu et al.
architecture: R2-VOS: ReferFormer-style RVOS model (ResNet-50 / Swin-T / Video-Swin-T) with an object localizing module and text reconstruction branch
mechanism: jointly models R-VOS and its dual (text reconstruction); a structural text-to-text cycle constraint judges semantic consensus between video and expression, so masks are suppressed for negative (unpaired) videos
objective: segmentation losses + cyclic structural consistency loss on positive and negative video-text pairs
robustness_tests: Core: R2-VOS task where an expression is queried against videos that may not contain the referent; on the robust benchmark R2-VOS gets J&F 57.2, robustness R 51.2, A 64.5 vs ReferFormer 42.2/46.3/54.4 and MTTR 50.0/41.4/49.3 (Table 2). The R score is later adopted by VISA/ReVOS
limitations: negatives are whole unpaired videos rather than subtle near-miss expressions (our reading)

title: Decoupling Static and Hierarchical Motion Perception for Referring Video Segmentation
authors: Shuting He, Henghui Ding
architecture: DsHmp: LMPM-style framework (Swin-T on MeViS; Video-Swin-T/B on Ref-YouTube-VOS) with static/motion sentence decoupling and hierarchical motion perception
mechanism: decouples the expression into static and motion cues; static cues select candidate objects per frame, hierarchical motion perception across temporal scales handles motion; contrastive learning across visually similar objects
objective: segmentation losses + contrastive loss with hard negative objects
robustness_tests: none reported in this paper; MeViS TPAMI (MeViSv2) later reports DsHmp no-target accuracy N-acc 21.0
limitations: no explicit no-target output (our reading)

title: SAMWISE: Infusing Wisdom in SAM2 for Text-Driven Video Segmentation
authors: Claudia Cuttano, Gabriele Trivigno, Gabriele Rosi et al.
architecture: frozen SAM2 (Hiera-B) + frozen text encoder (RoBERTa or CLIP-B) with Cross-Modal Temporal (CMT) adapters and a Conditional Memory Encoder; adds fewer than 5M trainable parameters (per paper)
mechanism: adapters inject textual and temporal cues into frozen SAM2 features; conditional memory encoder detects when a better-matching object appears and corrects SAM2's tracking bias towards the first-tracked object
objective: mask losses training only adapters
robustness_tests: none reported (comparison against GroundingDINO box-prompt baselines in Table 9)
limitations: online processing within short windows; no no-target output (our reading)

title: One Token to Seg Them All: Language Instructed Reasoning Segmentation in Videos
authors: Zechen Bai, Tong He, Haiyang Mei et al.
architecture: VideoLISA: 3.8B video MLLM with Sparse Dense Sampling of frames + SAM mask decoder; a single <TRK> token segments and associates the object across all frames
foundation_models: SAM; 3.8B LLM (name not extracted this session)
mechanism: One-Token-Seg-All: one LLM-produced embedding prompts SAM in every frame, giving temporally consistent masks without a separate tracker; optional post-optimisation
objective: text generation + mask losses on image and video segmentation data
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: a single token per object assumes one referent; no explicit no-target output (our reading)

title: ViLLa: Video Reasoning Segmentation with Large Language Model
authors: Rongkun Zheng, Lu Qi, Xi Chen et al.
architecture: ViLLa: InternVideo2 (1B/6B) video MLLM + segmentation decoder, with context synthesizer, hierarchical temporal synchronizer and key segment sampler for long videos
mechanism: multi-scale temporal tokens synchronised with the LLM; long videos are adaptively partitioned into short, semantically dense segments before reasoning and mask decoding
objective: text + mask losses; trained with a new VideoReasonSeg dataset
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: heavy backbone (InternVideo2-6B for best results); no no-target evaluation (our reading)

title: MPG-SAM 2: Adapting SAM 2 with Mask Priors and Global Context for Referring Video Object Segmentation
authors: Fu Rong, Meng Lan, Qian Zhang et al.
architecture: BEiT-3 multimodal encoder (following EVF-SAM) + mask prior generator + hierarchical global-historical aggregator + SAM 2 prompt encoder / mask decoder
mechanism: jointly encoded video-text features produce pseudo-mask priors and multimodal class tokens that become dense and sparse prompts for SAM 2; global context aggregation gives the online SAM 2 a video-level view
objective: mask losses + similarity loss (L_sim)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: offline (needs whole video for global context); single referent (our reading)

title: iKUN: Speak to Trackers without Retraining
authors: Yunhao Du, Cheng Lei, Zhicheng Zhao et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: off-the-shelf MOT (YOLOv8 + NeuralSORT with neural Kalman filter) + insertable knowledge unification network (iKUN) built on CLIP-RN50 visual/text encoders
mechanism: plug-and-play referring module: a knowledge unification module extracts text-guided visual features for each track and scores it against the expression, so the tracker needs no retraining; similarity calibration adjusts scores using the description distribution
objective: track-expression matching loss (trackers frozen)
robustness_tests: none reported (oracle-detection upper bound shows localisation errors cost ~17 HOTA)
limitations: depends on detector quality; CLIP-RN50 scoring per track may miss motion semantics (our reading)

title: Objects that Sound
authors: Relja Arandjelović, Andrew Zisserman
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Two-stream audio and vision ConvNets embedding both modalities in a shared space; a localisation network scores image regions against the audio embedding
mechanism: Region-level audio-visual embedding similarity yields the localisation map (sounding-object localisation given audio)
objective: Self-supervised audio-visual correspondence (AVC) on unlabelled video
robustness_tests: none reported (includes a 'cautionary tale' on shortcut avoidance in data preparation)
limitations: Predates box-annotated benchmarks (VGG-SS) and the cIoU/AUC protocol; localisation evaluated mostly qualitatively (our reading from Stage-1 abstract notes)

title: Learning to Localize Sound Source in Visual Scenes
authors: Arda Senocak, Tae-Hyun Oh, Junsik Kim et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Two-stream (sound and vision) network with an audio-guided attention module producing the localisation map
mechanism: Attention over visual feature locations conditioned on the audio embedding
objective: Unsupervised AV pair correspondence (triplet-style); extendable to semi-/fully-supervised with a small amount of location labels
robustness_tests: none reported; authors note the unsupervised model reaches false conclusions in some cases, corrected by a small amount of supervision
limitations: Single frame + audio; unsupervised attention can latch onto wrong regions (stated by authors)

title: The Sound of Pixels
authors: Hang Zhao, Chuang Gan, Andrew Rouditchenko et al.
task: pixel-level sound localisation and source separation
architecture: PixelPlayer: video analysis network producing per-pixel visual features, audio U-Net producing spectrogram components, and a synthesizer combining them per pixel
mechanism: Each pixel's visual feature selects/weights audio components, giving a per-pixel separated sound (pixel-level grounding)
objective: Mix-and-Separate self-supervision: mix audio from two videos and learn to separate each using its visual stream
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single music-instrument domain; pixel-level grounding shown mainly qualitatively (Stage-1 reading)

title: Localizing Visual Sounds the Hard Way
authors: Honglie Chen, Weidi Xie, Triantafyllos Afouras et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Two-stream audio and image encoders; audio embedding correlated with the spatial visual feature map
mechanism: Cosine similarity between global audio embedding and each visual location; soft tri-map splits positive, uncertain and hard-negative regions
objective: Contrastive loss with automatically mined hard negatives (non-sounding regions of the same image) plus easy negatives from other images
robustness_tests: Open-set evaluation on 110 unheard VGG-SS classes (Table 6)
limitations: Assumes a visible sounding source in every test image; later work (Mo & Morgado 2022) shows its model, trained without early stopping on annotated data, collapses (VGG-SS cIoU 10.43) and cannot reject negatives

title: A Closer Look at Weakly-Supervised Audio-Visual Source Localization
authors: Shentong Mo, Pedro Morgado
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; missing modality; novel categories/compositions
architecture: Two-stream image/audio encoders (ImageNet-initialised vision) with momentum target encoders; SLAVC decomposes the AV similarity into a localisation (AVLoc) term and an audio-visual correspondence (AVC) term
foundation_models: ImageNet-pretrained visual encoder (weak supervision per the authors' framing)
mechanism: AVLoc map from audio-to-location similarity; AVC score decides whether any visible source matches the audio; extreme visual dropout prevents overfitting
objective: Contrastive AV alignment with extreme visual dropout (0.9) and momentum encoders; no box labels and no early stopping on annotated data
robustness_tests: Negative (no visible source) clips added to both test sets: real negatives, automated easy and hard negatives; per-type false-positive max-F1 (Table 5); evaluation with vs without annotated-data early stopping (Table 2); open-set heard/unheard VGG-SS split (Table 7)
limitations: Paper does not report AUC; negative detection still far from solved (Extended VGG-SS AP 32.95); OGL variant adds an object prior unrelated to audio

title: Sound Source Localization is All about Cross-Modal Alignment
authors: Arda Senocak, Hyeonggon Ryu, Junsik Kim et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Two-stream audio/image encoders trained from scratch (no pretrained vision); multiple positives mined by nearest-neighbour search with pretrained encoders
foundation_models: Supervised or self-supervised pre-trained encoders used only for NN positive mining
mechanism: Joint localisation and instance-level cross-modal alignment; conceptually similar samples act as extra positives
objective: Contrastive localisation loss plus cross-modal semantic alignment loss with multiple positives
robustness_tests: Extended VGG-SS/Flickr with negative (no-source) samples (Table 7); open-set heard/unheard splits (Tables 3-4); cross-modal retrieval as a semantic-alignment check (Table 6)
limitations: Argues localisation benchmarks alone cannot detect semantically wrong localisation (silent objects, off-screen sounds); its own negative-detection AP remains low (34.73 on Extended VGG-SS)

title: Localizing Visual Sounds the Easy Way
authors: Shentong Mo, Pedro Morgado
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Two-stream audio/visual encoders (ImageNet-initialised vision); at inference the AV map is fused with an object-guided localisation (OGL) map from an ImageNet-pretrained CNN
mechanism: Multiple-instance alignment: audio matched to the max-similarity visual location (MaxPool over sim(V_xy, A)); OGL adds a visual objectness prior
objective: Multiple-instance contrastive learning (audio aligned with at least one location of its paired image)
robustness_tests: Open-set heard/unheard VGG-SS split (Table 3); cross-dataset generalisation (Table 4)
limitations: Part of the gain comes from the audio-agnostic OGL visual prior (Table 5: +2.9 cIoU on VGG-SS); assumes a sounding object is always present (no negatives)

title: Audio-Visual Scene Analysis with Self-Supervised Multisensory Features
authors: Andrew Owens, Alexei A. Efros
task: sound source localisation; on/off-screen audio-visual source separation
architecture: Early-fusion multisensory 3D-CNN over video frames and raw audio
mechanism: Fused audio-visual features; class activation maps over the network localise sound-related regions
objective: Self-supervised temporal-alignment (synchronisation) prediction between video and audio
robustness_tests: Addresses off-screen sound explicitly via on/off-screen separation (no grounding-specific robustness metric extracted)
limitations: Localisation via CAMs is coarse and qualitative (our reading)

title: Audio–Visual Segmentation
authors: Jinxing Zhou, Jianyuan Wang, Jiayi Zhang et al.
architecture: Encoder-decoder segmentation network with ResNet-50 or PVT-v2 visual backbone and VGGish audio features; TPAVI fusion at four encoder stages
mechanism: Temporal pixel-wise audio-visual interaction (TPAVI) injects audio semantics into multi-scale visual features
objective: BCE mask loss plus audio-visual mapping regularisation (L_AVM)
robustness_tests: Audio ablation only: model without TPAVI/audio reaches S4 J .778 vs .787 with audio (PVT-v2, Table 5), i.e. most S4 performance is attainable without audio fusion
limitations: No negative/silent/off-screen audio evaluation; S4 nearly solvable visually (our reading of Table 5); later audits (AVSBench-Robust, Sun et al. 2024) show salience-driven segmentation

title: Audio-Visual Segmentation with Semantics
authors: Jinxing Zhou, Xuyang Shen, Jianyuan Wang et al.
architecture: Same TPAVI encoder-decoder as AVSBench (ResNet-50 / PVT-v2 + VGGish) with semantic (category) mask output
mechanism: TPAVI audio-visual fusion at four stages; per-pixel category prediction
objective: Cross-entropy semantic mask loss plus L_AVM regularisation
robustness_tests: Audio ablation (without TPAVI): AVSS mIoU 27.71 vs 29.77 (PVT-v2, Table V)
limitations: No negative/off-screen audio evaluation; semantic labels make the task partly solvable by visual semantic segmentation (our reading)

title: Ref-AVS: Refer and Segment Objects in Audio-Visual Scenes
authors: Yaoting Wang, Peiwen Sun, Dongzhan Zhou et al.
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; novel categories/compositions; multi-target
architecture: EEMC: Mask2Former-style query decoder; VGGish audio, text and visual encoders; cached multimodal memory and modality encoding
foundation_models: VGGish (audio); Mask2Former-style segmenter (M2F per TSAM's table)
mechanism: Expression-enhancing multimodal cues: audio, text and visual features fused into multimodal-cue queries that guide mask prediction
objective: Supervised mask loss on referred objects
robustness_tests: Null test set (expressions whose referent is absent/not visible; empty GT masks) scored by S = sqrt(predicted mask area / background area); modality ablations removing text or audio (Table 4: Seen J 34.20 -> 23.67 without text, 27.27 without audio)
limitations: Null metric S only measures predicted mask area, not an explicit abstention decision; F reported as a fraction while J is in % (mixed scales)

title: Towards Omnimodal Expressions and Reasoning in Referring Audio-Visual Segmentation
authors: Kaining Ying, Henghui Ding, Guangquan Jie et al.
A_query: referring expression; implicit instruction; speech; non-speech sound; visual exemplar; composite
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; novel categories/compositions; multi-target
architecture: OISA: MLLM with audio-visual interleaving of tokens and a query-propagation mask head (Mask2Former/SAM-style decoder)
foundation_models: MLLM (OISA-1B); SAM2 used for dataset annotation; mask head M2F or SAM
mechanism: Audio-Visual Interleaving aligns per-frame audio and video tokens; segmentation query propagated across frames; model outputs explanation text
objective: Instruction-style segmentation and explanation generation (mask loss + language loss)
robustness_tests: Ref-AVS Null split reported (S = 9.8 vs EEMC 0.7 on the same x100 scale, i.e. worse at producing empty masks); TVQA split stressing dialogue-heavy audio-visual alignment (Table 3); ReVOS robustness score R (Table 8)
limitations: Better J on referents but markedly worse Null S than the specialist EEMC (our reading of Table 6): MLLM grounding improves positives while hurting absent-target behaviour

title: MEERKAT: Audio-Visual Large Language Model for Grounding in Space and Time
authors: Sanjoy Chowdhury, Sayan Nag, Subhrajyoti Dasgupta et al.
task: AV-LLM spatial and temporal grounding (audio-referred image grounding; image-guided audio temporal localisation; AV fact-checking)
architecture: Image and audio encoders with modality-specific latents fed to instruction-tuned Llama 2 (LoRA); optimal-transport alignment module and audio-visual cross-attention consistency module
mechanism: OT-based weak alignment of image patches and audio tokens plus cross-attention consistency; boxes and time intervals emitted as numbers in text
objective: Instruction tuning on AVFIT (3M samples) with LM loss plus OT and attention-consistency losses
robustness_tests: Audio-visual fact-checking task (detecting audio-visual inconsistency) and claimed robustness to negative samples (Table 1 'Robustness' column); role-of-audio ablation on AVQA (Table 16)
limitations: Box outputs evaluated with cIoU/AUC on test sets whose sizes differ from the standard VGG-SS (5,158) and Flickr-SoundNet (250) protocols (Table 2), so numbers are not directly comparable to SSL heatmap methods (our reading); training data built from OpenImages-AudioSet/VGGSound class mappings

title: Audio-Visual Event Localization in Unconstrained Videos
authors: Yapeng Tian, Jing Shi, Bochen Li et al.
task: audio-visual event localisation (temporal AV grounding); cross-modality localisation
architecture: VGG-19 (ImageNet) visual features + VGG-like audio features; audio-guided visual attention; LSTMs with dual multimodal residual network (DMRN) fusion; AV distance-learning network (AVDLN)
mechanism: Audio-guided spatial attention on frames; per-second segment classification into event vs background; A2V/V2A matching for cross-modality localisation
objective: Segment-level cross-entropy (supervised) or MIL with video-level labels (weakly supervised); contrastive distance learning for cross-modality localisation
robustness_tests: Unimodal (audio-only, visual-only) baselines reported, quantifying missing-modality performance (Table 1)
limitations: Each 10 s clip contains a single event; audio-only or visual-only segments are background by definition (task design)

title: Unveiling and Mitigating Bias in Audio Visual Segmentation
authors: Peiwen Sun, Honggang Zhang, Di Hu
architecture: n/c (not checked this session)
mechanism: Identifies 'audio priming bias' (audio queries collapse to dominant/common sounds) and 'visual prior' (segmentation driven by visual salience); proposes debiasing strategies for both (details n/c)
objective: n/c
robustness_tests: Bias analysis of AVS models (audio priming bias, visual prior); details not extracted
limitations: Not checked in full this session

title: Crab: A Unified Audio-Visual Scene Understanding Model with Explicit Cooperation
authors: Henghui Du, Guangyao Li, Chang Zhou et al.
task: unified AV-LLM: temporal localisation (AVE, AVVP), audio-referred image grounding, AVS, Ref-AVS, AVQA
A_query: non-speech sound; speech; referring expression; implicit instruction; composite
C_referent: event/action; sound source; object instance; set (0..K)
D_output: temporal interval; point/heatmap; mask; grounded text; 2D box
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; novel categories/compositions
architecture: CLIP-ViT-L/14 visual encoder with visual and audio Q-Formers (32 queries), LLaMA-2-7B-Chat with interaction-aware LoRA (multi-head), mask decoder for pixel-level outputs
mechanism: Explicit reasoning-process annotations (AV-UIE) teach cooperation across tasks; interaction-aware LoRA heads specialise on temporal / spatial / pixel-level interaction
objective: Multi-task instruction tuning on AV-UIE (text loss + segmentation BCE/Dice losses)
robustness_tests: Ref-AVS Null split reported (S 0.01); no other negative-audio tests
limitations: ARIG baselines in Table 4 (LVS 23.69, EZ-VSL 26.43, FNAC 27.15) coincide with FNAC's zero-shot AVSBench S4 mIoU values yet are labelled cIoU, so the ARIG comparison mixes metrics (our reading); AVSS 26.52 (Table 1) vs 26.59 (Tables 5/8) inconsistency

title: Empowering LLMs with Pseudo-Untrimmed Videos for Audio-Visual Temporal Understanding
authors: Yunlong Tang, Daiki Shimada, Jing Bi et al.
task: AV-LLM temporal grounding (audio-visual video temporal understanding)
architecture: AVicuna: audio-visual LLM (details n/c)
mechanism: Pseudo-untrimmed videos (PU-VALOR) built by concatenating trimmed clips give timestamped events for temporal grounding
objective: Instruction tuning on PU-VALOR with timestamp supervision (details n/c)
robustness_tests: none reported (n/c)
limitations: Pseudo-untrimmed concatenations may not reflect natural event boundaries (our reading)

title: Dense-Localizing Audio-Visual Events in Untrimmed Videos: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Baseline
authors: Tiantian Geng, Teng Wang, Jinming Duan et al.
task: dense audio-visual event localisation (temporal AV grounding)
architecture: Audio-visual pyramid transformer with cross-modal fusion and temporal downsampling; I3D (RGB+flow) visual features; class-aware regression and event dependency modelling
mechanism: Unimodal and cross-modal transformer layers over a temporal feature pyramid; dense per-timestep classification and boundary regression
objective: Classification + boundary regression losses (anchor-free, ActionFormer-style)
robustness_tests: Unimodal (audio-only / visual-only) variants quantify missing-modality performance (Table 2)
limitations: Event categories closed-set (100 classes); untrimmed but still short (42 s average) videos

title: R-AVST: Empowering Video-LLMs with Fine-Grained Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in Complex Audio-Visual Scenarios
authors: Lu Zhu, Tiantian Geng, Yangye Chen et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Video-LLM fine-tuned for audio-visual spatio-temporal reasoning (details n/c)
mechanism: n/c
objective: n/c
robustness_tests: n/c
limitations: Not checked in full this session

title: SAM2-LOVE: Segment Anything Model 2 in Language-aided Audio-Visual Scenes
authors: Yuji Wang, Haoran Xu, Yong Liu et al.
architecture: Multimodal fusion transformer (RoBERTa text, ViT visual, audio encoder) producing a learnable [seg] prompt token for SAM2; memory attention frozen, prompt encoder and mask decoder trained
mechanism: [seg] token propagation with [cls]-token accumulation across frames compresses audio-text-visual cues into one prompt for SAM2
objective: Supervised mask loss on Ref-AVS
robustness_tests: Ref-AVS Null split reported: s = 0.23, much worse than EEMC (0.007) and all +text/+audio baselines (0.17-0.21) in the same table
limitations: Large gains on Seen/Unseen come with the worst Null score in its own comparison table (our reading): a single prompt token always yields a mask, so absent referents are segmented

title: Hearing and Seeing Through CLIP: A Framework for Self-Supervised Sound Source Localization
authors: Sooyoung Park, Arda Senocak, Joon Son Chung
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: CLIP-based framework: audio mapped into CLIP text-encoder token space so the frozen CLIP image-text alignment localises the sounding region; LLM-guided extension (decoder details n/c)
foundation_models: CLIP; an LLM for guidance (which one n/c)
mechanism: Audio tokens replace text prompts so CLIP's text-image alignment localises the sound source
objective: Self-supervised AV contrastive + localisation objectives (details n/c)
robustness_tests: n/c (the WACV predecessor park2024clip evaluates Extended VGG-SS/Flickr negatives and open-set splits)
limitations: Not read in full this session

title: Seeing Speech and Sound: Distinguishing and Locating Audio Sources in Visual Scenes
authors: Hyeonggon Ryu, Seongyu Kim, Joon Son Chung et al.
task: simultaneous speech and sound grounding (audio-visual segmentation from mixed audio)
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: HuBERT audio backbone with separate speech and sound heads; visual encoder producing dense features (visual backbone n/c)
mechanism: Mix-and-separate: mixed speech+sound input, each head grounds its audio type in the image
objective: Self-supervised mix-and-separate contrastive objectives
robustness_tests: Overlapping speech + non-speech mixtures (simultaneous grounding) vs DenseAV
limitations: Speech grounding slightly below DenseAV on individual speech (Table 2); semantic segmentation protocol differs from VGG-SS/AVSBench

title: Exploiting Transformation Invariance and Equivariance for Self-supervised Sound Localisation
authors: Jinxiang Liu, Chen Ju, Weidi Xie et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: SSL-TIE: ResNet-18 visual and audio encoders in a Siamese framework over two transformed views
mechanism: Localisation maps required to be invariant to appearance/audio transformations and equivariant to geometric transformations across the two views
objective: Audio-visual contrastive loss plus geometric-consistency loss (L_cl + L_geo)
robustness_tests: Open-set heard/unheard split (Table 4); audio and cross-modal retrieval (Tables 5-6)
limitations: No negative (silent/off-screen) evaluation; assumes one visible source

title: Learning Sound Localization Better from Semantically Similar Samples
authors: Arda Senocak, Hyeonggon Ryu, Junsik Kim et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: HardPos: two-stream vision/audio encoders on the LVS framework
mechanism: Semantically similar samples (nearest neighbours in embedding space) used as hard positives in contrastive learning
objective: Contrastive localisation loss with hard positives mined from semantically similar pairs
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Notes that the released LVS model is ~3% cIoU below LVS's paper numbers (reproducibility caveat in Table 1)

title: Learning Audio-Visual Source Localization via False Negative Aware Contrastive Learning
authors: Weixuan Sun, Jiayi Zhang, Jianyuan Wang et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: FNAC on the EZ-VSL framework (two-stream encoders, optional OGL)
mechanism: Intra-modal audio/image adjacency used to suppress false negatives (FNS) and enhance true negatives (TNE) in contrastive learning
objective: False-negative-aware contrastive loss with adjacency-based regularisers
robustness_tests: Open-set heard/unheard VGG-SS (Table 3: unheard cIoU 42.91 with OGL); zero-shot transfer to AVSBench
limitations: No negative-sample evaluation in the paper; ACL-SSL (WACV 2024, Table 3) reports FNAC's Extended VGG-SS AP as only 23.48, lowest among compared methods (cross-paper observation)

title: Can CLIP Help Sound Source Localization?
authors: Sooyoung Park, Arda Senocak, Joon Son Chung
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; novel categories/compositions; multi-target
architecture: ACL-SSL: frozen pre-trained CLIP image and text encoders; audio-driven embedder maps audio into CLIP text-token space; audio-visual grounder (image encoder, grounder, mask generators)
mechanism: Audio-driven embeddings replace text prompts, so CLIP text-image alignment produces audio-grounded masks; audio-visual correspondence objective on the masked visual features
objective: Self-supervised audio-visual alignment (image- and feature-level ACL losses) plus area regularisation on generated masks; no text labels
robustness_tests: Extended VGG-SS/Flickr with negative samples (Table 3); open-set heard/unheard (Table 2); zero-shot AVSBench S4/MS3 (Table 4)
limitations: Gains rely on CLIP's large-scale image-text pre-training (extra pre-training data: yes); CLIPSeg with ground-truth text labels is a strong upper reference (VGG-SS cIoU 49.50)

title: Mix and Localize: Localizing Sound Sources in Mixtures
authors: Xixi Hu, Ziyang Chen, Andrew Owens
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: ResNet-18 image encoder and audio encoder; graph-based (random-walk) correspondence between image regions and mixed audio sources
mechanism: Synthetic mixtures of several videos' audio; contrastive random walk on a bipartite graph between audio and visual regions assigns each source to a location
objective: Self-supervised mixed-correspondence objective (random-walk cycle over audio-visual graph)
robustness_tests: Multi-source (mixture) localisation on MUSIC-Synthetic/Duet and VGGSound-Instruments
limitations: Authors flag (*) that some numbers may benefit from best-matching pair assignment (Sec. 4.4); no VGG-SS/Flickr evaluation

title: AVSegFormer: Audio-Visual Segmentation with Transformer
authors: Shengyi Gao, Zhe Chen, Guo Chen et al.
architecture: ResNet-50 or PVTv2 visual backbone, VGGish audio; transformer decoder with audio queries + 300 learnable queries; channel-attention audio-visual mixer
mechanism: Audio features become decoder queries attending to multi-scale visual features; audio-visual mixer amplifies relevant channels
objective: Mask losses plus an auxiliary mixing loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: 512x512 variant (*) reported alongside 224 results (S4 83.06, MS3 61.33, AVSS 37.31), so cross-paper comparisons must check resolution; Ref-AVS paper shows it reaches Null S 0.171 when given text (cross-paper)

title: Multimodal Variational Auto-encoder based Audio-Visual Segmentation
authors: Yuxin Mao, Jing Zhang, Mochu Xiang et al.
architecture: ECMVAE: ResNet-50 or PVT encoder; multimodal VAE factorising latent space into modality-shared and modality-specific parts; segmentation decoder
foundation_models: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 / PVT; VGGish (as in AVSBench setup, n/c)
mechanism: Explicitly conditional multimodal VAE models the audio-visual joint distribution; JS-divergence alignment of modality latents
objective: Segmentation loss + VAE ELBO terms + JS-divergence + latent constraints (L_diff, L_sic)
robustness_tests: Ablation with a 'w/o audio' baseline taken from AVSBench (Table 2: S4 77.80 / MS3 48.20)
limitations: No negative/noisy-audio evaluation

title: CATR: Combinatorial-Dependence Audio-Queried Transformer for Audio-Visual Video Segmentation
authors: Kexin Li, Zongxin Yang, Lei Chen et al.
architecture: ResNet-50 / PVT-v2 encoder; decoupled audio-visual transformer for spatio-temporal dependencies; blockwise-encoded gate; audio-queried decoder
foundation_models: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 / PVT-v2; AOT used to supplement annotations in the * setting
mechanism: Decoupled spatial and temporal audio-visual attention; audio-constrained queries decode object masks
objective: Mask segmentation losses (optionally with AOT-propagated extra annotations)
robustness_tests: Audio-removed variant (Table 4): without audio CATR still reaches S4 J 80.7 (vs 84.4 with audio, * setting) but MS3 drops to 43.9 (vs 62.7), quantifying visual-only shortcut on single-source data
limitations: Best numbers use extra AOT-generated annotations (*), complicating comparison

title: Cooperation Does Matter: Exploring Multi-Order Bilateral Relations for Audio-Visual Segmentation
authors: Qi Yang, Xing Nie, Tong Li et al.
architecture: COMBO: ResNet-50 / PVT-v2 encoder with Siam-Encoder module, Bilateral-Fusion module and inter-frame consistency loss (query-based decoder, our reading)
foundation_models: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 / PVT-v2; a foundation segmentation prior for the Siam-Encoder (marked 'external model' in CPM's comparison)
mechanism: Models pixel-, modality- and temporal-entanglement via bilateral audio-visual fusion and siamese prior features
objective: Mask losses plus inter-frame loss
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Uses an external foundation-model prior (flagged as 'External Model' in CPM's Table 1); no negative-audio tests

title: CPM: Class-Conditional Prompting Machine for Audio-Visual Segmentation
authors: Yuanhong Chen, Chong Wang, Yuyuan Liu et al.
architecture: Transformer (Mask2Former-style) AVS model on D-ResNet50 with class-conditional prompts for visual (VCP) and audio (ACP) streams, GMM-based class distributions, prompting-based contrastive learning (PCL)
mechanism: Class-agnostic queries augmented with class-conditional prompts sampled from learned class distributions to stabilise bipartite matching and cross-attention
objective: Mask/class losses + class-conditional distribution modelling + prompting-based contrastive learning
robustness_tests: VPO multi-source multi-instance split (same-class distractor instances)
limitations: Two AVSS protocols (224 J vs original-resolution mIoU) give very different numbers (34.53 vs 57.25), a comparability hazard

title: Unraveling Instance Associations: A Closer Look for Audio-Visual Segmentation
authors: Yuanhong Chen, Yuyuan Liu, Hu Wang et al.
architecture: CAVP: per-pixel classification (DeepLabV3+ on D-ResNet50) with audio-visual fusion and a contrastive audio-visual pairing module
mechanism: Supervised contrastive audio-visual pairing pulls same-class audio-visual fused features together and pushes different classes apart
objective: Segmentation loss + CAVP contrastive loss
robustness_tests: False detection rate (FDR) on AVSS and VPO; VPO multi-source multi-instance split with same-class instances where only some sound
limitations: VPO pairs images with audio synthetically (post-production), so spatial/temporal audio cues are artificial; Table 2 shows 'initial' vs revised results (version churn: arXiv v7)

title: Stepping Stones: A Progressive Training Strategy for Audio-Visual Semantic Segmentation
authors: Juncheng Ma, Peiwen Sun, Yaoting Wang et al.
architecture: AAVS: Mask2Former with Swin-B (ADE20k-pretrained), mostly frozen with adapters; VGGish audio; adaptive audio query generator
mechanism: Two-stage progressive training: first localise sounding objects (binary AVS), then use the localisation as a 'stepping stone' (mask fusion, robust key) for semantic segmentation
objective: Mask/class losses per stage
robustness_tests: Oracle analysis: replacing first-stage localisation with ground truth raises AVSS mIoU 48.5 -> 64.9 (Table 4), isolating localisation as the bottleneck
limitations: Strong segmentation prior (ADE20k Mask2Former) makes gains partly visual (our reading); no negative-audio tests

title: BAVS: Bootstrapping Audio-Visual Segmentation by Integrating Foundation Knowledge
authors: Chen Liu, Peike Li, Hu Zhang et al.
architecture: Two-stage: foundation segmentation model proposes instance masks (silent-object-aware), then an audio-visual semantic integration strategy (AVIS) selects sounding instances using audio tagging; ResNet / PVT / Swin backbones
foundation_models: Foundation segmentation model and audio tagging model (foundation knowledge; names n/c)
mechanism: Decouples 'segment all objects' from 'decide which sound'; audio-tag semantics matched to instance categories
objective: Silent-object-aware segmentation objective (L_cls + L_ins) in stage 1; integration rules in stage 2
robustness_tests: Test audio mixed with white noise, and with off-screen sounds, on AVSS (Table III); BAVS degrades 33.59->30.51 / 33.52 vs TPAVI 29.77->23.59 / 23.56
limitations: Relies on external foundation models and audio tagging (closed label space); integration step is rule-based (our reading)

title: Prompting Segmentation with Sound Is Generalizable Audio-Visual Source Localizer
authors: Yaoting Wang, Weisong Liu, Guangyao Li et al.
architecture: GAVS: SAM (ViT-B) with audio as prompt (encoder-prompt-decoder), semantic-aware audio prompt (SAP), visual adapters and correlation adapters (ColA); VGGish audio
mechanism: Audio embedding converted to sparse/semantic prompt tokens for SAM's mask decoder instead of fusing audio into visual features
objective: Supervised mask loss on AVSBench
robustness_tests: Unseen-class generalisation (AVS-V3 0/1/3/5-shot) and cross-dataset zero-shot to VGG-SS
limitations: Authors acknowledge deficiencies on V1S; Ref-AVS paper reports GAVS+text Null S 0.190 (cross-paper)

title: Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation
authors: Ruohao Guo, Xianghua Ying, Yaru Chen et al.
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; long-horizon drift
architecture: AVISM: query-based (Mask2Former-VIS-style) model with frame-level audio-visual fusion sound source localizer and video-level sounding object tracker (window attention); ResNet-50 / R-101 / Swin-L
mechanism: Frame-level and video-level audio-visual fusion modules; instance queries tracked across frames, keeping only sounding instances
objective: Instance mask/class losses + similarity loss for tracking
robustness_tests: Silent-frame accuracy FSLAn (VIS baselines Mask2Former-VIS/TeViT score 0.00); zero-shot MLLM baselines on audio-referred grounding (Table 3: AL-Ref-SAM 2 FSLA 18.55)
limitations: Small dataset (926 videos); silent-frame accuracy still low (32.22)

title: TSAM: Temporal SAM Augmented with Multimodal Prompts for Referring Audio-Visual Segmentation
authors: Abduljalil Radman, Jorma Laaksonen
architecture: SAM ViT-B with a temporal branch (4 blocks) and multimodal prompts built from text and selected audio queries (k=5)
mechanism: Audio and text cues converted into sparse/dense prompts for SAM; temporal branch propagates information across frames
objective: Supervised mask loss on Ref-AVS; best validation checkpoint selected
robustness_tests: Ref-AVS Null split (S 0.017, vs EEMC 0.007)
limitations: Null S worse than EEMC despite higher J/F (our reading)

title: Unified Multisensory Perception: Weakly-Supervised Audio-Visual Video Parsing
authors: Yapeng Tian, Dingzeyu Li, Chenliang Xu
task: audio-visual video parsing (AVVP; temporal AV grounding)
architecture: Hybrid Attention Network (HAN: self- and cross-modal attention over audio and visual segment features) with attentive MMIL pooling
mechanism: Per-segment audio and visual event predictions; attentive multimodal multiple-instance pooling aggregates to video-level labels
objective: Weak video-level labels: MMIL loss (L_wsl) plus guided loss (L_g) per Table 2; label smoothing for modality-specific label noise
robustness_tests: Task separates audio-only, visual-only and audio-visual events, so modality mismatch (audible-not-visible and vice versa) is evaluated by construction; noisy modality-specific labels handled by label smoothing
limitations: Video-level weak labels only for training; 10 s clips

title: Positive Sample Propagation along the Audio-Visual Event Line
authors: Jinxing Zhou, Liang Zheng, Yiran Zhong et al.
architecture: VGG-19 (ImageNet) visual features + audio features; positive sample propagation (PSP) module over audio-visual segment pairs
mechanism: Builds an all-pair audio-visual similarity graph and prunes negative/weak connections (threshold tau), aggregating only positive pairs
objective: Cross-entropy on segment labels plus audio-visual pair similarity loss (fully supervised) or weighting branch (weakly supervised)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Single-event 10 s clips (AVE design)

title: Towards Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization
authors: Jinxing Zhou, Dan Guo, Ruohao Guo et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: ImageBind audio/visual/text features; training-free baseline compares cross-modal consistency; fine-tuning baseline adds a temporal layer
mechanism: Event class names as text queries in a shared embedding space; an explicit 'other' text class absorbs background segments
objective: Training-free inference or supervised fine-tuning on seen classes
robustness_tests: Seen vs unseen event classes; closed-set AVE methods (PSP, MM-Pyramid) collapse on unseen classes (accuracy 33.7-44.6); ablation of the background 'other' class (Table 3)
limitations: Linear-layer fine-tuning overfits seen classes (unseen acc 34.8, Table 5)

title: LongVALE: Vision-Audio-Language-Event Benchmark Towards Time-Aware Omni-Modal Perception of Long Videos
authors: Tiantian Geng, Jinrui Zhang, Qingni Wang et al.
task: omni-modal temporal video grounding (Omni-TVG), dense captioning
architecture: LongVALE-LLM (7B): frame CLS features (100 frames), BEATs audio encoder, Whisper-Large-v2 speech encoder, LLM with boundary-perception and instruction-tuning stages
mechanism: Omni-modal (vision+audio+speech) tokens with timestamps emitted as text
objective: Two-stage training: boundary perception then instruction tuning on LongVALE
robustness_tests: Modality ablation (V vs V+A vs V+S vs V+A+S; Table 6)
limitations: Absolute grounding accuracy on long omni-modal videos remains very low (R@0.7 3.9)

title: Text-to-Audio Grounding: Building Correspondence Between Captions and Sound Events
authors: Xuenan Xu, Heinrich Dinkel, Mengyue Wu et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Separate audio encoder (frame embeddings) and phrase query encoder (word embeddings)
mechanism: Frame-wise similarity s_t = exp(-||e_{A,t} - e_P||_2) between audio frames and the phrase embedding, thresholded into onsets/offsets
objective: Frame-level binary cross-entropy against phrase-level sound-event timestamps
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Small validation/test sets (31/70 clips); only phrases that occur in captions are grounded (every query has a target, our reading)

title: Investigating Pooling Strategies and Loss Functions for Weakly-Supervised Text-to-Audio Grounding via Contrastive Learning
authors: Xuenan Xu, Mengyue Wu, Kai Yu
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Audio-text dual encoder trained contrastively on clip-caption pairs (details n/c)
mechanism: Frame-level audio-text similarity pooled to clip level; study of pooling strategies (e.g. mean vs max) and contrastive loss functions
objective: Clip-caption contrastive learning (weak supervision, no timestamps)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Not read in full this session

title: Towards Weakly Supervised Text-to-Audio Grounding
authors: Xuenan Xu, Ziyang Ma, Mengyue Wu et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: CRNN audio encoder (8 CNN layers, CNN10-like with 4x temporal downsampling, BiGRU; AudioSet-pretrained) and a word-embedding + mean-pooling phrase encoder; CLAP phrase embeddings used for negative sampling
foundation_models: AudioSet-pretrained CRNN; CLAP (PANNs CNN14 + BERT-medium) for phrase-embedding sampling
mechanism: Sentence-level WSTAG with audio max-pooling; phrase-level WSTAG with similarity- or clustering-based negative phrase sampling and self-supervised pseudo strong labels
objective: Clip-level audio-phrase matching (contrastive/BCE) without frame-level labels, plus self-supervision
robustness_tests: Separate evaluation on short events ('Short' subset) where mean pooling collapses (PSDS 5.5)
limitations: Strongly supervised TAG (CRNN-QGCA, PSDS 62.8) still better; no evaluation with queries for absent sounds (our reading)

title: Language-based Audio Moment Retrieval
authors: Hokuto Munakata, Taichi Nishimura, Shota Nakada et al.
task: audio moment retrieval (text-to-audio temporal grounding in long audio)
architecture: AM-DETR: frame-level audio features (CLAP or VR extractor) fed to a DETR-style moment decoder conditioned on the text query
mechanism: Moment queries attend to text-conditioned audio features to predict (start, end) spans in untrimmed audio, as in video moment retrieval
objective: DETR-style moment prediction losses with optional audio-text contrastive learning (loss details n/c)
robustness_tests: Transfer from simulated training data to real recordings (UnAV-100 subset, TUT 2017), where accuracy drops sharply
limitations: Trained on simulated mixtures; poor transfer to TUT real recordings (R1@0.5 14.42)

title: Detect Any Sound: Open-Vocabulary Sound Event Detection with Multi-Modal Queries
authors: Pengfei Cai, Yan Song, Qing Gu et al.
task: open-vocabulary sound event detection with text or audio queries (text-to-audio grounding)
architecture: DASM: HTS-AT or PaSST audio encoder; query generation module for text (CLAP-style) or audio queries; dual-stream decoder (cross-modality event decoder + context network)
foundation_models: HTS-AT / PaSST; CLAP-style text encoder (n/c which)
mechanism: Event queries derived from text or audio examples attend to frame features to output frame-level presence for each queried class
objective: Frame-level detection loss with clip-level loss and clip-level prior; trained with partial labels (rare classes removed) for open-vocabulary setting
robustness_tests: Novel-class detection (PSDS_r) and cross-dataset zero-shot (DESED); Table 4 shows novel-class PSDS_r collapses from 30.1 to 4.6 when base classes are not visible at inference
limitations: Novel-class detection depends on base classes being present among queries at inference (inference-time masking)

title: ScanRefer: 3D Object Localization in RGB-D Scans Using Natural Language
authors: Dave Zhenyu Chen, Angel X. Chang, Matthias Nießner
architecture: VoteNet (PointNet++) proposal module + GloVe/GRU language encoder + fusion module scoring proposals
mechanism: sentence embedding fused with each 3D object proposal feature; localisation head selects the best-matching proposal
objective: proposal localisation (cross-entropy on proposal with highest IoU) + detection loss + language object-classification loss
robustness_tests: unique vs multiple (same-class distractor) split; oracle analysis with GT boxes (OracleRefer, OracleCatRand) separating detection from grounding errors; feature ablation (xyz/rgb/normals/multiview)
limitations: two-stage: grounding is capped by VoteNet proposal quality (VoteNetBest upper bound in Table 6); large gap on the 'multiple' subset; one target per description, no zero-target case (our reading)

title: ReferIt3D: Neural Listeners for Fine-Grained 3D Object Identification in Real-World Scenes
authors: Panos Achlioptas, Ahmed Abdelreheem, Fei Xia, et al.
architecture: PointNet++ object encoder + RNN utterance encoder + dynamic graph convolution (DGCN) over objects; language fused before and after the graph
mechanism: multi-modal neural listener: object-to-object graph reasoning conditioned on the utterance, then softmax over segmented scene objects
objective: cross-entropy over candidate objects + auxiliary object-class and utterance target-class classification losses
robustness_tests: every utterance has >=1 same-class distractor; easy/hard (number of distractors) and view-dependent/view-independent breakdowns; human listener accuracy as reference; training with Sr3D/Sr3D+ augmentation
limitations: assumes ground-truth object segmentation (identification, not detection); Sr3D language is template-based; view-dependent utterances remain hardest (our reading)

title: Refer-it-in-RGBD: A Bottom-up Approach for 3D Visual Grounding in RGBD Images
authors: Haolin Liu, Anran Lin, Xiaoguang Han, et al.
architecture: RGB-D frame lifted to a partial point cloud; voxel-level language-conditioned heatmap; weighted FPS proposal generation; object-level matching and box refinement
mechanism: bottom-up early language-visual fusion yields a 3D relevance heatmap that guides adaptive proposal sampling, then proposal-text matching
objective: supervised heatmap + proposal matching + box regression losses
robustness_tests: partial, occluded single-view geometry is the task setting; modality ablation (image-only vs point-cloud-only branches)
limitations: single-view RGB-D observes only partial geometry; single-RGBD numbers are not comparable with whole-scene ScanRefer (our reading)

title: 3DVG-Transformer: Relation Modeling for Visual Grounding on Point Clouds
authors: Lichen Zhao, Daigang Cai, Lu Sheng, et al.
architecture: VoteNet-style proposal generation with coordinate-guided contextual aggregation (CCA) + multiplex attention (MA) fusion transformer
mechanism: relation-aware proposal features (coordinate-guided attention among proposals) cross-attended with language in multiplex attention
objective: ScanRefer-style localisation + detection + language classification losses
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split; Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdowns
limitations: proposal-based ceiling; little gain on view-dependent Nr3D/Sr3D utterances (Table 2) (our reading)

title: Bottom Up Top Down Detection Transformers for Language Grounding in Images and Point Clouds
authors: Ayush Jain, Nikolaos Gkanatsios, Ishita Mediratta, et al.
architecture: PointNet++ (3D) / ResNet-101 (2D) visual encoder + RoBERTa text encoder + detector-box stream; DETR-style decoder with non-parametric queries
foundation_models: RoBERTa, Group-Free 3D detector, Faster R-CNN (2D), ResNet-101
mechanism: joint attention over visual tokens, utterance tokens and bottom-up detected boxes; top-down decoding of boxes rather than selecting a proposal
objective: box regression + span-prediction/contrastive alignment of boxes to utterance spans; detection cast as grounding of label prompts
robustness_tests: evaluates Nr3D/Sr3D with detected boxes (no GT-box oracle) as well as GT boxes; ScanRefer unique/multiple and Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard, view-dependent/independent breakdowns
limitations: always outputs a box (no explicit no-target handling); view-dependent accuracy lags view-independent (Tables 6-7) (our reading)

title: ViewRefer: Grasp the Multi-view Knowledge for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Zoey Guo, Yiwen Tang, Ray Zhang, et al.
architecture: multi-view (rotated) 3D object encoder + BERT text encoder; fusion transformer with intra-view, inter-view and cross-modal attention; learnable multi-view prototypes
mechanism: LLM-expanded view-consistent descriptions; inter-view attention across rotated scene views; prototype-guided text context and view-guided scoring of logits
objective: cross-entropy over proposals + 3D and text classification losses (weighted 0.5 each)
robustness_tests: targets view-dependence: reports view-dependent vs view-independent and easy/hard breakdowns on Nr3D/Sr3D; ScanRefer multiple (distractor) subset
limitations: view-dependent Sr3D accuracy (52.2) stays far below view-independent (67.7) and below MVT (58.4) (our reading of Table 1); depends on proposal quality

title: 3D-VisTA: Pre-trained Transformer for 3D Vision and Text Alignment
authors: Ziyu Zhu, Xiaojian Ma, Yixin Chen, et al.
architecture: BERT-style text encoder + PointNet++ object encoder + spatial-aware self-attention fusion transformer (no task-specific modules)
foundation_models: BERT (text encoder initialisation), PointNet++, Mask3D/PointGroup (proposals), GPT-3 (pre-training text generation)
mechanism: plain self-attention over concatenated object and word tokens; grounding head scores each object token
objective: pre-training: masked language modelling, masked object modelling, scene-text matching; fine-tuning: proposal classification
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple; Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/independent; detector swap (PointGroup vs Mask3D) shows sensitivity to proposals; data-efficiency with limited fine-tuning annotations
limitations: gains largely come from better proposals (Mask3D) and pre-training text derived from ScanNet-based datasets (our reading); no zero-target handling

title: Multi3DRefer: Grounding Text Description to Multiple 3D Objects
authors: Yiming Zhang, ZeMing Gong, Angel X. Chang
architecture: PointGroup detector + CLIP text encoder + CLIP image encoder on online-rendered proposal views + transformer fusion; per-proposal match scores thresholded
mechanism: fuses 3D proposal features with CLIP features of rendered views; at inference all proposals with score above a threshold tau_pred are returned, so the output set may be empty
objective: detection loss + reference loss on proposal scores (positives assigned by IoU threshold or Hungarian matching) + sentence-object contrastive loss
robustness_tests: five-way breakdown: zero-target without/with same-class distractors, single-target without/with distractors, multiple targets; GT-box vs predicted-box evaluation; F1 penalises both missing and spurious objects
limitations: zero-target with distractors remains low with GT boxes (F1 29.4, Table 8); descriptions partly ChatGPT-rephrased; F1@0.25 not reported in the paper (our reading)

title: EmbodiedScan: A Holistic Multi-Modal 3D Perception Suite Towards Embodied AI
authors: Tai Wang, Xiaohan Mao, Chenming Zhu, et al.
architecture: Embodied Perceptron: 2D/3D encoders over an arbitrary number of RGB-D views, dense fusion, sparse DETR-style decoder; text-conditioned grounding head
mechanism: multi-view ego-centric RGB-D features fused into a 3D representation; language-conditioned sparse decoder predicts oriented 3D boxes
objective: supervised oriented-box regression and classification on EmbodiedScan annotations
robustness_tests: grounding benchmark split into easy/hard (distractors) and view-dependent/independent queries (Table 5); real vs rendered images ablation
limitations: grounding AP25 is low overall (25.72 for the baseline, Table 5), showing the difficulty of ego-centric grounding (our reading)

title: SceneVerse: Scaling 3D Vision-Language Learning for Grounded Scene Understanding
authors: Baoxiong Jia, Yixin Chen, Huangyue Yu, et al.
architecture: Grounded Pre-training for Scenes (GPS): PointNet++ object encoder + spatial-attention transformer + language encoder, multi-level contrastive alignment
foundation_models: PointNet++, Mask3D (proposals), LLM for description rephrasing
mechanism: object-, scene- and referral-level contrastive alignment between object/scene features and text; grounding by scoring object tokens
objective: multi-level contrastive pre-training + masked language modelling; fine-tuning with proposal classification
robustness_tests: zero-shot transfer to ScanRefer/Nr3D/Sr3D and to held-out SceneVerse-val (Tables 3-4); unique/multiple, easy/hard and view-dependent breakdowns; human vs generated data ablation
limitations: most language is generated from scene graphs or rephrased by an LLM, so template/generation bias is possible (our reading); zero-shot ScanRefer still well below fine-tuned

title: LLM-Grounder: Open-Vocabulary 3D Visual Grounding with Large Language Model as an Agent
authors: Jianing Yang, Xuweiyi Chen, Shengyi Qian, et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: GPT-4 (or GPT-3.5) agent that parses the query and calls an open-vocabulary 3D grounder (OpenScene or LERF) for target and landmark candidates, then reasons over their spatial properties
