mechanism: LLM decomposes the query into target/landmark noun phrases, queries a visual grounding tool, and selects candidates using box volumes and distances in its reasoning
objective: none (training-free)
robustness_tests: visual-difficulty split: low (no same-class distractor, 232 queries) vs high (>1 distractor, 766 queries) (Table II); GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 agent
limitations: absolute accuracy is low and Acc@0.5 barely improves over the tool; agent gains shrink with distractors; inherits tool errors (stated and our reading)

title: 3D-LLM: Injecting the 3D World into Large Language Models
authors: Yining Hong, Haoyu Zhen, Peihao Chen, et al.
architecture: 3D feature extractor lifting multi-view 2D features to 3D points + 2D VLM backbone (BLIP-2 / Flamingo) + 3D localisation mechanism (position embeddings and location tokens)
mechanism: 3D point features fed as visual tokens to a 2D VLM; locations expressed as discretised location tokens in the text output
objective: language modelling on LLM-generated 3D-language instruction data
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: grounding accuracy well below specialist 3D-VG models (Table 5); relies on rendered/multi-view features (our reading)

title: LERF: Language Embedded Radiance Fields
authors: Justin Kerr, Chung Min Kim, Ken Goldberg, et al.
architecture: NeRF (Nerfacto) with a multi-scale language field and DINO feature field; CLIP image features of multi-scale crops as targets
mechanism: volume-rendered CLIP embeddings along rays at a chosen physical scale; relevancy = similarity to the query vs canonical negative phrases
objective: per-scene distillation of multi-scale CLIP crop embeddings (and DINO features) into the field
robustness_tests: existence determination: precision-recall over relevancy thresholds with long-tail positive and negative (absent) labels (Sec. 4.2, Fig. 8)
limitations: CLIP bag-of-words behaviour; relevancy is a similarity score, not a calibrated presence probability; per-scene optimisation (stated limitations and our reading)

title: LangSplat: 3D Language Gaussian Splatting
authors: Minghan Qin, Wanhua Li, Jiawei Zhou, et al.
architecture: 3D Gaussian Splatting with per-Gaussian low-dimensional language features from a scene-wise autoencoder; SAM-derived hierarchical (subpart/part/whole) semantics
mechanism: tile-based splatting of language features; query by CLIP text similarity on decoded features at three SAM granularity levels
objective: per-scene distillation of CLIP features of SAM masks into Gaussians (autoencoder latent space)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: category-level open-vocabulary querying, not referring expressions with relations; per-scene optimisation (our reading)

title: ReferSplat: Referring Segmentation in 3D Gaussian Splatting
authors: Shuting He, Guangquan Jie, Changshuo Wang, et al.
architecture: 3DGS scene (LangSplat-style RGB training) + per-Gaussian referring features; position-aware cross-modal interaction with BERT sentence/word features
mechanism: Gaussian-text similarity with position-aware cross-modal interaction; rendered referring masks in novel views
objective: rendered-mask supervision from pseudo masks + Gaussian-text contrastive learning
robustness_tests: queried targets may be occluded or not visible in the rendered novel view (task setting); language-encoder ablation (BERT vs CLIP)
limitations: per-scene training; small benchmark (Ref-LERF); no absent-target queries (our reading)

title: Mono3DVG: 3D Visual Grounding in Monocular Images
authors: Yang Zhan, Yuan Yuan, Zhitong Xiong
architecture: Mono3DVG-TR: visual encoder + depth predictor/encoder + RoBERTa-style text encoder, dual text-guided adapter, depth-text-visual stacking-attention decoder
mechanism: text-guided adapters refine visual and depth features; decoder queries attend to depth, text and multi-scale visual features to regress a 3D box
objective: supervised 2D/3D box, depth and dimension regression losses
robustness_tests: unique/multiple (distractor) split, near/medium/far distance and easy/moderate/hard (occlusion/truncation) subsets (Table 4)
limitations: depth estimated from a single image; descriptions partly LLM-generated (our reading)

title: SpatialVLM: Endowing Vision-Language Models with Spatial Reasoning Capabilities
authors: Boyuan Chen, Zhuo Xu, Sean Kirmani, et al.
architecture: PaLM-E architecture with PaLM 2-S language backbone; trained on a mix of PaLM-E data and synthetic spatial VQA
foundation_models: PaLM 2-S, PaLM-E recipe, CLIP (image filtering), off-the-shelf segmentation, metric-depth and captioning experts
mechanism: internet images lifted to metric 3D point clouds by expert models; templated spatial QA about object pairs; VLM answers in text
objective: next-token prediction on 2B synthetic spatial VQA examples (5% of training tokens) mixed with PaLM-E data
robustness_tests: training with injected Gaussian noise in the synthetic 3D labels (Table 5); frozen vs unfrozen ViT
limitations: metric answers depend on the accuracy of the automatic 3D lifting; answers are text, not grounded boxes (our reading)

title: SpatialRGPT: Grounded Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
authors: An-Chieh Cheng, Hongxu Yin, Yang Fu, et al.
architecture: VLM with visual encoder + region-feature extractor + plug-in relative-depth branch + linear connectors + LLaMA2-7B
foundation_models: LLaMA2-7B, Llama3-70B (data generation), Metric3Dv2 (metric depth), open-vocabulary detection/segmentation models
mechanism: user-specified region masks/boxes pooled into region tokens; depth features injected into region embeddings; answers distances/directions in text
objective: instruction tuning on template and LLM-generated spatial QA built from single-image 3D scene graphs
robustness_tests: input-modality ablation (with/without depth); axis-aligned vs oriented boxes; augmented benchmark
limitations: spatial labels come from monocular metric-depth estimation; axis-aligned boxes approximate object extent (stated in ablations and our reading)

title: SeeGround: See and Ground for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Rong Li, Shijie Li, Lingdong Kong, et al.
architecture: 3D scene rendered into query-aligned 2D views + text object table (Mask3D boxes) fed to a 2D VLM (Qwen2-VL-72B); depth-aware visual prompts
mechanism: Perspective Adaptation Module chooses a query-driven viewpoint; Fusion Alignment Module marks objects in the rendered image and aligns them with the 3D object table; VLM selects the object ID
objective: none (training-free)
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple and Nr3D easy/hard, view-dependent/independent breakdowns; viewpoint-selection strategies (Table 4); detector swap incl. GT boxes (Table 10); robustness to incomplete text queries
limitations: depends on 3D detector proposals (59.5 with GT boxes vs 44.1 with Mask3D, Table 10) and on the 2D VLM; no absent-target handling (our reading)

title: VLM-Grounder: A VLM Agent for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Runsen Xu, Zhiwei Huang, Tai Wang, et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: GPT-4V agent over dynamically stitched frame grids; 2D open-vocabulary detector + SAM; multi-view ensemble projection with PATS feature matching to estimate the 3D box
mechanism: query analysis, view pre-selection and stitching, VLM grounding with feedback/retry on invalid predictions, ID visual prompts, then multi-view back-projection to 3D
objective: none (training-free)
robustness_tests: feedback loop re-grounds after invalid predictions; unique/multiple and easy/hard, view-dependent/independent breakdowns; 2D-detector ablation; error analysis
limitations: evaluated on 250-sample subsets for cost; depth/field-of-view errors in back-projection; API cost and latency (stated limitations)

title: Video-3D LLM: Learning Position-Aware Video Representation for 3D Scene Understanding
authors: Duo Zheng, Shijia Huang, Liwei Wang
architecture: video MLLM (LLaVA-Video 7B on Qwen2-7B) with sinusoidal 3D position encodings of back-projected patch coordinates; maximum-coverage frame sampling
mechanism: hidden state of a <ground> token is matched (InfoNCE) to object features pooled from visual patches inside each proposal plus centre-coordinate encoding
objective: instruction tuning on 3D-VL tasks; InfoNCE grounding loss between <ground> token and GT object features
robustness_tests: none reported (frame-number and sampling ablations only)
limitations: grounding is proposal selection over Mask3D boxes, so detector misses cap accuracy; no zero-target breakdown reported (our reading)

title: InstanceRefer: Cooperative Holistic Understanding for Visual Grounding on Point Clouds through Instance Multi-level Contextual Referring
authors: Zhihao Yuan, Xu Yan, Yinghong Liao, et al.
architecture: Frozen PointGroup panoptic segmentation -> instance point-cloud candidates filtered by language-predicted target class; GloVe+BiGRU text encoder; attribute (AP), relation (RP) and global-localization (GLP) perception modules + matching module
mechanism: grounding-by-matching: language-guided multi-level (attribute, local relation, global localisation) instance features ranked by cosine similarity with sentence feature
objective: matching (cross-entropy over instance candidates) + language target-class classification loss
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split (val + online test); Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdown (view-dependence breakdown); same-backbone and GT-instance oracle comparisons (Table 4)
limitations: Relies on a frozen PointGroup segmenter and language-predicted target class to filter candidates, so segmentation/classification errors are unrecoverable; gains concentrated on 'unique' (Acc@0.5 66.83) vs 'multiple' (24.77); large gap to GT instances (49.20 Acc@0.5, Table 4) (our reading)

title: SAT: 2D Semantics Assisted Training for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Zhengyuan Yang, Songyang Zhang, Liwei Wang, et al.
architecture: PointNet++ proposal encoder (GT segments on ReferIt3D, VoteNet proposals on ScanRefer) + BERT (first 3 layers) text encoder + multimodal fusion transformer; 2D semantics (Faster R-CNN ROI feature, class, 2D box + camera pose) from ScanNet frames as extra tokens in TRAINING ONLY
foundation_models: BERT (first 3 layers); Faster R-CNN pre-trained on Visual Genome (2D semantics, train-only); PointNet++
mechanism: 2D semantics tokens fused in the transformer during training with an attention mask that prevents language/3D tokens from attending to them; inference uses only point cloud + text
objective: 3D grounding softmax loss + 2D grounding loss + 3D-2D object correspondence (triplet) loss + object/text classification losses
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split (detected proposals); Nr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdown (view-dependence breakdown); Nr3D accuracy vs. number of same-class distractors (2-6), query length, target class and spatial keywords (Tables 9-12); comparison with oracles using 2D at test time (Table 7)
limitations: Needs aligned 2D image semantics (ScanNet frames, camera poses, 2D detector) at training time; main results use GT proposals; authors note detected-proposal quality bounds ScanRefer accuracy (Sec. B.3)

title: Multi-View Transformer for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Shijia Huang, Yilun Chen, Jiaya Jia, et al.
architecture: PointNet++ object encoder shared across views; object position encodings for N rotated views of the scene; BERT (first 3 layers) text encoder; multi-modal transformer decoder; multi-view feature aggregation
mechanism: projects the 3D scene into multiple rotated views, fuses language with view-specific object features and aggregates across views for view-robust ranking
objective: grounding cross-entropy + auxiliary object classification (via category text features) + text target-class classification losses
robustness_tests: Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdown (view-dependence breakdown); ScanRefer unique/multiple split; sensitivity to number of train/test views (Table 5)
limitations: Multi-view is obtained by rotating object coordinates (no images); proposal-based, so ScanRefer accuracy is bounded by the PointGroup detector and the gain there is small (33.26 vs 32.93 Acc@0.5 for InstanceRefer) (our reading)

title: 3D-SPS: Single-Stage 3D Visual Grounding via Referred Point Progressive Selection
authors: Junyu Luo, Jiahui Fu, Xianghao Kong, et al.
architecture: PointNet++ seed points + CLIP text encoder; Description-aware Keypoint Sampling (DKS) then Target-oriented Progressive Mining (TPM) transformer layers progressively selecting language-relevant keypoints (512->32); box regression from final keypoints
mechanism: language-guided progressive selection of referred keypoints with cross-modal attention, avoiding a separate detect-then-match stage
objective: referring-confidence loss on selected keypoints + DKS keypoint supervision (in-box / mentioned-category points) + auxiliary detection loss (GroupFree/VoteNet-style) + language target-class loss
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split; Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdown (view-dependence breakdown)
limitations: Authors: view-dependent descriptions and ambiguous queries still confuse the model. Nr3D/Sr3D results use a modified two-stage-style variant with SAT 2D-assisted training, so they are not single-stage (our reading)

title: 3DJCG: A Unified Framework for Joint Dense Captioning and Visual Grounding on 3D Point Clouds
authors: Daigang Cai, Lichen Zhao, Jing Zhang, et al.
architecture: Shared task-agnostic VoteNet detector + attribute & relation aware feature-enhancement transformer; lightweight task-specific heads: 1-layer multi-head cross-attention grounding head (GloVe+GRU language) and captioning head
foundation_models: GloVe; VoteNet/PointNet++; ENet multiview image features in the '2D+3D' setting
mechanism: object proposals (queries) cross-attend to word features; captioning and grounding act as proxy tasks for each other through shared modules
objective: detection loss + 0.3 grounding (localisation + language object classification) + 0.2 captioning cross-entropy (captioning loss added in last 50 epochs)
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split (val + online test)
limitations: Authors: the improvement from joint training is much smaller for visual grounding than for dense captioning; VoteNet proposals bound accuracy (our reading)

title: D3Net: A Unified Speaker-Listener Architecture for 3D Dense Captioning and Visual Grounding
authors: Dave Zhenyu Chen, Qirui Wu, Matthias Nießner, et al.
architecture: PointGroup detector (sparse-conv U-Net, multiview ENet features) -> speaker (dense captioning module) and listener (GRU language encoder + transformer fusion as in 3DVG-Transformer) trained end-to-end
mechanism: self-critical speaker-listener loop: the listener grounds the speaker's generated captions and its localisation/classification reward makes captions discriminative; enables training on scans without descriptions
objective: detection + MLE captioning, then self-critical training with CIDEr + listener (localisation + object-class) rewards; listener grounding loss; semi-supervised on unannotated scans
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split (val + online test); grounding with GT vs VoteNet vs PointGroup detections (Table 3); listener-based discriminability of generated captions (Table 4)
limitations: Only Acc@0.5 reported for grounding; relies on multiview image features and PointGroup detection; Nr3D grounding uses a detection-based protocol not comparable with ReferIt3D GT-box accuracy (our reading)

title: Language Conditioned Spatial Relation Reasoning for 3D Object Grounding
authors: Shizhe Chen, Pierre-Louis Guhur, Makarand Tapaswi, et al.
architecture: BERT (3 layers) text encoder; PointNet++ object encoder (pre-trained on ScanNet object classification, frozen) + color GMM embedding; multimodal transformer with language-conditioned spatial self-attention (pairwise distance + orientation); teacher-student distillation
foundation_models: BERT (first 3 layers); PointNet++ (pre-trained, frozen); GloVe (class-label embeddings for teacher)
mechanism: spatial self-attention whose pairwise distance/orientation features are weighted by language-conditioned gates and merged with standard attention via sigsoftmax; teacher with GT class labels distils relation reasoning into the point-cloud student
objective: grounding cross-entropy + sentence target-class and per-object class cross-entropy; student adds distillation of attention and hidden states (L_attn + L_hidden) from teacher to student
robustness_tests: Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdown (view-dependence breakdown); ScanRefer unique/multiple split; variance over 5 random seeds (Table 11); PointGroup upper bound on ScanRefer (Table 8)
limitations: Teacher requires GT object class labels; proposal-based, so ScanRefer accuracy is bounded by PointGroup (upper bound 62.98 Acc@0.5, Table 8) (our reading)

title: EDA: Explicit Text-Decoupling and Dense Alignment for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Yanmin Wu, Xinhua Cheng, Renrui Zhang, et al.
architecture: BUTD-DETR-style encoder-decoder: PointNet++ visual tokens, RoBERTa text tokens, optional GroupFree box tokens; cross-encoder + DETR-like object decoder; dependency-parse text decoupling into main object, attributes, pronoun, auxiliary object, relation
foundation_models: RoBERTa-base (frozen); PointNet++ (pre-trained on ScanNet); GroupFree 3D detector
mechanism: dense position + semantic alignment between object queries and decoupled text components (not just the object name), removing need for GT target-name labels
objective: DETR-style box losses + position alignment (L_pos) + semantic contrastive alignment (L_sem) to decoupled text components
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split; Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/view-independent breakdown (supp. Table 8; view-dependence breakdown); new VG-w/o-ON test: object names replaced by 'object' on ScanRefer val (Table 5); evaluation with GT boxes (supp. Table 7); re-evaluation of BUTD-DETR without GT text labels on full Nr3D
limitations: Authors: bottlenecks of PointNet++, RoBERTa and the text parser; text decoupling may fail on long sentences; failures from referential ambiguity

title: Four Ways to Improve Verbo-visual Fusion for Dense 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Ozan Unal, Christos Sakaridis, Suman Saha, et al.
architecture: Sparse-conv UNet kernel-based instance segmenter producing instance kernels/masks; MPNet word encoder; bottom-up attentive fusion transformer (spherical masking that grows across layers) with learned global camera token
mechanism: localised bottom-up verbo-visual attention over instance kernels, contrastive separation of same-class instances, camera token supervised with annotation viewpoint for view-dependent utterances, multi-view (yaw-rotation) ensembling with IoU-consensus mask selection
objective: instance segmentation losses + grounding cross-entropy + contrastive loss + L2 camera-position loss
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split (val + online test); camera-token ablation for view-dependent utterances (Table 5); mask-IoU-based evaluation (Table 8)
limitations: Authors: GCT requires ground-truth annotation camera positions; MVE requires multiple forward passes of encoder and decoder (runtime/memory cost)

title: 3D-GRES: Generalized 3D Referring Expression Segmentation
authors: Changli Wu, Yihang Liu, Jiayi Ji, et al.
architecture: Sparse 3D U-Net point features pooled to superpoints; RoBERTa text encoder; MDIN: 6 stacked Query-Superpoint Aggregation + Query-Language Aggregation layers; per-query mask head + per-query target-confidence head
mechanism: Text-driven Sparse Queries: farthest-superpoint-sampled seed queries filtered by text correlation; queries attend to superpoints and words; each query yields a mask and a binary target confidence; the union of positive queries is the 0..N-object mask (all-negative = no target)
objective: Multi-object Decoupling Optimization: per-instance decoupled BCE+Dice mask loss, target-confidence decoupling loss, query-generation decoupling loss, query-text alignment loss
robustness_tests: Multi3DRes five-way breakdown (zero target w/ and w/o same-class distractors, single target w/ and w/o distractors, multiple targets); ScanRefer unique/multiple split; Nr3D/Sr3D easy/hard and view-dependent/independent breakdown (mask evaluation without GT boxes, appendix Table 5)
limitations: Single target with distractors (Acc@0.5 29.5) and zero target with distractors (47.9) remain the weakest subsets (our reading); for zero-target samples IoU is set to 1/0 from query confidences, so mIoU mixes absence detection with mask quality (our reading); Multi3DRes inherits Multi3DRefer's partly ChatGPT-rephrased descriptions (our reading); no sensor-noise or cross-dataset tests (our reading)

title: 3D-STMN: Dependency-Driven Superpoint-Text Matching Network for End-to-End 3D Referring Expression Segmentation
authors: Changli Wu, Yiwei Ma, Qi Chen, et al.
architecture: Sparse 3D U-Net point features pooled to superpoints; BERT word encoder; Dependency-Driven Interaction (graph over Stanford CoreNLP dependency trees); stacked Superpoint-Word Aggregation transformer layers; mask from a word-token kernel
mechanism: Superpoint-text matching: text-guided sampling of description-relevant superpoints, then words cross-attend to superpoints (attention masked by the predicted mask); the mask is the response map of the most visually correlated word embedding against superpoint features
objective: superpoint-level BCE + Dice mask losses + auxiliary mask-score loss
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique (~19%) / multiple (~81%) split; inference-time comparison against two-stage TGNN (283 ms vs 27,097 ms, ~95.7x)
limitations: Single-target formulation only: it cannot return zero or several objects (addressed by the follow-up 3D-GRES/MDIN) (our reading); there is a large unique-vs-multiple gap (mIoU 74.5 vs 31.1), so same-class distractors remain the main failure (our reading); it depends on an external dependency parser (our reading)

title: Chat-Scene: Bridging 3D Scene and Large Language Models with Object Identifiers
authors: Haifeng Huang, Yilun Chen, Zehan Wang, et al.
task: 3D-VG and multi-object 3D-VG via a 3D-LLM (plus 3D captioning and QA)
architecture: Mask3D proposals -> per-object Uni3D 3D features + DINOv2 multi-view 2D features, each through a 3-layer MLP projector; learnable object-identifier tokens interleaved with object tokens; Vicuna-7B-v1.5 LLM fine-tuned with LoRA
foundation_models: Mask3D, Uni3D, DINOv2, Vicuna-7B-v1.5 (LLaMA 2); DEVA (video-input variant)
mechanism: scene given to the LLM as a sequence of <identifier, 3D token, 2D token> per proposal; the model grounds by generating the identifier token(s) of the referred object(s), which map back to proposal masks/boxes
objective: single-stage joint instruction tuning with the LM cross-entropy loss only (no task heads)
robustness_tests: ScanRefer unique/multiple split; Multi3DRefer five-way breakdown (zero target w/ and w/o distractors, single target w/ and w/o distractors, multiple targets); video-only input (no depth/point cloud, DEVA proposals) variant; ablations on identifier type and 2D/3D feature fusion
limitations: Authors: relies on frozen pre-trained detectors and 2D/3D encoders whose errors propagate; 3D-language data scarcity; misclassifies under-represented classes (e.g. hair dryer, soap dish). Our reading: grounding can only select among Mask3D proposals; abstention is implicit (emitting no identifier); hallucinated or wrong identifiers are not analysed separately; joint training on the benchmark train sets

title: ScanReason: Empowering 3D Visual Grounding with Reasoning Capabilities
authors: Chenming Zhu, Tai Wang, Wenwei Zhang, et al.
architecture: Visual-centric reasoning module = 3D-LLM (BLIP-2 Q-Former over back-projected multi-view 2D features, FlanT5-XL) that emits a <LOC> token; 3D grounding module = frozen point-cloud encoder + <LOC>-conditioned query selection (256 queries) + 3D box decoder
mechanism: the <LOC> hidden state cross-attends to geometry-enhanced point features ('look-back') to select object queries and decode boxes; at inference, Chain-of-Grounding first grounds the explicitly mentioned objects and feeds their locations back to the LLM before grounding the target
objective: next-token LM loss + 3D detection loss; LoRA instruction tuning on reformulated 3D-VG/detection/QA data + ScanReason
robustness_tests: ScanReason breakdown by reasoning type (spatial, functional, logical, emotional, safety); training-data ablation; no unique/multiple, zero-target or distractor analysis
limitations: (our reading) The benchmark is GPT-4-generated (only val manually verified); there is no handling of unanswerable/false-premise questions; absolute ScanReason accuracy is low (Acc@0.25 about 29-31); Nr3D/Sr3D are not evaluated; ScanRefer is reported overall only

title: CityRefer: Geography-aware 3D Visual Grounding Dataset on City-scale Point Cloud Data
authors: Taiki Miyanishi, Fumiya Kitamori, Shuhei Kurita, et al.
architecture: baseline: SoftGroup++ instance segmentation (2% point sampling) + modified InstanceRefer ranker (sparse-conv object encoder, BiGRU language encoder, BiGRU fusion with landmark features, MLP scorer)
mechanism: geography-aware ranking: candidate objects are fused with landmark features (names and 3D geometry from an OpenStreetMap spatial join) and the description; the highest-scoring of 10 candidates is selected
objective: softmax cross-entropy over candidate objects
robustness_tests: none reported (per-category breakdown Building/Car/Ground/Parking; human upper bound; landmark/colour/name feature ablations)
limitations: Authors: static scenes only, so the vocabulary is limited to static objects; the baseline is far below humans. Our reading: grounding is scored with 10 given candidates (simplified protocol); data come from two UK cities only

title: Language-Guided Progressive Attention for Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing Images
authors: Ke Li, Di Wang, Haojie Xu, et al.
architecture: ResNet-50 visual backbone modulated by language-generated dynamic weights/biases (Progressive Attention module); BERT linguistic backbone; Multi-level Feature Enhancement decoder; box localization module
mechanism: progressive attention: expression-conditioned multi-scale weights and biases steer the visual backbone towards expression-related features at spatial and channel levels (counters attention drift); the MFE decoder aggregates context of the referred object and suppresses irrelevant regions
objective: box regression supervision (loss details not read: full text not accessible)
robustness_tests: none reported (judged from abstract and author README; full text not read)
limitations: (our reading) Single ResNet-50/BERT configuration; no ambiguity, absent-target or sensor-shift evaluation visible; full paper not inspected

title: Talk2Car: Taking Control of Your Self-Driving Car
authors: Thierry Deruyttere, Simon Vandenhende, Dusan Grujicic, et al.
architecture: Benchmark of 7 models: region-proposal-based OSM and SCRC (on an RPN), non-proposal MAC and STACK-NMN, and simple baselines RS/BOBB/RNM
mechanism: Dataset paper: free-form commands (AMT) to a car, each grounded to one referred object in nuScenes scenes; 3D boxes projected to 2D for evaluation
objective: Per baseline (proposal ranking or box prediction); no new model
robustness_tests: Challenging test subsets (Fig. 3): top-k furthest objects, shortest/longest commands, and number of same-category objects in the scene (ambiguity); command-blanking bias probe (SCRC 40.37% with zeroed command vs 38.70% with command; OSM 21.65% vs 35.31%); effect of region-proposal quality
limitations: Stated: SCRC exploits a dataset bias (performs as well without the command). (our reading) one referent per command, no no-target commands; 2D evaluation of objects annotated in 3D; small scale

title: Talk2Radar: Bridging Natural Language with 4D mmWave Radar for 3D Referring Expression Comprehension
authors: Runwei Guan, Ruixiao Zhang, Ningwei Ouyang, et al.
architecture: T-RadarNet: radar point cloud as 2D pseudo-image, SECOND backbone with Deformable-FPN; ALBERT text encoder; Gated Graph Fusion; anchor-free center-based head with deformable separable localisation head
mechanism: Gated Graph Fusion: graph aggregation of neighbouring radar BEV features plus point-wise cross-modal gating between radar and text features at three scales
objective: Text-referenced 3D detection with a center-based detection head (loss details not re-checked)
robustness_tests: Radar vs LiDAR input compared per prompt type (Table IV) - a sensor comparison, not a degradation test; prompts may refer to one or more objects
limitations: (our reading) single source dataset (VoD urban scenes); radar sparsity and multi-path clutter noted as a challenge; no adverse-weather split reported

title: RGBT-GroundBench: Visual Grounding Beyond RGB in Complex Real-World Scenarios
authors: Tianyi Zhao, Jiawen Xi, Linhui Xiao, et al.
architecture: Benchmark of 11 VG models in one codebase (RGB-only, TIR-only, RGB+TIR inputs); reference baseline RGBT-VGNet: CLIP-based with Asymmetric Modality Adaptation, Language-Aware Visual Synergy, Illumination-Local-Global Tri-Prior Fusion, VL-Transformer and MLP box head on a [Reg] token
mechanism: Illumination-aware tri-prior fusion weights RGB vs thermal features; language-aware visual synergy for cross-modal interaction; [Reg]-token box regression
objective: Box regression from the [Reg] token (loss details not re-checked)
robustness_tests: Test subsets: TestA (normal-size targets, normal/strong light), TestB (night, weak/very-weak light), TestC (small targets); annotations of scene type, illumination, weather, size and occlusion (scene/weather/occlusion splits in supplement); same models run with RGB-only, TIR-only and RGB+TIR inputs; MLLMs also evaluated
limitations: Stated findings: accuracy drops with scene complexity and under low illumination; MLLMs show cross-spectral limitations. (our reading) one box per expression, no absent-target expressions

title: Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing Images
authors: Yuxi Sun, Shanshan Feng, Xutao Li, et al.
architecture: GeoVG: language encoder that builds a geospatial relation graph from the expression, image encoder with adaptive region attention, fusion module (from abstract/project page; full text not accessed)
mechanism: Geospatial relation graph from the expression guides adaptive region attention over a large-scale remote-sensing scene
objective: Box supervision (details not checked)
robustness_tests: none reported (not checked: full text not accessed)
limitations: (our reading) single-target boxes; no negatives; full text not examined this session

title: RSVG: Exploring Data and Models for Visual Grounding on Remote Sensing Data
authors: Yang Zhan, Zhitong Xiong, Yuan Yuan
architecture: TransVG-based: truncated ResNet-50 + 6 conv layers (multi-scale), BERT-base, multi-level cross-modal module (MLCM/MGVLF), 6-layer fusion transformer, MLP box head on a learnable token
foundation_models: ResNet-50 and transformer weights from DETR; BERT-base
mechanism: Multi-scale visual features filtered by word- and sentence-level text embeddings, then self-attention; joint visual-text-[REG] transformer regresses the box
objective: Smooth L1 + GIoU box regression
robustness_tests: none reported (component ablation only)
limitations: (our reading) expressions produced by an automatic generation method with manual assistance; one target per query; no negatives

title: RRSIS: Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
authors: Zhenghang Yuan, Lichao Mou, Yuansheng Hua, et al.
architecture: LAVT baseline (Swin-B backbone with language-aware visual encoding, BERT-base) plus a language-guided cross-scale enhancement (LGCE) module
mechanism: LGCE uses linguistic features to fuse deep (stage-4) and shallow Swin features, enhancing small and scattered targets
objective: Per-pixel mask segmentation loss (as in LAVT; not re-checked)
robustness_tests: none reported (component ablation; qualitative analysis of small and scattered objects)
limitations: Stated: no notable oIoU gain over LAVT because LAVT already handles large objects; natural-image RIS models miss small and scattered objects. (our reading) small dataset with template-generated expressions

title: GeoChat: Grounded Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing
authors: Kartik Kuckreja, Muhammad Sohail Danish, Muzammal Naseer, et al.
task: REC / region captioning / grounded description (remote-sensing MLLM)
A_query: referring expression; implicit instruction; visual prompt
architecture: LLaVA-1.5: CLIP ViT-L/14 (positional encoding interpolated to 504x504, 1,296 patches) + one-hidden-layer MLP adaptor + Vicuna-v1.5; LoRA fine-tuning
mechanism: Task tokens ([grounding], [refer], [identify]); boxes as text {x_left, y_top, x_right, y_bottom | theta} normalised to [0,100], usable as input regions and as outputs
objective: LoRA instruction tuning (next-token prediction) on a ~318k remote-sensing instruction set generated with Vicuna-v1.5 from detection, VQA and scene-classification datasets
robustness_tests: Object-size breakdown (small/medium/large) and single- vs multi-object grounding (Table 7)
limitations: Stated: grounding accuracy is low and leaves significant room for improvement (Table 7 caption). (our reading) referring expressions synthesised from detection labels and attributes; no absent-target handling

title: Making the Most of Text Semantics to Improve Biomedical Vision–Language Processing
authors: Benedikt Boecking, Naoto Usuyama, Shruthi Bannur, et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Dual encoder: ResNet-50 image encoder (SimCLR-pretrained on MIMIC-CXR) + CXR-BERT (radiology vocabulary, MLM, radiology section matching) with projection heads
mechanism: Global image-report contrastive alignment; grounding read out as cosine-similarity map between patch embeddings and phrase embedding
objective: Image-text InfoNCE + MLM during joint training (BioViL-L adds a local loss)
robustness_tests: none reported (results averaged over 4 seeds; per-finding breakdown)
limitations: (our reading) similarity-map grounding only, no box or mask output; each MS-CXR sentence describes a single finding; small benchmark (1,153 pairs)

title: Generalized Medical Phrase Grounding
authors: Wenjun Zhang, Shekhar S. Chandra, Aaron Nicolson
task: generalised medical phrase grounding (0..K boxes per sentence)
G_conditions: absent target/false premise; multi-target; domain/sensor shift
architecture: MDETR-based: ResNet-101 image encoder + BioClinical ModernBERT, bidirectional cross-modal encoder, Transformer decoder with 5 object queries, box FFN and confidence head; weighted box fusion
mechanism: Set prediction: each query outputs a box and confidence, so a sentence can get zero, one or several boxes; Hungarian matching
objective: Hungarian-matched box and confidence losses; stage 1 pretraining on GMPG-ImaGenome sentence-anatomy boxes, stage 2 fine-tuning on human-annotated finding boxes
robustness_tests: Non-groundable (negated/normal) phrases scored with N-Acc on PadChest-GR (MS-CXR has no zero-box phrases); single vs multi-box breakdown; zero-shot transfer of the pretrained model to both datasets; cross-dataset fine-tuning and annotation-discrepancy analysis (Tables V, VII)
limitations: Stated: strict boundary agreement is unreliable for diffuse findings; joint fine-tuning on PadChest-GR+MS-CXR hurts MS-CXR because annotation styles differ (Table VII). (our reading) boxes only

title: SUN-Spot: An RGB-D Dataset With Spatial Referring Expressions
authors: Cecilia Mauceri, Martha Palmer, Christoffer Heckman
architecture: Mao et al. (2016) CNN-LSTM speaker baseline with VGG-16 image features; RGB-D variant adds a 4th depth channel to VGG-16's first layer
mechanism: Comprehension by generation-likelihood ranking: pick the box that maximises the probability of generating the expression
objective: LSTM expression-generation likelihood; depth VGG pretrained with multi-label BCE on COCO
robustness_tests: Cross-dataset transfer RefExp to SUN-Spot (Baseline vs Baseline+fine, Table 2); RGB vs RGB-D input comparison (Table 3)
limitations: (our reading) very small dataset; weak comprehension baselines; depth for RefExp pretraining is synthetic (MegaDepth)

title: WildRefer: 3D Object Localization in Large-Scale Dynamic Scenes with Multi-modal Visual Data and Natural Language
authors: Zhenxiang Lin, Xidong Peng, Peishan Cong, et al.
task: 3D-VG in the wild (LiDAR + camera, dynamic scenes)
architecture: PointNet++ on temporal LiDAR point clouds + pretrained ResNet34 on temporal images + RoBERTa; Dynamic Visual Encoder; Triple-modal Feature Interaction; DETR-like decoder
mechanism: Spatio-temporal attention extracts motion features across frames; tri-modal (point/image/language) interaction; decoder selects the target from contextualised language-visual tokens
objective: DETR-style box prediction and target selection (loss details not re-checked)
robustness_tests: none reported (our reading of main and ablation tables)
limitations: (our reading) human-centric scenes only; one target per description; ~30 m LiDAR perception radius

title: Language Prompt for Autonomous Driving
authors: Dongming Wu, Wencheng Han, Yingfei Liu, et al.
task: prompt-referred multi-object 3D tracking and trajectory prediction (driving)
architecture: PromptTrack: built on the camera-only query-based 3D tracker PF-Track (past and future reasoning branches), plus prompt-visual cross-attention and a prompt reasoning branch
mechanism: Cross-attention between prompt embedding and multi-view, multi-frame visual features; prompt reasoning selects the referred tracks
objective: Tracking + prompt-referral + trajectory-forecast losses (details not re-checked)
robustness_tests: none reported (our reading)
limitations: Evident: prompts are generated by GPT-3.5 from combined language elements, so language is partly synthetic (annotation provenance). (our reading) camera-only input

title: Talk2BEV: Language-enhanced Bird’s-eye View Maps for Autonomous Driving
authors: Tushar Choudhary, Vikrant Dewangan, Shivam Chandhok, et al.
task: language-queried BEV scene understanding / VQA with object grounding (driving)
architecture: Lift-Splat-Shoot BEV from multi-view images; each BEV object projected to the image, cropped and captioned by an LVLM (BLIP-2, InstructBLIP-2, MiniGPT-4); GPT-4 reasons over the language-enhanced map
mechanism: Language-enhanced BEV map (geometry + captions per object) passed to an LLM that answers in JSON and calls primitive spatial operators (distance, direction, area) via API
objective: none (training-free)
robustness_tests: LSS-predicted vs ground-truth BEV maps compared (Table II); without spatial operators ablation (Table III); per-category results (Table IV)
limitations: (our reading) depends on a closed LLM (GPT-4); outputs answers/object IDs rather than boxes; benchmark descriptions partly generated by captioners before human annotation

title: Rotated Multi-Scale Interaction Network for Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
authors: Sihan Liu, Yiwei Ma, Xiaoqing Zhang, et al.
architecture: Swin-B (ImageNet-22K) + BERT-base; Intra-scale Interaction Module (IIM), Cross-scale Interaction Module (CIM); oriented-aware decoder with Adaptive Rotated Convolution (ARC)
mechanism: Intra- and cross-scale vision-language interaction, then rotation-adaptive convolution in the decoder for arbitrarily oriented targets
objective: Mask segmentation loss (not re-checked)
robustness_tests: none reported (qualitative examples on small and rotated objects)
limitations: Stated: SAM accuracy varies on aerial images (domain gap), so masks needed manual refinement. (our reading) one target per expression; no absent-target expressions

title: Medical Phrase Grounding with Region-Phrase Context Contrastive Alignment
authors: Zhihao Chen, Yang Zhou, Anh Tran, et al.
task: medical phrase grounding (REC on chest X-ray)
architecture: Lightweight vision-language transformer (TransVG-style): ResNet-50 + BERT, [REG] token, 3-layer MLP box head; TaCo module
foundation_models: ResNet-50, BERT (initialised from natural-image grounding models)
mechanism: Tri-attention Context contrastive alignment (TaCo): InfoNCE over region-phrase pairs with triple-attention context pooling, at feature and attention level
objective: Smooth L1 + GIoU box regression + TaCo InfoNCE
robustness_tests: Unimodal probes on MS-CXR (Table II): image-only input 41.91 Acc, phrase-only input 40.12 Acc (vs 69.86 full)
limitations: (our reading) one box per phrase, so multi-region and non-groundable phrases are not handled; own data split limits comparability

title: GeoGround: A Unified Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing Visual Grounding
authors: Yue Zhou, Mengcheng Lan, Xiang Li, et al.
architecture: CLIP-ViT visual encoder + two-layer MLP connector + Vicuna-1.5 LLM (LLaVA-1.5-7B), no extra encoders or decoders; optional SAM refinement
mechanism: Signal textualisation: Text-HBB, Text-OBB (long-side 90-degree angle) and Text-Mask (mask downsampled to an NxN binary grid written as text)
objective: Next-token prediction with hybrid supervision: prompt-assisted learning (PAL) and geometry-guided learning (GGL) to keep HBB, OBB and mask outputs consistent
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Stated: higher Text-Mask resolution is harder to train, and low-resolution masks are coarse (SAM needed for fine boundaries); still below the specialist RMSIN on RRSIS-D. (our reading) not peer-reviewed

authors: Shruthi Bannur, Kenza Bouzid, Daniel C. Castro, et al.

architecture: Frozen Rad-DINO-MAIRA-2 ViT image encoder (518x518 input, 1,369 visual tokens) + trained adapter + autoregressive language model with coordinate tokens

mechanism: Boxes emitted as coordinate tokens attached to report sentences; inputs include current frontal and lateral views, prior frontal image and report, and Indication/Technique/Comparison sections
objective: Multi-task next-token prediction: findings generation, grounded reporting and phrase grounding (510,848 examples)
robustness_tests: none reported (not checked)
limitations: (our reading) partly private training data (USMix/GR-Bench); RadFact relies on an LLM judge (GPT-4-based)

title: Visual Referring Expression Recognition: What Do Systems Actually Learn?
authors: Volkan Cirik, Louis-Philippe Morency, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick

authors: Liangyu Chen, Zihao Yue, Boshen Xu et al.

authors: Jia Li, Wenjie Zhao, Ziru Huang et al.

title: Words or Vision: Do Vision-Language Models Have Blind Faith in Text?
authors: Ailin Deng, Tri Cao, Zhirui Chen et al.
