limitations: Missingness means dropped frames / words within the same two modalities, not loss of an auxiliary modality such as audio or subtitles; incompleteness is synthetic (our reading)

title: Both-or-Neither: Counterfactual Joint-Evidence Auditing for Reliable Audio-Visual Event Localization
authors: Vadim Tynchenko, Aleksei Borodulin, Nikolay Kalutskiy et al.
venue: Proceedings of the 1st International Workshop on Joint Audio-Video Comprehension and Generation (ACM MM 2026 Workshop)
architecture: Lightweight CPU probes on frozen AVE audio and visual features; AV-AND combines geometric fusion, cross-modal disagreement, modality agreement and validation-constrained selective gating
mechanism: Counterfactual interventions (modality removal, same-class and cross-class replacement, temporal audio shift) to test whether segment predictions need both modalities
objective: Segment-level event classification on AVE (supervised)
robustness_tests: Modality removal; same-class and cross-class audio/visual replacement; temporal audio shift; group-disjoint re-split after finding 18 source videos shared across AVE subsets
limitations: Frozen features and lightweight probes only; single dataset (AVE); full text not read, details from abstract (our reading)

title: AVTrace: Diagnosing Audio-Visual Temporal Reasoning in Omni Models
authors: Longyin Zhang, Parth Sakhare Mahendra, Chengwei Wei et al.
architecture: Benchmark; evaluates Qwen3-Omni-30B, MiniCPM-o-4.5, Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, InteractiveOmni-4B and Gemma4-E4B-it, plus post-trained Gemma4-E4B variants
mechanism: Seven diagnostic categories: minimal-span and event-span grounding, A/V synchronisation verification, next-step, conditional cross-modal localisation, chain parsing, event-conditioned grounding
objective: n/a (benchmark); parameter-efficient temporal post-training baseline
robustness_tests: Development-set perturbations of Qwen3-Omni-30B: input-stream removal (including text-only), lower visual sampling, frame permutation; paired-bootstrap CIs (Figure 2)
limitations: Silver-standard (model-assisted) references; modality-removal analysis covers one model and is shown only in a figure (our reading)

title: AVID: A Benchmark for Omni-Modal Audio-Visual Inconsistency Understanding via Agent-Driven Construction
authors: Zixuan Chen, Depeng Wang, Hao Lin et al.
architecture: Benchmark built by temporal segmentation (active speaker / voiceover / scenic), an agent-driven strategy planner and five conflict injectors; baseline AVID-Qwen fine-tuned from Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct
mechanism: Omni-model reads interleaved video frames and audio and outputs inconsistency timestamps, category and explanation as text
objective: Two-stage fine-tuning on segment-level then full-video inconsistency data (baseline)
robustness_tests: Whole benchmark targets injected audio-visual conflicts (8 inconsistency categories); omni-models evaluated on detecting, temporally grounding, classifying and explaining them
limitations: Conflicts are synthetically injected; the grounding target is the conflict itself rather than a user query grounded under conflicting streams; LLM-assisted construction (our reading)

title: GEAL: Generalizable 3D Affordance Learning with Cross-Modal Consistency
authors: Dongyue Lu, Lingdong Kong, Tianxin Huang et al.
architecture: Dual-branch: 3D point branch plus a 2D branch that renders views from sparse point clouds via Gaussian splatting and uses large pre-trained 2D models; granularity-adaptive fusion and 2D-3D consistency alignment
mechanism: Cross-modal (2D-3D) consistency alignment transfers 2D semantics to the 3D affordance branch
objective: Supervised per-point affordance prediction plus 2D-3D consistency alignment
robustness_tests: PIAD-C and LASO-C: seven point-cloud corruptions (Add Global, Add Local, Drop Global, Drop Local, Rotate, Scale, Jitter), five severities each, 4,890 object-affordance pairs (arXiv 2412.09511 Sec. 3.4)
limitations: Object-level affordance grounding on isolated object point clouds, not scene-level referring grounding; synthetic corruptions only (our reading)

title: HAMMER: Harnessing MLLMs via Cross-Modal Integration for Intention-Driven 3D Affordance Grounding
authors: Lei Yao, Yong Chen, Yuejiao Su et al.
architecture: MLLM aggregates the interaction intention in a reference image into a contact-aware embedding; hierarchical cross-modal integration refines 3D point features; multi-granular geometry lifting module
mechanism: Intention embedding from the MLLM, lifted with geometry, guides per-point affordance decoding
objective: Supervised affordance prediction with MLLM-inferred textual affordance labels (per abstract)
robustness_tests: Newly constructed corrupted benchmark 'with noise-infused point clouds' (arXiv 2603.02329 Sec. 1; construction in Supp. S.3, per-corruption results in Supp. S.2.7)
limitations: Object-level affordance grounding with image (not language) queries; synthetic corruptions (our reading)

title: MVGGT: Multimodal Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer for Multiview 3D Referring Expression Segmentation
authors: Changli Wu, Haodong Wang, Jiayi Ji et al.
architecture: End-to-end dual-branch transformer that integrates language into sparse-view visual-geometry reasoning (no pre-built point cloud)
mechanism: Language injected into feed-forward multi-view geometry reasoning; Per-view No-target Suppression Optimization (PVSO) balances gradients across views
objective: Supervised 3D mask prediction with PVSO to counter 'Foreground Gradient Dilution'
robustness_tests: Setting itself removes the dense point cloud: segmentation 'directly from sparse multi-view images'; compares with two-stage reconstruct-then-segment pipelines
limitations: Sparse views are the task definition, not a controlled degradation sweep against a dense-scan reference (our reading)

title: LangRef3DGS: Natural Language-Guided 3D Referential Segmentation from Partial Observations via 3D Gaussian Splatting
authors: Xulun Ye, Qin Zhang, Kun Zhou
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Real-time 3DGS semantic embedding field built from partial RGB-D observations; Dirichlet-process novel-category discovery; gradient low-rank mechanism for class separability
mechanism: Text prompt queries a continuous, differentiable 3DGS embedding field
objective: Embedding-field learning (details per paper; F facet our reading)
robustness_tests: Reports 'robustness to partial inputs' (abstract claim); exact partial-observation protocol not checked
limitations: Text prompts appear to be open-vocabulary category prompts rather than full referring expressions (our reading of abstract); supervision type not confirmed

title: Affostruction: 3D Affordance Grounding with Generative Reconstruction
authors: Chunghyun Park, Seunghyeon Lee, Minsu Cho
architecture: Generative reconstruction of complete object geometry from partial RGB-D views via sparse voxel fusion of multi-view features; flow-based affordance distribution; affordance-guided active view selection
mechanism: Grounds the text-described action on the reconstructed full shape, including unobserved surfaces
objective: Flow-based generative affordance modelling plus reconstruction (per abstract)
robustness_tests: Partial observation is the task setting (grounding on unobserved regions); no corruption sweep stated in abstract
limitations: Object-level; partial views by construction rather than a controlled degradation study (our reading)

title: Talk2Sensors: 3D Visual Grounding in Autonomous Driving via Sensor-Adaptive Physical Cue Matching
authors: Runwei Guan, Di Tian, Ningwei Ouyang et al.
architecture: TSFormer built on FUTR3D: ResNet-101+FPN image encoder, voxelised LiDAR and radar encoders, CLIP text encoder; Language-Routed Property Sampler and Sparse-Preserving Modality Arbiter; DETR-style decoder
mechanism: Text-conditioned modality gating routes appearance (camera), geometry (LiDAR) and kinematics (radar) per query
objective: Hungarian matching with referring-confidence CE, L1 box and 3D GIoU losses
robustness_tests: Inference-time modality dropout (Sec. V-C, Fig. 8b): TSFormer loses 5.17 mAP vs FUTR3D 7.64 without camera, 4.34 vs 4.56 without radar; both collapse without LiDAR. Adverse-weather and night evaluation explicitly left to future work
limitations: Dropout results shown in a figure with deltas in text only; no weather/night split; preprint (our reading)

title: I Speak and You Find: Robust 3D Visual Grounding with Noisy and Ambiguous Speech Inputs
authors: Yu Qi, Lipeng Gu, Honghua Chen et al.
architecture: SpeechRefer plug-in for existing 3D-VG models: Speech Complementary Module (proposal scores from speech) and Contrastive Complementary Module (aligns erroneous transcripts with speech features)
mechanism: Speech-derived complementary proposal scores reduce reliance on erroneous ASR transcripts
objective: Grounding loss plus contrastive speech-text alignment
robustness_tests: Evaluates 3D-VG under noisy/ambiguous speech-to-text transcriptions (accents, background noise, speech rate)
limitations: Degradation is on the query side (speech/ASR), not on the 3D input (our reading); preprint

title: SeqAlign3DVG: A Sequence-Aligned Benchmark and Voxel Reasoning Framework for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Yi Zhang, Yi Wang, Yueting Wu et al.
architecture: Voxel-based pipeline with Relevance-Ordered Voxel Memory (ROVM) and Progressive Language-Voxel Fusion (PLVF)
mechanism: Ranks and aggregates multi-view evidence into a conservative voxel memory 'to mitigate noisy observations', then coarse-to-fine language-voxel fusion
objective: Supervised 3D box grounding
robustness_tests: Depth-free protocol; expressions strictly grounded in the provided RGB observations (partial views)
limitations: Missing depth is a protocol choice, not a controlled comparison with depth available (our reading)

title: Unveiling the Mist over 3D Vision-Language Understanding: Object-centric Evaluation with Chain-of-Analysis
authors: Jiangyong Huang, Baoxiong Jia, Yan Wang et al.
architecture: Benchmark; evaluates state-of-the-art 3D-VL models including LLM-based ones
mechanism: Object-centric evaluation (multiple tests per object) plus chain-of-analysis linking grounding and QA
objective: n/a (benchmark)
robustness_tests: Re-annotated high-quality test data; object-centric evaluation for language robustness; grounding-QA coherence analysis
limitations: Not a blind-baseline study; flaws of existing test sets are characterised qualitatively in the abstract (our reading)

title: P$^3$-VLM: A Point-based Alternative for Grounded 3D Vision-Language Models
authors: Anna-Maria Halacheva, Jan-Nico Zaech, Sombit Dey et al.
architecture: Blind-LLM audit (Qwen3-VL-4B LLM fine-tuned with LoRA on box or point coordinates only) plus a proposed detector-free tri-pathway 3D VLM (P^3-VLM)
mechanism: Replaces bounding-box prompts with single-point prompts to remove the box-geometry category shortcut
objective: n/a for the audit; P^3-VLM trained for point-prompted grounded captioning
robustness_tests: Blind-LLM baseline; box-vs-point prompting; robustness to bounding-box and query-point perturbation; OOD generalisation
limitations: Audits location-prompted captioning/identification (location is input, not output), not localisation-output grounding; class accuracy relies on an LLM extractor (our reading)

title: ViGiL3D: A Linguistically Diverse Dataset for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Austin T. Wang, ZeMing Gong, Angel X. Chang
architecture: Linguistic analysis framework for 3D-VG prompts plus a diagnostic dataset; evaluates open-vocabulary 3D-VG methods
mechanism: Taxonomy of language patterns used to measure coverage of existing 3D-VG datasets and to build out-of-distribution prompts
objective: n/a (dataset)
robustness_tests: Out-of-distribution, linguistically diverse prompts for existing open-vocabulary 3D-VG methods
limitations: Audits linguistic coverage, not label noise or blind baselines (our reading)

title: LanguageRefer: Spatial-Language Model for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Junha Roh, Karthik Desingh, Ali Farhadi et al.
architecture: Transformer combining spatial embeddings of candidate 3D boxes (with predicted classes) and fine-tuned DistilBERT language embeddings
mechanism: Language + box-geometry tokens scored by a transformer; no dense visual features beyond class labels
objective: Target classification among candidates
robustness_tests: Analysis decoupled from perception noise (ground-truth classes), accuracy on view-dependent utterances, viewpoint annotations
limitations: Not a dedicated audit; viewpoint analysis covers ReferIt3D only (our reading)

title: A Critical Assessment of Visual Sound Source Localization Models Including Negative Audio
authors: Xavier Juanola, Gloria Haro, Magdalena Fuentes
architecture: Evaluation of SOTA VSSL models with a new negative-audio test set and metrics
mechanism: Negative audio (silence, noise, off-screen) where no visible object matches the sound; analysis of similarity-map maxima
objective: n/a (evaluation)
robustness_tests: Silence, noise and off-screen negative audio; threshold analysis of audio-visual similarity maps
limitations: Image-level VSSL; synthetic negative construction (our reading)

title: Learning from Silence and Noise for Visual Sound Source Localization
authors: Xavier Juanola, Giovana Morais, Magdalena Fuentes et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Self-supervised audio-visual model (SSL-SaN) trained with silence and noise negatives
mechanism: Audio-visual similarity maps learned with explicit negative-audio samples
objective: Self-supervised contrastive training including silence/noise
robustness_tests: Negative audio (silence, noise, off-screen); new metric quantifying alignment vs. separability across positive and negative pairs
limitations: Method plus evaluation contribution; synthetic IS3+ (our reading)

title: What's Making That Sound Right Now? Video-centric Audio-Visual Localization
authors: Hahyeon Choi, Junhoo Lee, Nojun Kwak
architecture: Benchmark (AVATAR) plus a temporal model (TAVLO)
mechanism: Video-level, temporally resolved evaluation with Single-sound, Mixed-sound, Multi-entity and Off-screen scenarios
objective: n/a for the benchmark
robustness_tests: Off-screen and mixed-sound scenarios; temporal variation
limitations: F facet is our reading (evaluated AVL models are mostly self-supervised)

title: Can I Trust Your Answer? Visually Grounded Video Question Answering
authors: Junbin Xiao, Angela Yao, Yicong Li et al.
architecture: NExT-GQA benchmark plus a weakly-supervised grounding module (Gaussian mask optimisation + cross-modal learning) on dual (Temp[CLIP]) and stacked (FrozenBiLM) VLMs
mechanism: Learnable Gaussian temporal mask selects the answer-supporting segment; QA from masked video
objective: QA loss with Gaussian-mask grounding and cross-modal contrastive learning (no temporal labels in training)
robustness_tests: BlindQA (text-only) baseline; PosQA/NegQA sampling frames inside vs outside ground-truth evidence segments (QA accuracy 'almost unaffected')
limitations: Weak grounding even with the proposed method (Acc@GQA <18% vs 82.1 human); short NExT-QA videos (our reading; CG-Bench makes the same point)

title: CG-Bench: Clue-grounded Question Answering Benchmark for Long Video Understanding
authors: Guo Chen, Yicheng Liu, Yifei Huang et al.
architecture: Benchmark of 1,219 long videos and 12,129 question-answer-clue triplets; evaluates closed and open MLLMs
foundation_models: GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5, Claude-3.5, Qwen2-VL-72B, InternVL2-78B and others (evaluated)
mechanism: White-box: model outputs clue intervals scored by tIoU and jointly with answer (acc.@IoU); black-box: Clue Recovery Rate compares full-video vs clue-only MCQ accuracy
objective: n/a (benchmark)
robustness_tests: Clue-only vs full-video MCQ (black-box CRR); text-only GPT-4o baseline; 444 hallucination-type questions
limitations: Clue grounding scored by tIoU against human intervals with very low absolute values; acc.@IoU threshold default tau=0 (our reading)

title: ReXTime: A Benchmark Suite for Reasoning-Across-Time in Videos
authors: Jr-Jen Chen, Yu-Chien Liao, Hsi-Che Lin et al.
architecture: Benchmark (921 val / 2,143 test human-verified samples) plus 9,695 machine-generated training samples; evaluates frontier MLLMs and moment-retrieval models
foundation_models: GPT-4o, GPT-4V, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Claude3-Opus, Reka-Core, VTimeLLM, TimeChat, LITA, UniVTG, CG-DETR (evaluated)
mechanism: Models must output the time span of the chosen answer; joint accuracy@IoU>=0.5
objective: n/a (benchmark); fine-tuning on generated data studied
robustness_tests: Requires answer-span output to counter language-only MCQ shortcuts (Sec. 3.3)
limitations: Answer-span localisation is scored against re-annotated caption spans; frontier models evaluated on a 300-sample mini-test (stated)

title: V-STaR: Benchmarking Video-LLMs on Video Spatio-Temporal Reasoning
authors: Zixu Cheng, Jian Hu, Ziquan Liu et al.
architecture: Benchmark with coarse-to-fine CoT question chains (GPT-4-assisted, semi-automatic) evaluating 14-16 Video-LLMs
mechanism: Reverse Spatio-Temporal Reasoning (RSTR): jointly scores what (answer), when (temporal grounding) and where (box grounding) along ordered chains
objective: n/a (benchmark)
robustness_tests: Consistency across reasoning-chain orders (what-when-where vs what-where-when)
limitations: CoT questions generated with GPT-4 pipeline (our reading)

title: Open-o3-Video: Grounded Video Reasoning with Explicit Spatio-Temporal Evidence
authors: Jiahao Meng, Xiangtai Li, Haochen Wang et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: Non-agent Video-LLM (Qwen2.5-VL baseline) that emits timestamps, objects and boxes inside its reasoning trace
mechanism: Explicit spatio-temporal evidence (key timestamps + boxes) embedded in the reasoning chain
objective: Cold-start SFT on STGR data, then RL with rewards for answer accuracy, temporal alignment and spatial precision
robustness_tests: Grounded traces used for confidence-aware test-time scaling
limitations: Evidence is scored against annotations; whether the cited evidence causally drives the answer is not tested (our reading)

title: VideoZeroBench: Probing the Limits of Video MLLMs with Spatio-Temporal Evidence Verification
authors: Jiahao Meng, Yue Tan, Qi Xu et al.
task: long-video QA with spatio-temporal evidence verification
architecture: Benchmark with manually annotated QA, temporal intervals and key-frame boxes across 13 domains; 19 models evaluated
mechanism: Five-level diagnostic protocol: answering with/without evidence hints, then answer correctness combined with independently evaluated temporal and spatial grounding
objective: n/a (benchmark)
robustness_tests: Evidence-hint ablation (with vs without evidence hints)
limitations: Preprint (our reading)

title: What You Ask is What You Ground: Bridging Question Intent to Temporal Evidence for Grounded VideoQA
authors: Jinhwan Seo, Kyubeom Han, Jumin Lee et al.
architecture: GroundFormer: question-conditioned video features via learnable communication tokens, factorised MIL cross-attention coupling answer selection with temporal evidence, Gaussian smoothing
mechanism: Question intent injected before localisation so that evidence segments differ across questions on the same video
objective: Candidate-level MIL supervision plus hierarchical video-question-answer contrastive loss (two-pass training)
robustness_tests: Diagnoses question-invariant grounding (near-identical segments for different questions on the same video)
limitations: Preprint; temporal-only evidence (our reading)

title: ANCHOR: Audio-Visually Grounded Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Benchmark
authors: Joel Julin, Souraja Kundu, Liza Dahiya et al.
architecture: Benchmark: 2,319 videos / 8,272 QA with structured reasoning traces, temporal evidence, spatial boxes and salient audio cues; human-refined test set of 224 videos / 975 QA; 12 MLLMs evaluated
mechanism: Grounded-rationale alignment: separately scores answer correctness, hallucination, logical divergence, conciseness, and direct spatial/temporal grounding on a focused subset
objective: n/a (benchmark)
robustness_tests: Grounding-cue ablations (remove video / boxes / audio); reference-circularity check across human, Gemini and GPT references (Pearson r=0.99 on a matched subset)
limitations: Spatial/temporal grounding measured only on a focused subset (stated in abstract)

title: EvaOmni: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Audio-Visual Reasoning
authors: Xiaoxing Hu, Wenxi Yao, Chaoyuan Shi et al.
task: audio-visual QA with audio and visual evidence intervals
architecture: Benchmark: 392 videos, 1,027 human-annotated QA over 15 capabilities; expert-annotated audio and visual evidence; unimodal/text shortcut filtering; 24 Omni LLMs evaluated
mechanism: Models must return the answer and supporting evidence intervals per modality
objective: n/a (benchmark)
robustness_tests: Model-based filtering of textual and unimodal shortcuts; video-based distractors
limitations: Small (1,027 QA); temporal evidence only, no spatial evidence (our reading)

title: Video-HolmesV2: Can MLLMs Reason with Spatio-Temporal Audio-Visual Evidence in Long Videos?
authors: Zhaoyang Wei, Zipeng Wang, Yushe Cao et al.
task: long-video audio-visual reasoning with spatio-temporal evidence
architecture: Benchmark with multi-model cross-verification pipeline plus an audio-text guided token-compression baseline
mechanism: Evidence-Based Evaluation: answers must be justified with spatio-temporal audio-visual evidence, scored by a Spatio-temporal Evidence-Aware Metric
objective: n/a (benchmark); baseline uses audio/text-guided token compression
robustness_tests: Designed to reduce 'confounding effects of guessing and hallucinated evidence'
limitations: Preprint; metric details not checked (our reading)

title: ScanQA: 3D Question Answering for Spatial Scene Understanding
authors: Daichi Azuma, Taiki Miyanishi, Shuhei Kurita et al.
architecture: VoteNet proposals + GloVe/BiLSTM question encoder, transformer encoder-decoder fusion, heads for answer classification, object localisation and object classification
mechanism: Question-aware object proposals scored for localisation of question/answer-related objects jointly with answer classification
objective: Answer BCE + localisation CE + object classification + VoteNet detection losses
robustness_tests: none reported (ablation of localisation/classification heads shows QA benefits from joint localisation)
limitations: Answer and box are scored separately; no joint answer-evidence consistency metric (our reading)

title: Toward Explainable 3D Grounded Visual Question Answering: A New Benchmark and Strong Baseline
authors: Lichen Zhao, Daigang Cai, Jing Zhang et al.
architecture: FE-3DGQA dataset with dense, complete box annotations of answer-grounded and contextual objects, plus a 3D VQA baseline
mechanism: Predicts answers together with completely visually grounded objects (answer-grounded objects, including ones not mentioned in the question, and contextual objects)
objective: Joint answer and grounding supervision (per abstract)
robustness_tests: Motivated by susceptibility of 3D VQA 'to language priors and co-reference ambiguity'
limitations: Metric details not checked in this pass (our reading)

title: SceneCOT: Eliciting Grounded Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in 3D Scenes
authors: Xiongkun Linghu, Jiangyong Huang, Ziyu Zhu et al.
task: 3D situated / scene QA with grounded chain-of-thought
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: 3D-LLM reasoning pipeline that decomposes a query into task recognition, region localisation, entity grounding and grounded reasoning, with visual clues from multimodal expert modules
mechanism: Grounded CoT: intermediate steps localise regions/objects that are then used as clues for the answer
objective: Supervised training on SceneCOT-185K grounded CoT data
robustness_tests: none reported in abstract
limitations: Dataset size reported as 185K (arXiv) vs ~190K (proceedings abstract summary); coherence metric details not checked (our reading)

title: On the Consistency of Video Large Language Models in Temporal Comprehension
authors: Minjoon Jung, Junbin Xiao, Byoung-Tak Zhang et al.
architecture: Existing Video-LLMs (timestamps as text) probed after an initial grounding; plus instruction-tuned variants with the proposed event temporal verification tuning (VTune)
mechanism: Consistency probes applied after the model grounds a moment: rephrased language queries, temporally shifted ground-truth moment in the video, and verification questions that must agree with the initial prediction
objective: Study: prediction consistency; method: event temporal verification tuning (instruction tuning that explicitly accounts for consistency)
robustness_tests: Query rephrasing and temporal shifting of the target moment in the video (perturbation probes), plus verification-task probes; consistency measured relative to the model's own initial temporal grounding
limitations: Perturbations are semantic (paraphrase, moment shift), not low-level corruptions (noise, blur, compression, frame drops); limited to Video-LLMs on two datasets (our reading)

title: Distinguishing semantically similar queries in temporal video grounding via LLM-generated query
authors: Yibo Dang, Zhaobo Qi, Xinyan Liu et al.
G_conditions: degraded/noisy modality; ambiguity/distractors; absent target/false premise
architecture: VTG/HD models trained and evaluated with LLM-generated query sets (specific backbones not extracted)
foundation_models: LLM for query generation (model not extracted)
mechanism: Natural Language Query Generation (NLQG): an LLM generates meaning-preserving paraphrases and semantically similar but mismatched hard-negative queries
objective: Training with generated paraphrases/hard negatives; new evaluation metrics for robustness and generalisation
robustness_tests: Evaluation under LLM-paraphrased queries (same meaning) and semantically similar hard-negative queries, with new robustness metrics
limitations: Text-side perturbations only (paraphrase, near-miss negatives); no video corruptions (our reading, from abstract)

title: HERO: Hierarchical Embedding-Refinement for Open-Vocabulary Temporal Sentence Grounding in Videos
authors: Tingting Han, Xinsong Tao, Yufei Yin et al.
architecture: TSGV model with hierarchical linguistic embeddings, parallel cross-modal refinement, semantic-guided visual filtering and contrastive masked text refinement (paradigm label: our reading)
mechanism: Hierarchical text embeddings refined jointly with visual features; semantic-guided filtering of visual features
objective: Interval localisation loss plus contrastive masked text refinement
robustness_tests: Charades-OV / ActivityNet-OV: test-ood queries of Charades-CD/ActivityNet-CD 'rewritten to include at least one novel concept' by an LLM with manual verification, simulating 'vocabulary shifts and paraphrastic variations'
limitations: Query rewriting introduces novel vocabulary (open-vocabulary shift) rather than controlled typos/paraphrase severities; no video corruptions; preprint (our reading)

title: Knowledge-Preserved Model Tuning in Null-Space for Robust Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
authors: Haoxuan Chen, Xianqin Liu, Jian-Fang Hu
architecture: CG-STVG (CVPR 2024) baseline with Null-Space Tuning: Quality-Adaptive Unit + Dual-Space Reparameterization (DETR-style paradigm inherited from CG-STVG; our reading)
mechanism: Learnable input-feature residuals placed in the null space of frozen weights for high-quality inputs and in the non-null space (restoration) for low-quality inputs
objective: Parameter-efficient tuning on mixed high/low-quality data while preserving pre-trained knowledge
robustness_tests: Physics-based degradation pipeline (motion blur, defocus blur, low-light simulation, resolution reduction) mixed 1:1 with clean data; evaluates spatio-temporal tubes (incl. temporal IoU) under degraded video
limitations: Degradations limited to blur, low light and low resolution (no noise, compression, frame drops); spatio-temporal grounding only, not moment retrieval; single base model (our reading)

title: Beyond Uncertainty: Evidential Deep Learning for Robust Video Temporal Grounding
authors: Kaijing Ma, Haojian Huang, Jin Chen et al.
task: video temporal grounding (moment retrieval + highlight detection)
architecture: SRAM: Reflective Flipped Fusion cross-attention blocks on frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 + SlowFast R50 features, with VTG head, MLM head and Deep Evidential Regression head
mechanism: Two-stage cross-modal alignment; deep evidential regression to estimate aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty of interval predictions
objective: VTG losses + masked language modelling + evidential regression with a Geom-regularizer
robustness_tests: QVHighlights val: Gaussian noise of increasing variance added to video features, query tokens swapped at proportion r, and both jointly; reports shift of epistemic-uncertainty distributions (no localisation accuracy under perturbation); qualitative OOD cases (infrared, animated video, ambiguous/abstract queries)
limitations: Perturbations are feature-level and synthetic; only uncertainty shifts are reported, not R1/mAP under corruption; preprint (our reading)

title: Seeing is Not Believing: Adversarial Natural Object Optimization for Hard-Label 3D Scene Attacks
authors: Daizong Liu, Wei Hu
architecture: Attack on seven 3D visual grounding victims: ScanRefer, ReferIt3D, SAT, 3DTrans., 3D-SPS, ViL3DRel, EDA
mechanism: Hard-label (input/output access only) universal adversarial object: a realistic object trigger placed naturally in any scene and perturbed with slight additive noise via weighted gradient estimation, so grounding models mislocalise the described target
objective: Query-based optimisation of a universal trigger to minimise grounding IoU with the true target box
robustness_tests: Adversarial (hard-label, universal, physically plausible object insertion) attack on 7 3D-VG models on ScanRefer and Nr3D/Sr3D; imperceptibility and resistance to defenses
limitations: Classic 3D-VG models only; no 3D-LLM grounders; scene-side (point cloud) attack only, no text-side attack (our reading)

title: Manipulating the Bounding Box: Multimodal Controlled Backdoor Attacks on 3D Visual Grounding Models
authors: Xiayue Zhang, Huashuo Lei, Daizong Liu et al.
architecture: Backdoor attack applied to several standard 3D visual grounding models (victims not extracted)
mechanism: Multimodal backdoor: triggers designed for both point-cloud and text modalities with modality-specific placement strategies; optimised point-cloud trigger; triggered inputs shift the position and size of the predicted 3D box
objective: Data-poisoning backdoor training: adversary-chosen box manipulation on triggered inputs, normal behaviour on clean inputs
robustness_tests: Backdoor (training-time poisoning) attack on 3D visual grounding; reports attack effectiveness with 'negligible impact on performance in clean datasets' (abstract)
limitations: Full text not accessed (IEEE paywall); no defense/verification evaluated per abstract (our reading)

title: Can Audio-Visual Integration Strengthen Robustness Under Multimodal Attacks?
authors: Yapeng Tian, Chenliang Xu
task: sound source localisation (weakly supervised; secondary to AV event recognition)
architecture: Audio-visual event recognition networks with different fusion mechanisms; a weakly-supervised sound source visual localisation model used to interpret attacks
mechanism: Adversarial perturbations on audio, visual or both modalities; localisation maps inspected/attacked; defense with audio-visual dissimilarity constraint and external feature memory banks
objective: Study of multimodal adversarial robustness; defense trained with dissimilarity constraint + memory banks
robustness_tests: Unimodal and multimodal adversarial attacks on AV event recognition; shows that a weakly-supervised sound source localisation model 'can be successfully fooled'
limitations: Main task is classification; sound-source localisation is used as an interpretation tool, not a full grounding benchmark; pre-AVS era (our reading)

title: SNEAK: Synonymous Sentences-Aware Adversarial Attack on Natural Language Video Localization
authors: Wenbo Gou, Wen Shi, Jian Lou et al.
task: temporal sentence grounding (natural language video localization)
architecture: Victim: VSLNet (anchor-free span-based NLVL)
mechanism: Video-side adversarial perturbation optimised to mislead the model over a set of synonymous queries (gradient-splitting optimisation, frame pruning), compared with query-side and joint attacks; defense via adversarial training with synonymous queries
objective: Minimise IoU of predicted moments under bounded video perturbation across synonymous sentences
robustness_tests: White-box adversarial attacks on video, query and both for NLVL; robustness across synonymous queries; adversarial-training defense
limitations: Single victim model (VSLNet), pre-LLM; never peer-reviewed as far as found (our reading)

title: Conformal Coverage Guarantees for Any Video Temporal Grounder
authors: Aseel Mohamed, Rasul Khanbayov, Erchin Serpedin et al.
architecture: Post-hoc, model-agnostic wrapper (COVER) around any grounder: trained localisers or black-box video-language models
mechanism: Split-conformal calibration of a temporal nonconformity score; two score families: boundary-widening for interval outputs, super-level-set for relevance-signal outputs
objective: None for the grounder; quantile of the nonconformity score calibrated on held-out labels
robustness_tests: Theory and experiments on coverage conditional on event length and on exchangeability violations when several moments come from one video (abstract)
limitations: Marginal, exchangeability-based guarantee; benchmark names not given in the abstract (our reading)

title: Surrogate Uncertainty for Black-box Visual Grounding
authors: Hanbo Zhang, Tianrun Hu, Cedar Site Bai et al.
task: visual grounding of robot instructions (black-box VLM grounder)
architecture: External surrogate Bayesian model over a black-box VLM grounder; hierarchical cross-modal retrieval of a calibration-set neighbourhood
foundation_models: state-of-the-art black-box VLMs (not named in abstract)
mechanism: Treats the VLM prediction as an observation; per-query aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty from a local neighbourhood of a held-out calibration set; plugs into conformal prediction or model-based planning (ask or act)
objective: Bayesian surrogate fitted on a held-out calibration set (no VLM training)
robustness_tests: Real Fetch robot under open-world instructions (abstract)
limitations: Needs a labelled calibration set close to deployment distribution; output format of grounding (box vs. object choice) not specified in abstract, D_output is our reading

title: PROVE: Probabilistic Visual Grounding via Patch-Level Evidence for Vision-Language Models
authors: Mayank Nautiyal, Tianru Zhang, Li Ju et al.
E_paradigm: E4 open-set grounding pre-training / dual encoder
architecture: Post-hoc evidential adapter on frozen CLIP patch features; per-patch Beta distributions
mechanism: Per-patch membership evidence (positive/negative) -> posterior-mean grounding map, spatial vacuity map and image-level absence score in closed form
objective: Evidential loss on soft patch-coverage targets plus a prior-pull term keeping absent-referent examples near an uninformative prior
robustness_tests: Absent-referent detection and selective prediction (abstract)
limitations: CLIP heatmap grounding only; benchmark names not in abstract (our reading)

title: Adaptive Evidential Learning for Temporal-Semantic Robustness in Moment Retrieval
authors: Haojian Huang, Kaijing Ma, Jin Chen et al.
architecture: DEMR: Reflective Flipped Fusion block for cross-modal alignment + query-reconstruction task + deep evidential regression head (E_paradigm is our reading)
foundation_models: pre-trained video/text encoders (not named in abstract)
mechanism: Deep evidential regression over boundaries; Geom-regularizer to align uncertainty with difficult moments; debiasing against modality imbalance
objective: Moment-retrieval loss + evidential regression with Geom-regularizer + query reconstruction
robustness_tests: Debiased OOD splits Charades-CD and ActivityNet-CD (abstract)
limitations: Uncertainty quality reported qualitatively/through accuracy; no conformal guarantee (our reading)

title: Video Activity Localisation with Uncertainties in Temporal Boundary
authors: Jiabo Huang, Hailin Jin, Shaogang Gong et al.
architecture: Elastic Moment Bounding (EMB) with guided attention for frame-wise endpoint selection
mechanism: Elastic, adaptively constructed temporal boundaries tolerant to boundary-label uncertainty
objective: Training with elastic boundary targets instead of fixed annotated endpoints
robustness_tests: none reported beyond standard benchmarks (abstract)
limitations: Models annotation uncertainty during training; outputs a single interval without a confidence statement (our reading)

title: Thinking Inside Uncertainty: Interest Moment Perception for Diverse Temporal Grounding
authors: Hao Zhou, Chongyang Zhang, Yan Luo et al.
architecture: Diverse Temporal Grounding (DTG) framework with a diverse moment regression network (DMRNet) emitting multiple predictions in one pass
mechanism: Soft multi-labels from semantic similarity across video-query pairs reveal plausible alternative moments (label uncertainty)
objective: Joint optimisation over dynamically selected plausible interest moments with soft multi-label supervision
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Multiple hypotheses, but no calibrated probabilities (our reading)

title: LLM-Powered Query Expansion for Enhancing Boundary Prediction in Language-Driven Action Localization
authors: Zirui Shang, Xinxiao Wu, Shuo Yang
architecture: Model-agnostic plug-in for existing action-localization models (E_paradigm is our reading)
foundation_models: LLM for query expansion (not named in abstract)
mechanism: LLM-generated descriptions of start/end boundaries; probabilistic boundary targets from frame-query similarity and distance to annotated boundary
objective: Soft boundary-probability supervision tolerant to boundary uncertainty
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Addresses annotation (aleatoric) boundary uncertainty in training; no uncertainty output at test time (our reading)

title: Giving Commands to a Self-Driving Car: How to Deal with Uncertain Situations?
authors: Thierry Deruyttere, Victor Milewski, Marie-Francine Moens
architecture: Uncertainty-detection pipeline on top of a visual grounding model, plus a referring-expression generator for clarifying questions
mechanism: Detects uncertain situations and the objects causing them; optionally generates a question describing the uncertain objects
objective: Supervised uncertainty detection + REG training
robustness_tests: Ambiguous-command subset handling (abstract)
limitations: Binary uncertain/certain decision; no calibration analysis (our reading)

title: CroBIM-U: Uncertainty-Driven Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
authors: Yuzhe Sun, Zhe Dong, Haochen Jiang et al.
architecture: Plug-and-play Referring Uncertainty Scorer (RUS) + Uncertainty-Gated Fusion + Uncertainty-Driven Local Refinement on an RRSIS backbone
mechanism: Pixel-wise referring-uncertainty map (trained by online error-consistency supervision) gates language injection and focuses refinement
objective: Segmentation loss + online error-consistency supervision for the uncertainty map
robustness_tests: none reported beyond complex remote-sensing scenes (abstract)
limitations: Uncertainty map is used internally to guide fusion; it is not exposed or evaluated as calibrated confidence (our reading)

title: SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration
authors: Qingni Wang, Yue Fan, Xin Eric Wang
venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop (Agentic AI in the Wild); ICML 2026 Workshop (Trustworthy AI for Good)
architecture: Model-agnostic wrapper over GUI grounding MLLMs; cascade to a stronger model (Gemini) when uncertain
foundation_models: Gemini (cascade target); several GUI grounding models
mechanism: Uncertainty from spatial dispersion of stochastic click samples; calibrated test-time threshold with FDR control
objective: None for the grounder; threshold calibrated on held-out data
robustness_tests: Risk control across multiple GUI grounding models (abstract)
limitations: GUI screenshots only; guarantee is marginal (our reading)

title: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
authors: Shaojie Zhang, Pei Fu, Ruoceng Zhang et al.
E_paradigm: E8 agentic / tool-using / RL-trained reasoning grounder
architecture: HyperClick: MLLM policy outputting a click and an explicit confidence estimate
mechanism: Self-critiqued RL (SCRL) combining correctness reward and confidence-alignment reward
objective: GRPO-style RL with correctness + confidence-alignment rewards (our reading of 'self-critiqued RL')
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: GUI domain only (our reading)

title: Zoom Consistency: A Free Confidence Signal in Multi-Step Visual Grounding Pipelines
authors: Keon Kim, Krish Chelikavada
architecture: Two-step zoom-in pipeline with specialist/generalist routing
mechanism: Distance between step-2 prediction and crop centre as a geometric confidence signal
objective: None (training-free)
robustness_tests: Consistency across models, application categories and operating systems (abstract)
limitations: Weak signal (abstract: 'the correlation is small but consistent'); no calibration guarantee

title: Uncertainty-Aware Medical Diagnostic Phrase Identification and Grounding
authors: Ke Zou, Yang Bai, Bo Liu et al.
task: medical report grounding / medical phrase grounding
architecture: uMedGround: MLLM with a <BOX> token whose embedding is decoded to boxes by a vision encoder-decoder, plus an uncertainty-aware prediction model
mechanism: Special-token embedding decoded to grounding boxes; uncertainty-aware prediction of box reliability
objective: Supervised phrase identification + box regression with uncertainty modelling
robustness_tests: none reported in abstract
limitations: Medical domain; uncertainty formulation not detailed in abstract (our reading)

title: Robust Audio-Visual Segmentation via Audio-Guided Visual Convergent Alignment
authors: Chen Liu, Peike Li, Liying Yang et al.
architecture: Audio-guided modality alignment (AMA) module + uncertainty estimation (UE) module with separate mask and uncertainty heads (E_paradigm is our reading)
mechanism: Grouped audio-visual interaction and contrastive sounding/silent separation; UE flags spatio-temporal regions with frequent sound-state changes and lowers confidence there
objective: Segmentation loss + contrastive loss + uncertainty estimation
robustness_tests: Challenging scenes with ambiguous AV correspondences (abstract)
limitations: Uncertainty is used to down-weight predictions, not evaluated as calibrated confidence (our reading)

title: CLUE: Crossmodal disambiguation via Language-vision Understanding with attEntion
authors: Mouad Abrini, Mohamed Chetouani
architecture: LoRA-fine-tuned VLM decoder emitting grounding location tokens + lightweight CNN ambiguity detector on text-to-image attention maps
mechanism: Cross-modal attention maps converted to an explicit signal for deciding when to ask a clarification question
objective: Supervised IVG dialog training (InViG) + ambiguity-detector training on a mixed ambiguity set
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Decision to ask is binary; no calibration analysis (our reading)

title: Confidence Scores in Open-Vocabulary Detection Are a Biased Mixture of Scale and Semantics
authors: Yi Tang Soon, Jun-Wei Hsieh
architecture: Controlled analysis of three foundation-model-based OV detectors
mechanism: Regression of detector scores on object scale and query specificity; temperature-scaling correction
objective: n/a (analysis; parameter-free temperature scaling)
robustness_tests: Scale-bias replication on LVIS (abstract)
limitations: Studies score bias/ranking rather than full reliability diagrams (our reading)

title: Agreement versus Softmax under Spatial Disambiguation
authors: Michał Zakrzewski, Mariia Shpir, Taras Rumezhak et al.
architecture: GeoClassifier referencer with ground-truth proposals
mechanism: Object-level softmax confidence vs. cross-epoch agreement as confidence proxies; ECE on ScanRefer Unique vs. Multiple
objective: n/a (calibration analysis)
robustness_tests: Unique vs. Multiple (same-class distractor) split; scene bootstrap intervals (abstract)
limitations: Single referencer with ground-truth proposals; non-archival 7-page workshop note (our reading)

title: GRIT: General Robust Image Task Benchmark
authors: Tanmay Gupta, Ryan Marten, Aniruddha Kembhavi et al.
task: multi-task benchmark incl. referring expression grounding and object localization
G_conditions: degraded/noisy modality; domain/sensor shift; novel categories/compositions
architecture: n/a (benchmark)
mechanism: n/a
objective: n/a
robustness_tests: Image perturbations, image-source distribution shift, concept distribution shift (abstract)
limitations: Per-task calibration metric for REC not checked in this gap search

title: When Seeing Is Not Enough: Benchmarking Interactive Visual Grounding in LVLMs
authors: Zhengxiang Wang, Owen Rambow
architecture: n/a (evaluation framework over LVLMs)
mechanism: Controlled interaction protocols varying upfront vs. dialogue-acquired target information
objective: n/a
robustness_tests: Varied description sources, reasoning effort, repeated interactions, visual contexts (abstract)
limitations: Target selection output format not specified in abstract (D_output our reading)

title: Mechanisms of Object Localization in Vision-Language Models
authors: Timothy Schaumlöffel, Martina G. Vilas, Gemma Roig
architecture: Analysis of LLaVA-1.5 and InternVL-3.5 (MLLMs emitting boxes as text)
mechanism: Token ablation, attention knockout and causal mediation analysis at token, layer and head level, with the predicted box as outcome
objective: n/a (mechanistic analysis)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Two model families; object localisation prompts rather than full referring expressions (our reading)

title: Retrieval Heads Meet Vision: Uncovering How VLMs Locate and Extract Visual Information
authors: Chanho Park, Daehyeon Choi, Jihyun Lee et al.
task: REC (MLLM box prediction) and other visual-reference tasks
architecture: Analysis across eleven VLMs (not enumerated in abstract)
mechanism: Head scoring from output-token attention over the ground-truth referent region; causal head masking (top-20 Visual Retrieval Heads vs. random heads); cross-model transfer
objective: n/a (mechanistic analysis)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Benchmarks and models not named in abstract; preprint (our reading)

title: Grounding Isn't Knowing: Do VLMs Need Object Localization for Spatial Reasoning?
authors: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xinlin Zhuang et al.
task: object localization and spatial relation prediction in VLMs
architecture: Analysis of LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL
mechanism: Token ablation, layer-wise probing, attention knockout, causal mediation analysis for localisation and spatial-relation outputs
objective: n/a (mechanistic analysis)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Two model families; datasets not named in abstract (our reading)

title: From Drop-off to Recovery: A Mechanistic Analysis of Segmentation in MLLMs
authors: Boyong Wu, Sanghwan Kim, Zeynep Akata
task: segmentation capacity of MLLM visual tokens (probing)
architecture: Layer-wise linear probes across vision encoder, adapter and LLM of MLLMs
mechanism: Linear probing for segmentation + attention-knockout intervention + bidirectional image-token attention test
objective: n/a (mechanistic analysis)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Semantic segmentation probe readout, not language-conditioned referring segmentation; borderline for the grounding scope (our reading)

title: Emergent Visual Grounding in Large Multimodal Models Without Grounding Supervision
authors: Shengcao Cao, Liang-Yan Gui, Yu-Xiong Wang
task: pixel grounding / grounded conversation generation from LMM attention
architecture: Attend-and-segment readout from standard LMM attention maps; DIFFLMM with a diffusion-based visual encoder
foundation_models: standard LMMs with CLIP encoder; diffusion-based visual encoder (DIFFLMM)
mechanism: Attention maps between generated tokens and image tokens converted to pixel masks (correlational, no intervention)
objective: Standard LMM training without grounding supervision (DIFFLMM)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Attention-based (correlational) evidence; no causal test (our reading)

title: Angular Supervision for Visual Object Grounding in Autoregressive Vision-Language Models
authors: Parsa Esmaeilkhani, Longin Jan Latecki
task: RES via explanation heatmaps of autoregressive VLMs
architecture: Angular Relevance readout on visual-token embeddings vs. unembedding rows; optional Angular Object-Aware Loss fine-tuning
mechanism: Norm-invariant cosine similarity between visual token embeddings and vocabulary directions as an explanation/grounding map (correlational)
objective: Next-token prediction + auxiliary Angular Object-Aware Loss (optional)
robustness_tests: none reported
limitations: Explanation faithfulness argued via sharper maps and RES accuracy, not by intervention (our reading)

title: YouRefIt: Embodied Reference Understanding With Language and Gesture
authors: Yixin Chen, Qing Li, Deqian Kong, et al.
task: embodied reference understanding (image ERU, video ERU) + dataset
architecture: Baselines and a full model combining language embedding with gesture cues (pose/heatmap); inpainted-human variant removes gestural cues
mechanism: Language and gesture (pointing) cues fused to locate the referred object in the canonical frame
objective: Box regression on annotated canonical frames
robustness_tests: Information-source ablation: language-only, gesture-only, and language+gesture models; inpainted images with humans masked out to remove gestural cues
limitations: Indoor scenes; single referent per clip (our reading)
